title.zh: 卷二百零八 列傳第一百三十三 宦者下
title.raw: 卷二百零八 列傳第一百三十三 宦者下 Volume 208 Biographies 133: Imperial Officials 2

sentences.zh: ◎宦者下李輔國，本名靜忠，以閹奴為閑廄小兒。

translations.literal: Eunuchs, Part 2 — Li Fuguo. Li Fuguo's original name was Jingzhong; as a castrated bondsman he served as a petty attendant in the spare stables.
translations.idiomatic: Eunuchs, Part 2 — Li Fuguo. Li Fuguo, born Jingzhong, entered service as a young groom in the imperial spare stables in the capacity of a castrated bondsman.

sentences.zh: 貌佇陋，略通書計。

translations.literal: His appearance was clumsy and ugly; he had a slight knowledge of writing and reckoning.
translations.idiomatic: Homely and awkward in bearing, he knew a little of letters and accounts.

sentences.zh: 事高力士，年四十餘，使主廄中簿最。

translations.literal: He served Gao Lishi; when he was over forty, he was made to supervise the stable registers.
translations.idiomatic: Under Gao Lishi's patronage, he was assigned at forty-odd to keep the stable ledgers.

sentences.zh: 王鉷為使，以典禾豆，能檢擿耗欺，馬以故肥，薦之皇太子，得侍東宮。

translations.literal: When Wang Hong was commissioner, he put him in charge of grain and fodder; able to detect waste and fraud, the horses thereby grew fat; he was recommended to the Crown Prince and obtained service in the Eastern Palace.
translations.idiomatic: Under Commissioner Wang Hong he oversaw grain and fodder, exposing shrinkage and fraud so diligently that the horses grew notably fat; recommended to the crown prince, he gained a post in the Eastern Palace.

sentences.zh: 陳玄禮等誅楊國忠，輔國豫謀，又勸太子分中軍趨朔方，收河、隴兵，圖興復。

translations.literal: When Chen Xuanli and others killed Yang Guozhong, Fuguo took part in the planning beforehand, and again urged the Prince to split off the central army and hasten to Shuofang, gather the He and Long troops, and plan restoration.
translations.idiomatic: When Chen Xuanli and his fellows struck down Yang Guozhong, Fuguo had helped plan the move, and he urged the prince to detach the central army for Shuofang, rally the armies of He and Long, and work toward restoring the dynasty.

sentences.zh: 太子至靈武，愈親近，勸遂即位系天下心。

translations.literal: When the Prince reached Lingwu, he became still closer to him and urged him forthwith to ascend the throne to bind the hearts of the realm.
translations.idiomatic: Once the prince reached Lingwu, Fuguo grew still closer to him and pressed him to take the throne at once and rally the empire's allegiance.

sentences.zh: 擢家令，判元帥府行軍司馬。

translations.literal: He was promoted to Director of the Palace Household and given concurrent duties as acting chief of staff for the army on campaign at the Marshal's headquarters.
translations.idiomatic: He was raised to Director of the Palace Household and made acting chief of staff for the army on campaign at the marshal's headquarters.

sentences.zh: 肅宗稍稍任以肱膂事，更名護國，又改今名。

translations.literal: Emperor Suzong gradually entrusted him with matters of the sinews and backbone; his name was changed to Huguo, then again to his present name.
translations.idiomatic: Suzong gradually entrusted him with matters at the body's core of power; he was renamed Huguo, then given his present name.

sentences.zh: 凡四方章奏、軍符、禁寶一委之。

translations.literal: All memorials from the four quarters, military tallies, and imperial seals were entirely entrusted to him.
translations.idiomatic: All memorials from the provinces, military tallies, and imperial seals passed solely through his hands.

sentences.zh: 輔國能隨事齪齪謹密，取人主親信，而內深賊未敢肆。

translations.literal: Fuguo could in each matter act with petty meticulousness and secrecy, winning the sovereign's intimate trust, while inwardly deep with treachery yet not daring to run riot.
translations.idiomatic: Fuguo winnowed every affair with fussy secrecy and won the emperor's intimate trust, while inwardly nurturing deep malice he yet dared not show it openly.

sentences.zh: 不啖葷，時時為浮屠詭行，人以為柔良，不忌也。

translations.literal: He did not eat meat and from time to time performed Buddhist eccentricities; people thought him gentle and good and did not beware him.
translations.idiomatic: Abstaining from meat and affecting Buddhist devotions, he passed for gentle and harmless, and drew no suspicion.

sentences.zh: 帝還京師，拜殿中監，閑廄、五坊、宮苑、營田、栽接總監使，兼隴右群牧、京畿鑄錢、長春宮等使，少府、殿中二監，封成國公，實封戶五百。

translations.literal: When the Emperor returned to the capital, Fuguo was appointed Director of the Palace Department, General Superintendent of the spare stables, the Five Wards, palace parks, military farms, and grafting, and concurrently Commissioner of the Longyou stud farms, metropolitan coinage, Changchun Palace, and other posts; he held both the Court of the Imperial Treasury and the Palace Department directorships, was enfeoffed as Duke of Cheng, with five hundred households of actual fief income.
translations.idiomatic: When the emperor returned to the capital, Fuguo was made Director of the Palace Department and superintendent of the spare stables, the Five Wards, palace parks, military farms, and grafting operations, while also holding the Longyou stud farms, metropolitan coinage, Changchun Palace, and other commissions; he directed both the Imperial Treasury and the Palace Department, was enfeoffed as Duke of Cheng with five hundred taxable households, and drew income from the fief.

sentences.zh: 宰相群臣欲不時見天子，皆因輔國以請，乃得可。

translations.literal: If the chief ministers and officials wished to see the Son of Heaven at an irregular time, they all had to request it through Fuguo before permission was granted.
translations.idiomatic: Chief ministers and officials who wished an audience outside the usual schedule had to petition through Fuguo before the emperor would consent.

sentences.zh: 常止銀臺門決事。

translations.literal: He regularly halted at the Yintai Gate to decide affairs.
translations.idiomatic: He routinely conducted business at the Yintai Gate.

sentences.zh: 置察事聽兒數十人，吏雖有秋豪過，無不得，得輒推訊。

translations.literal: He set up several dozen informant listeners; though an official's fault were as slight as an autumn hair, none escaped detection, and once caught they were immediately interrogated.
translations.idiomatic: He stationed several dozen spies; no official's fault, however slight, escaped them, and anyone caught was at once interrogated.

sentences.zh: 州縣獄訟，三司制劾，有所捕逮流降，皆私判臆處，因稱制敕，然未始聞上也。

translations.literal: In prefectural and county lawsuits and in cases prosecuted by the Three Offices, whenever anyone was seized, banished, or demoted, he privately judged and disposed at will, citing imperial edicts, yet the sovereign was never informed.
translations.idiomatic: In local suits and prosecutions by the Three Offices, every arrest, exile, or demotion was decided by his private judgment in the name of imperial edict, without the throne ever being told.

sentences.zh: 詔書下，輔國署已乃施行，群臣無敢議。

translations.literal: When edicts were issued, Fuguo would sign them and only then were they put into effect; the ministers dared not discuss it.
translations.idiomatic: Edicts took effect only after Fuguo had countersigned them, and no minister dared object.

sentences.zh: 出則介士三百人為衛。

translations.literal: When he went out, three hundred armored soldiers served as his guard.
translations.idiomatic: Whenever he went abroad, three hundred armored guards attended him.

sentences.zh: 貴幸至不敢斥官，呼五郎。

translations.literal: The honored and favored did not even dare call him by his office title, but addressed him as Fifth Master.
translations.idiomatic: Even the most favored courtiers dared not use his title, calling him simply Fifth Master.

sentences.zh: 李揆當國，以子姓事之，號「五父」。

translations.literal: When Li Kui held the government, he served him as a junior kinsman would and called him the Fifth Father.
translations.idiomatic: Li Kui, who then directed the government, treated him with the deference of a junior kinsman and styled him the Fifth Father.

sentences.zh: 帝為娶元擢女為妻，擢以故為梁州長史，弟兄皆位臺省。

translations.literal: The Emperor had him marry Yuan Zhuo's daughter as his wife; Yuan Zhuo for this reason became prefectural secretary of Liangzhou, and his brothers all held posts in the central ministries.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor arranged his marriage to Yuan Zhuo's daughter; Yuan Zhuo was made chief secretary of Liang prefecture on that account, and his brothers all received posts in the central ministries.

sentences.zh: 李峴輔政，叩頭言：「且亂國。」

translations.literal: When Li Xian assisted in government, he kowtowed and said, "He will soon throw the state into disorder.
translations.idiomatic: Li Xian, then assisting in government, kowtowed and said, "He will soon throw the state into disorder.

sentences.zh: 於是詔敕不由中書出者，峴必審覆，輔國不悅。

translations.literal: Thereupon any edict or order not issued through the Secretariat, Xian would invariably review; Fuguo was displeased.
translations.idiomatic: Henceforth Xian insisted on reviewing every edict not routed through the Secretariat, to Fuguo's displeasure.

sentences.zh: 時太上皇居興慶宮，帝自復道來起居，太上皇亦間至大明宮，或相逢道中。

translations.literal: At that time the Retired Emperor dwelt in Xingqing Palace; the Emperor came by the covered way to inquire after his health, and the Retired Emperor also occasionally went to Daming Palace, sometimes meeting on the road.
translations.idiomatic: The retired emperor then lived in Xingqing Palace; the emperor visited by the covered passage to pay his respects, while the retired emperor sometimes came to Daming Palace, and they occasionally met on the road.

sentences.zh: 帝命陳玄禮、高力士、王承恩、魏悅、玉真公主常在太上皇左右，梨園弟子日奏聲伎為娛樂。

translations.literal: The Emperor ordered Chen Xuanli, Gao Lishi, Wang Chengen, Wei Yue, and Princess Yuzhen to remain constantly at the Retired Emperor's side; Pear Garden performers daily presented music and entertainers for his amusement.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor kept Chen Xuanli, Gao Lishi, Wang Chengen, Wei Yue, and Princess Yuzhen constantly at the retired emperor's side, while Pear Garden performers daily supplied music and entertainers.

sentences.zh: 輔國素微賤，雖暴貴，力士等猶不為禮，怨之，欲立奇功自固。

translations.literal: Fuguo had always been base and low; though he rose suddenly to wealth and rank, Lishi and the others still did not show him courtesy; he resented them and wished to perform a striking exploit to secure himself.
translations.idiomatic: Fuguo had risen from the lowest ranks; though suddenly exalted, men like Lishi still withheld courtesy from him. He resented them and sought some bold stroke to secure his position.

sentences.zh: 初，太上皇每置酒長慶樓，南俯大道，因裴回觀覽，或父老過之，皆拜舞乃去。

translations.literal: At first the Retired Emperor would set out wine at Changqing Tower, looking south down upon the great road; as he strolled and gazed, when old men of the district passed by, they would all bow and dance before departing.
translations.idiomatic: At first the retired emperor often held wine at Changqing Tower, gazing south over the main road; when local elders passed below, they would bow and dance before going on.

sentences.zh: 上元中，劍南奏事吏過樓下，因上謁，太上皇賜之酒，詔公主及如仙媛主之，又召郭英乂、王銑等飲，賚予頗厚。

translations.literal: In the Shangyuan era, a Jiannan memorial envoy passed below the tower and came up to pay his respects; the Retired Emperor bestowed wine on him and ordered the Princess and Lady Rushanyuan to preside; he also summoned Guo Yingyi, Wang Xian, and others to drink, with generous gifts.
translations.idiomatic: During the Shangyuan years a Jiannan memorial envoy passed below the tower and was summoned up; the retired emperor gave him wine with the princess and Lady Rushanyuan presiding, then called Guo Yingyi, Wang Xian, and others to join the feast and rewarded them lavishly.

sentences.zh: 輔國因妄言於帝曰：「太上皇居近市，交通外人，玄禮、力士等將不利陛下，六軍功臣反側不自安，願徙太上皇入禁中。」

translations.literal: Fuguo therefore spoke falsely to the Emperor, saying, "The Retired Emperor dwells near the market and associates with outsiders; Xuanli, Lishi, and the rest intend harm to Your Majesty; the meritorious officers of the Six Armies are restless and ill at ease — I beg that the Retired Emperor be moved into the inner palace."
translations.idiomatic: Fuguo then lied to the emperor: "The retired emperor lives near the market and consorts with outsiders; Xuanli, Lishi, and the rest mean you harm; the meritorious officers of the Six Armies are uneasy. Move him into the inner palace."

sentences.zh: 帝不寤。

translations.literal: The Emperor did not perceive the truth.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor did not see through him.

sentences.zh: 先時，興慶宮有馬三百，輔國矯詔取之，裁留十馬。

translations.literal: Earlier, Xingqing Palace had three hundred horses; Fuguo forged an edict and took them, leaving only ten.
translations.idiomatic: Earlier Xingqing Palace had held three hundred horses; Fuguo forged an edict and seized them, leaving only ten.

sentences.zh: 太上皇謂力士曰：「吾兒用輔國謀，不得終孝矣。」

translations.literal: The Retired Emperor said to Lishi, "My son, following Fuguo's schemes, will not be able to fulfill filial piety to the end."
translations.idiomatic: The retired emperor told Lishi, "My son, heeding Fuguo's plots, will not see his filial duty through to the end."

sentences.zh: 會帝屬疾，輔國即詐言皇帝請太上皇按行宮中，至睿武門，射生官五百遮道，太上皇驚，幾墜馬，問何為者，輔國以甲騎數十馳奏曰：「陛下以興慶宮湫陋，奉迎乘輿還宮中。」

translations.literal: When the Emperor fell ill, Fuguo at once falsely reported that the Emperor invited the Retired Emperor to tour the palace; when they reached Ruiwu Gate, five hundred archer-guards blocked the road; the Retired Emperor was startled and nearly fell from his horse; he asked what this meant; Fuguo galloped up with several dozen armored horsemen and reported, "Your Majesty, finding Xingqing Palace cramped and mean, welcomes the imperial carriage back to the inner palace."
translations.idiomatic: When the emperor fell ill, Fuguo falsely announced that the emperor wished the retired emperor to tour the palace. At Ruiwu Gate five hundred archer-guards barred the way; the retired emperor started and nearly fell from his horse. Fuguo galloped up with dozens of armored riders and reported, "Your Majesty finds Xingqing Palace cramped and is escorting you back to the inner palace."

sentences.zh: 力士厲聲曰：「五十年太平天子，輔國欲何事？」

translations.literal: Lishi cried out in a harsh voice, "Fifty years a Son of Heaven in peace — what does Fuguo intend?"
translations.idiomatic: Lishi thundered, "Fifty years a peaceful emperor — what does Fuguo mean by this?"

sentences.zh: 叱使下馬，輔國失轡，罵力士曰：「翁不解事！」

translations.literal: He shouted for them to dismount; Fuguo dropped his reins and cursed Lishi, saying, "Old man, you don't understand affairs!"
translations.idiomatic: He ordered them down from their horses; Fuguo dropped his reins and cursed Lishi: "Old fool, you don't understand!"

sentences.zh: 斬一從者。

translations.literal: He beheaded one attendant.
translations.idiomatic: He beheaded one attendant on the spot.

sentences.zh: 力士呼曰：「太上皇問將士各好在否！」

translations.literal: Lishi called out, "The Retired Emperor asks whether the officers and soldiers are all well!"
translations.idiomatic: Lishi shouted, "The retired emperor asks whether you officers and soldiers are all well!"

sentences.zh: 將士納刀嘑萬歲，皆再拜。

translations.literal: The officers and soldiers sheathed their blades, shouted "Long live the Emperor!" and all bowed twice.
translations.idiomatic: The men sheathed their blades, shouted "Long live the emperor!" and all bowed twice.

sentences.zh: 力士復曰：「輔國可御太上皇馬！」

translations.literal: Lishi said again, "Fuguo may hold the Retired Emperor's reins!"
translations.idiomatic: Lishi added, "Fuguo, take the retired emperor's reins!"

sentences.zh: 輔國靴而走，與力士對執轡還西內，居甘露殿，侍衛才數十，皆尫老。

translations.literal: Fuguo ran in his boots; he and Lishi faced each other holding the reins and returned to the western inner palace, dwelling in Ganlu Hall, with only several dozen guards, all frail and old.
translations.idiomatic: Fuguo ran alongside in his boots while he and Lishi together led the horse back to the western inner palace. The retired emperor was lodged in Ganlu Hall with only a few dozen guards, all frail and elderly.

sentences.zh: 太上皇執力士手曰：「微將軍，朕且為兵死鬼。」

translations.literal: The Retired Emperor took Lishi's hand and said, "But for the general, I would already be a ghost slain by soldiers."
translations.idiomatic: The retired emperor seized Lishi's hand and said, "But for you, general, I would already be a ghost killed by soldiers."

sentences.zh: 左右皆流涕。

translations.literal: Those at his side all wept.
translations.idiomatic: Those around him wept.

sentences.zh: 又曰：「興慶，吾王地，數以讓皇帝，帝不受。

translations.literal: He also said, "Xingqing was my princely domain; I repeatedly offered it to the Emperor, but he would not accept it.
translations.idiomatic: He added, "Xingqing was my princely estate; I offered it to the emperor again and again, but he would not take it.

sentences.zh: 今之徙，自吾志也。」

translations.literal: This move now is of my own will."
translations.idiomatic: This move is of my own choosing."

sentences.zh: 俄而流承恩播州，魏悅溱州，如仙媛歸州，公主居玉真觀；

translations.literal: Before long Wang Chengen was banished to Bozhou, Wei Yue to Qinzhou, Lady Rushanyuan to Guizhou, and the Princess lodged at Yuzhen Abbey;
translations.idiomatic: Soon Wang Chengen was exiled to Bozhou, Wei Yue to Qinzhou, Lady Rushanyuan to Guizhou, and the princess was sent to Yuzhen Abbey;

sentences.zh: 更料後宮聲樂百餘，更侍太上皇，備灑掃；

translations.literal: more than a hundred musicians and entertainers from the rear palace were reassigned to attend the Retired Emperor and perform sweeping and cleaning;
translations.idiomatic: more than a hundred musicians and attendants from the rear palace were reassigned to serve him and keep his quarters;

sentences.zh: 詔萬安、咸宜二公主視服膳。

translations.literal: an edict ordered Princesses Wan'an and Xianyi to oversee his meals.
translations.idiomatic: and Princesses Wan'an and Xianyi were ordered to oversee his meals.

sentences.zh: 自是太上皇怏怏不豫，至棄天下。

translations.literal: From this the Retired Emperor was resentful and ill at ease until he departed the world.
translations.idiomatic: From then on the retired emperor languished in discontent until he left the world.

sentences.zh: 輔國以功遷兵部尚書。

translations.literal: For his merit Fuguo was transferred to Minister of War.
translations.idiomatic: For this exploit Fuguo was promoted to Minister of War.

sentences.zh: 南省視事，使武士戎裝夾道，陳跳丸舞劍，百騎前驅，御府設食，太常備樂，宰相群臣畢會。

translations.literal: When he took office at the southern ministries, he had warriors in armor line both sides of the road, displaying ball-juggling and sword dances; a hundred horsemen rode ahead; the imperial pantry set out food and the Court of Imperial Sacrifices prepared music; chief ministers and officials all attended.
translations.idiomatic: At his investiture in the southern ministries, armored warriors lined the road while performers juggled balls and danced with swords; a hundred horsemen rode ahead, the imperial pantry supplied a feast, the Court of Sacrifices provided music, and the whole court attended.

sentences.zh: 既得志，乃厭然驕觖，求宰相，帝重違曰：「卿勛力何任不可，但群望未一，如何？」

translations.literal: Once his aims were achieved, he became insolently arrogant and overbearing and sought the chancellorship; the Emperor, loath to refuse outright, said, "With your merit, what office could you not hold? Yet the court is not of one mind — what then?"
translations.idiomatic: Once he had his way, he grew brazen and overbearing and demanded the chancellorship. The emperor, reluctant to refuse outright, said, "Your merit entitles you to any post — but the court is not united. What then?"

sentences.zh: 輔國遂諷宰相裴冕使聯表薦己。

translations.literal: Fuguo then prompted the chief minister Pei Mian to submit a joint memorial recommending himself.
translations.idiomatic: Fuguo then induced Chief Minister Pei Mian to submit a joint memorial recommending him.

sentences.zh: 帝密擿蕭華使喻止冕。

translations.literal: The Emperor secretly sent Xiao Hua to instruct Mian to stop.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor secretly dispatched Xiao Hua to tell Mian to desist.

sentences.zh: 張皇后數疾其顓，帝寢疾，太子監國，后召太子，將誅輔國及程元振，太子不從，更召越王、兗王圖之。

translations.literal: Empress Zhang often resented his monopoly of power; when the Emperor fell gravely ill and the Crown Prince supervised the state, the Empress summoned the Prince intending to execute Fuguo and Cheng Yuanzhen; the Prince would not agree and she instead summoned the Princes of Yue and Yan to plot it.
translations.idiomatic: Empress Zhang often resented his monopoly of power. When the emperor fell gravely ill and the crown prince took charge of state affairs, the empress summoned the prince to kill Fuguo and Cheng Yuanzhen; he refused, so she called in the princes of Yue and Yan to plot it instead.

sentences.zh: 元振告輔國，即伏兵淩霄門，迎太子，伺變，是夜捕二王及中人朱輝光、馬英俊等囚之，而殺后它殿。

translations.literal: Yuanzhen informed Fuguo; they at once set ambush at Lingxiao Gate, welcomed the Crown Prince, and watched for developments; that night they seized the two princes and the eunuchs Zhu Huiguang, Ma Yingjun, and others and imprisoned them, then killed the Empress in another hall.
translations.idiomatic: Yuanzhen warned Fuguo; they laid ambush at Lingxiao Gate, welcomed the crown prince, and waited. That night they seized the two princes and the eunuchs Zhu Huiguang and Ma Yingjun, imprisoned them, and killed the empress in another hall.

sentences.zh: 代宗立，輔國等以定策功，愈跋扈，至謂帝曰：「大家弟坐宮中，外事聽老奴處決。」

translations.literal: When Emperor Daizong ascended the throne, Fuguo and the others, for their merit in settling the succession, grew still more overbearing, even saying to the Emperor, "Young master, you sit in the palace; let this old slave decide outside affairs."
translations.idiomatic: When Daizong took the throne, Fuguo and his allies, credited with fixing the succession, grew still more overbearing, even telling the emperor, "Young master, you sit in the palace; leave outside affairs to this old slave."

sentences.zh: 帝矍然欲翦除，而憚其握兵，因尊為尚父，事無大小率關白，群臣出入皆先詣輔國，輔國頗自安。

translations.literal: The Emperor started and wished to cut him down, but feared his grip on the army; he therefore honored him as Imperial Father, and matters great and small all passed through his report; officials entering and leaving all first called on Fuguo, and Fuguo grew somewhat reassured.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor started and wished to destroy him but feared his hold on the army; he therefore honored him as Imperial Father. Every affair, great or small, passed through Fuguo's report, and officials called on him first when entering or leaving court — which somewhat reassured him.

sentences.zh: 又冊進司空兼中書令，實封戶八百。

translations.literal: He was further enfeoffed and promoted to Grand Preceptor with concurrent appointment as Chief Minister of the Secretariat, with eight hundred households of actual fief income.
translations.idiomatic: He was further promoted to Grand Preceptor and Chief Minister of the Secretariat, with eight hundred taxable households in his fief.

sentences.zh: 未幾，以左武衛大將軍彭體盈代為閑廄、嫩牧、苑內、營田、五坊等使，以右武衛大將軍藥子昂代判元帥行軍司馬，賜輔國大第於外。

translations.literal: Before long the Left Martial Guard General Peng Tiying replaced him as commissioner of the spare stables, tender pastures, inner parks, military farms, and Five Wards; the Right Martial Guard General Yao Zi'ang replaced him as acting chief of staff for the army on campaign; and Fuguo was granted a great mansion outside the palace.
translations.idiomatic: Soon the Left Martial Guard general Peng Tiying took over the spare stables, tender pastures, inner parks, military farms, and Five Wards; the Right Martial Guard general Yao Zi'ang replaced him as acting chief of staff; and Fuguo was given a great mansion outside the palace.

sentences.zh: 中外聞其失勢，舉相賀。

translations.literal: Inside and outside the court, hearing he had lost power, all congratulated one another.
translations.idiomatic: Inside and outside the court, hearing he had lost power, everyone congratulated one another.

sentences.zh: 輔國始惘然憂，不知所出，表乞解官。

translations.literal: Fuguo at first grew dazed with worry, not knowing what course to take, and memorialized begging to resign his office.
translations.idiomatic: Fuguo at first grew dazed with worry and, not knowing what to do, memorialized asking to resign.

sentences.zh: 有詔進封博陸郡王，仍為司空、尚父，許朝朔望。

translations.literal: An edict advanced him to Prince of Bolu, while he remained Grand Preceptor and Imperial Father, permitted to attend court on the first and fifteenth of the month.
translations.idiomatic: An edict advanced him to Prince of Bolu while he remained Grand Preceptor and Imperial Father, permitted to attend court on the first and fifteenth of each month.

sentences.zh: 輔國欲入中書作謝表，閽者不內，曰：「尚父罷宰相，不可入。」

translations.literal: Fuguo wished to enter the Secretariat to draft a letter of thanks; the gatekeepers would not admit him, saying, "The Imperial Father has been removed from the chancellorship and may not enter."
translations.idiomatic: Fuguo wished to enter the Secretariat to draft a letter of thanks, but the gatekeepers refused him, saying, "The Imperial Father has been removed from the chancellorship and may not enter."

sentences.zh: 輔國氣塞，久乃曰：「老奴死罪，事郎君不了，請地下事先帝矣！」

translations.literal: Fuguo was choked with rage; after a long while he said, "This old slave deserves death — I have failed to serve my young master; let me go below and wait on the late Emperor!"
translations.idiomatic: Choking with rage, Fuguo at last said, "This old slave deserves death — I have failed you, young master; let me go below and wait on the late emperor!"

sentences.zh: 帝優辭諭遣。

translations.literal: The Emperor spoke gently to console him and sent him away.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor spoke gently to console him and sent him away.

sentences.zh: 有韓穎、劉烜善步星，乾元中待詔翰林，穎位司天監，烜起居舍人，與輔國匿甚。

translations.literal: There were Han Ying and Liu Xuan, skilled in pacing the stars; in the Qianyuan era they awaited edicts at the Hanlin Academy — Ying held the post of Director of the Astronomy Bureau and Xuan was Recorder of the Left; they were very close with Fuguo in secret.
translations.idiomatic: Han Ying and Liu Xuan were skilled astrologers; in the Qianyuan era they awaited edicts at the Hanlin Academy — Ying as Director of the Astronomy Bureau and Xuan as Recorder of the Left — and were secretly very close to Fuguo.

sentences.zh: 輔國領中書，穎進秘書監，烜中書舍人，裴冕引為山陵使判官，輔國罷，俱流嶺南，賜死。

translations.literal: When Fuguo headed the Secretariat, Ying was advanced to Director of the Palace Library and Xuan to Secretariat Drafter; Pei Mian brought them in as aides to the imperial tomb commissioner; when Fuguo fell, all were banished to Lingnan and ordered to die.
translations.idiomatic: When Fuguo headed the Secretariat, Ying was made Director of the Palace Library and Xuan Secretariat drafter; Pei Mian brought them in as aides to the imperial tomb commissioner. When Fuguo fell, all were exiled to Lingnan and ordered to die.

sentences.zh: 自輔國徙太上皇，天下疾之，帝在東宮積不平。

translations.literal: From the time Fuguo moved the Retired Emperor, the realm hated him; the Emperor, while still in the Eastern Palace, had long nursed resentment.
translations.idiomatic: From the time Fuguo moved the retired emperor, the realm hated him; the emperor, while still crown prince in the Eastern Palace, had long nursed resentment.

sentences.zh: 既嗣位，不欲顯戮，遣俠者夜刺殺之，年五十九，抵其首混中，殊右臂，告泰陵。

translations.literal: Once he succeeded to the throne, unwilling to execute him openly, he sent bravos by night to stab and kill him; he was fifty-nine; his head was placed in a mixed vessel and his right arm severed separately, and this was reported at Tailing.
translations.idiomatic: Once on the throne, unwilling to execute him openly, he sent bravos to stab him to death by night. Fuguo was fifty-nine. His head was placed in one vessel and his right arm severed and set apart; the deed was reported at Tailing.

sentences.zh: 然猶秘其事，刻木代首以葬，贈太傅，謚曰鬼。

translations.literal: Yet the matter was still kept secret; a wooden head was carved to substitute in burial; he was posthumously enfeoffed as Grand Tutor with the posthumous title Gui.
translations.idiomatic: Yet the matter was kept secret; a wooden head was carved for burial; he was posthumously enfeoffed as Grand Tutor with the posthumous title Gui.

sentences.zh: 後梓州刺史杜濟以武人為牙門將，自言刺輔國者。

translations.literal: Later Du Ji, prefect of Zizhou, had a military man as gate commander who claimed of himself that he was the one who had stabbed Fuguo.
translations.idiomatic: Later Du Ji of Zizhou had a military gate commander who claimed to be Fuguo's assassin.

sentences.zh: 王守澄者，史亡所來。

translations.literal: Wang Shoucheng: the histories do not record his origins.
translations.idiomatic: Wang Shoucheng — the histories do not record his origins.

sentences.zh: 元和中監徐州軍，召還。

translations.literal: In the Yuanhe era he supervised the Xuzhou army and was summoned back.
translations.idiomatic: In the Yuanhe era he supervised the Xuzhou army and was recalled to court.

sentences.zh: 方憲宗喜方士說，詔天下求其人，宰相皇甫镈、左金吾將軍李道古等白見楊仁晝、浮屠大通。

translations.literal: Just then Emperor Xianzong delighted in the talk of alchemists and ordered a search throughout the realm for such men; the chief minister Huangfu Bo, the Left Golden Guard General Li Daogu, and others presented Yang Renzhou and the Buddhist Datong.
translations.idiomatic: Just then Xianzong delighted in alchemists' talk and ordered a search throughout the realm; Chief Minister Huangfu Bo, Left Golden Guard General Li Daogu, and others presented Yang Renzhou and the Buddhist Datong.

sentences.zh: 仁晝更姓名曰柳泌，大通自言壽百五十歲，有不死藥，並待詔翰林。

translations.literal: Renzhou changed his name to Liu Bi; Datong claimed himself to be one hundred fifty years old and to possess an elixir of immortality; both awaited edicts at the Hanlin Academy.
translations.idiomatic: Renzhou changed his name to Liu Bi; Datong claimed to be one hundred fifty years old and to possess an elixir of immortality; both awaited edicts at the Hanlin Academy.

sentences.zh: 虢人田元佐言有秘方，能化瓦礫為黃金，詔除虢令，與董景珍、李元戢皆介泌、大通薦於天子，天子惑其說。

translations.literal: Tian Yuanzuo of Guo said he had a secret formula able to turn rubble into gold; an edict appointed him magistrate of Guo; he, Dong Jingzhen, and Li Yuanji were all introduced to the Son of Heaven through Bi and Datong, and the Son of Heaven was beguiled by their doctrines.
translations.idiomatic: Tian Yuanzuo of Guo claimed a secret formula to turn rubble into gold and was appointed magistrate of Guo; he, Dong Jingzhen, and Li Yuanji were all introduced to the emperor through Bi and Datong, and the emperor was taken in by their claims.

sentences.zh: 泌以金石進帝餌之，躁甚，數暴怒，恚責左右，踵得罪，禁中累息，帝自是不豫。

translations.literal: Bi presented the Emperor with mineral drugs as food; he grew very restless, often flew into rage, angrily blamed those around him, and one after another they were punished; the inner palace was filled with sighs, and from this the Emperor was unwell.
translations.idiomatic: Bi fed the emperor mineral drugs; he grew restless, flew into repeated rages, and blamed those around him until one after another they were punished. The inner palace was filled with sighs, and from then on the emperor was unwell.

sentences.zh: 十五年，罷元會，群臣危恐，會義成劉悟來朝，賜對麟德殿，悟出曰：「上體平矣。」

translations.literal: In the fifteenth year the New Year's audience was canceled; the ministers were fearful; when Liu Wu of Yicheng came to court and was granted audience in Linde Hall, Wu on leaving said, "His Majesty's condition is stable."
translations.idiomatic: In the fifteenth year the New Year's audience was canceled and the ministers were fearful. When Liu Wu of Yicheng came to court and was granted audience in Linde Hall, he said on leaving, "His Majesty's condition is stable."

sentences.zh: 內外乃安。

translations.literal: Inside and outside the court were then reassured.
translations.idiomatic: Court and capital were then reassured.

sentences.zh: 是夜，守澄與內常侍陳弘志弒帝於中和殿，緣所餌，以暴崩告天下，乃與梁守謙、韋元素等定冊立穆宗。

translations.literal: That night Shoucheng and the Inner Regular Attendant Chen Hongzhi assassinated the Emperor in Zhonghe Hall; citing the drugs he had taken, they announced to the realm that he had died suddenly, then with Liang Shouqian, Wei Yuansu, and others settled the succession and enthroned Muzong.
translations.idiomatic: That night Shoucheng and Inner Regular Attendant Chen Hongzhi assassinated the emperor in Zhonghe Hall; citing the drugs he had taken, they announced sudden death to the realm, then with Liang Shouqian, Wei Yuansu, and others fixed the succession and enthroned Muzong.

sentences.zh: 俄知樞密事。

translations.literal: Before long he came to know affairs of the Privy Secretariat.
translations.idiomatic: Before long he took charge of privy affairs.

sentences.zh: 文宗嗣位，守澄有助力，進拜驃騎大將軍。

translations.literal: When Emperor Wenzong succeeded to the throne, Shoucheng had aided his accession and was advanced to General of Agile Cavalry.
translations.idiomatic: When Wenzong succeeded to the throne, Shoucheng had aided his accession and was promoted to General of Agile Cavalry.

sentences.zh: 帝疾元和逆罪久不討，故以宋申錫為宰相，謀因事除之，不克，更因其黨鄭註、李訓乘其罅，於是流楊承和於州，韋元素象州。

translations.literal: The Emperor resented that the Yuanhe regicides had long gone unpunished; he therefore made Song Shenxi chief minister to plot their removal when occasion offered, but failed; he then relied on their factionaries Zheng Zhu and Li Xun to exploit their gaps; Yang Chengho was banished to a prefecture and Wei Yuansu to Xiangzhou.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor resented that the Yuanhe regicides had long gone unpunished; he made Song Shenxi chief minister to plot their removal but failed, then used their factionaries Zheng Zhu and Li Xun to exploit their weaknesses. Yang Chengho was exiled to a prefecture and Wei Yuansu to Xiangzhou.

sentences.zh: 遣中人劉忠諒追殺元素於武昌，承和次公安賜死。

translations.literal: He sent the eunuch Liu Zhongliang to pursue and kill Yuansu at Wuchang; Chengho was ordered to die when he reached Gong'an.
translations.idiomatic: He sent the eunuch Liu Zhongliang to pursue and kill Yuansu at Wuchang; Chengho was ordered to die when he reached Gong'an.

sentences.zh: 訓乃脅守澄以軍容使就第，使內養賫鴆賜死，事秘，時無知者，贈揚州大都督。

translations.literal: Xun then coerced Shoucheng, summoning him as Army Commissioner to his residence and sending inner attendants bearing poisoned wine to grant death; the affair was secret and none knew at the time; he was posthumously enfeoffed as Grand Governor of Yangzhou.
translations.idiomatic: Xun then summoned Shoucheng to his residence as army commissioner and sent inner attendants with poisoned wine to grant death. The affair was secret and none knew at the time; he was posthumously enfeoffed as Grand Governor of Yangzhou.

sentences.zh: 其弟守涓自徐州監軍召還，死於中牟。

translations.literal: His younger brother Shoujuan was recalled from supervising the Xuzhou army and died at Zhongmou.
translations.idiomatic: His younger brother Shoujuan was recalled from supervising the Xuzhou army and died at Zhongmou.

sentences.zh: 劉克明，亦亡所來，得幸敬宗。

translations.literal: Liu Keming likewise has no recorded origins; he won favor under Emperor Jingzong.
translations.idiomatic: Liu Keming — likewise of unknown origins — won favor under Jingzong.

sentences.zh: 敬宗善擊球，於是陶元皓、靳遂良、趙士則、李公定、石定寬以球工得見便殿，內籍宣徽院或教坊，然皆出神策隸卒或里閭惡少年，帝與狎息殿中為戲樂。

translations.literal: Jingzong was skilled at cuju; thus Tao Yuanhao, Jin Suiliang, Zhao Shize, Li Gongding, and Shi Dingkuan, as ball-players, gained audience in the side hall; they were enrolled in the Xuanhui Court or the Music School, yet all came from Shence Army bondsmen or vicious youths of the lanes; the Emperor sported and rested with them in the hall for amusement.
translations.idiomatic: Jingzong loved cuju; Tao Yuanhao, Jin Suiliang, Zhao Shize, Li Gongding, and Shi Dingkuan, as ball-players, gained audience in the side hall and were enrolled in the Xuanhui Court or Music School, though all were Shence bondsmen or vicious street youths. The emperor sported with them in the hall for amusement.

sentences.zh: 四方聞之，爭以趫勇進於帝。

translations.literal: When the four quarters heard of this, they vied to present the bold and agile to the Emperor.
translations.idiomatic: When word spread, men from every quarter vied to present the bold and agile to the emperor.

sentences.zh: 嘗閱角觝三殿，有碎首斷臂，流血廷中，帝歡甚，厚賜之，夜分罷。

translations.literal: Once he reviewed wrestling in the Three Halls; heads were smashed and arms severed, blood flowing in the courtyard; the Emperor was greatly pleased, richly rewarded them, and dismissed only at midnight.
translations.idiomatic: Once he watched wrestling in the Three Halls; heads were smashed and arms severed and blood flowed in the courtyard. The emperor was delighted, rewarded them lavishly, and dismissed the show only at midnight.

sentences.zh: 所親近既皆凶不逞，又小過必責辱，自是怨望。

translations.literal: Those he favored were all violent and unbridled; moreover he punished and humiliated them for the slightest fault — from this they nursed resentment.
translations.idiomatic: Those he favored were violent and unbridled, yet he punished and humiliated them for the slightest fault — from which they nursed resentment.

sentences.zh: 帝夜艾自捕狐貍為樂，謂之「打夜狐」，中人許遂振、李少端、魚志弘侍從不及，皆削秩。

translations.literal: The Emperor at night went out himself to hunt foxes for sport, calling it "beating the night fox"; the eunuchs Xu Suizhen, Li Shaoduan, and Yu Zhihong could not keep up in attendance and all had their ranks reduced.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor at night went out himself to hunt foxes for sport, calling it "beating the night fox"; the eunuchs Xu Suizhen, Li Shaoduan, and Yu Zhihong could not keep up and all had their ranks reduced.

sentences.zh: 帝獵夜還，與克明、田務澄、許文端、石定寬、蘇佐明、王嘉憲、閻惟直等二十有八人群飲，既酣，帝更衣，燭忽滅，克明與佐明、定寬弒帝更衣室，矯詔召翰林學士路隋作詔書，命絳王領軍國事。

translations.literal: The Emperor returned from a night hunt and drank in a group of twenty-eight with Keming, Tian Wucheng, Xu Wenduan, Shi Dingkuan, Su Zuoming, Wang Jiaxian, Yan Weizhi, and others; when they were drunk the Emperor went to change clothes; the candles suddenly went out; Keming with Zuoming and Dingkuan assassinated the Emperor in the changing room; they forged an edict summoning Hanlin Academician Lu Sui to draft an imperial order appointing the Prince of Jiang to direct state affairs.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor returned from a night hunt and drank with twenty-eight men including Keming, Tian Wucheng, Xu Wenduan, Shi Dingkuan, Su Zuoming, Wang Jiaxian, and Yan Weizhi. When they were drunk the emperor went to change clothes; the candles went out; Keming with Zuoming and Dingkuan killed him in the changing room, forged an edict summoning Hanlin academician Lu Sui to draft an order appointing the Prince of Jiang to direct state affairs.

sentences.zh: 明日，下遺詔，絳王即位。

translations.literal: The next day a testamentary edict was issued and the Prince of Jiang ascended the throne.
translations.idiomatic: The next day a testamentary edict was issued and the Prince of Jiang ascended the throne.

sentences.zh: 克明等恃功，將易置左右，自引支黨顓兵柄。

translations.literal: Keming and the others, relying on their merit, intended to replace those around the throne and brought in their own faction to monopolize military power.
translations.idiomatic: Keming and his fellows, relying on their exploit, intended to replace those around the throne and brought in their faction to monopolize military power.

sentences.zh: 於時，樞密使王守澄楊承和、中尉梁守謙魏從簡與宰相裴度共迎江王，發左、右神策及六軍飛龍兵討之，克明投井死，出其屍戮之。

translations.literal: At that time the Privy Councilors Wang Shoucheng and Yang Chengho, the Army Commissioners Liang Shouqian and Wei Congjian, and Chief Minister Pei Du together welcomed the Prince of Jiang; they mobilized the Left and Right Shence Armies and the Flying Dragon troops of the Six Armies to suppress them; Keming threw himself into a well and died; his corpse was taken out and publicly mutilated.
translations.idiomatic: Privy councilors Wang Shoucheng and Yang Chengho, army commissioners Liang Shouqian and Wei Congjian, and Chief Minister Pei Du welcomed the Prince of Jiang, mobilized the Left and Right Shence Armies and Flying Dragon troops to suppress them; Keming threw himself into a well and died, and his corpse was taken out and publicly mutilated.

sentences.zh: 務澄等皆斬首以徇，籍入家貲，又殺其黨數十人。

translations.literal: Wucheng and the others were all beheaded and displayed; their household property was confiscated; several dozen of their partisans were also killed.
translations.idiomatic: Wucheng and the others were beheaded and displayed, their property confiscated, and several dozen partisans were also killed.

sentences.zh: 始，克明謀逆，母禁不許。

translations.literal: At first when Keming plotted rebellion, his mother forbade it and would not permit it.
translations.idiomatic: When Keming first plotted rebellion, his mother forbade it.

sentences.zh: 文宗立，嘉母忠，賜錢千緡、絹五百匹，給婢二人。

translations.literal: When Wenzong ascended the throne, he praised the mother's loyalty and bestowed one thousand strings of cash, five hundred bolts of silk, and two maidservants.
translations.idiomatic: When Wenzong ascended the throne, he praised the mother's loyalty and bestowed one thousand strings of cash, five hundred bolts of silk, and two maidservants.

sentences.zh: 田令孜，字仲則，蜀人也，本陳氏。

translations.literal: Tian Lingzi, courtesy name Zhongze, was a man of Shu; his original surname was Chen.
translations.idiomatic: Tian Lingzi — courtesy name Zhongze, a man of Shu, originally surnamed Chen.

sentences.zh: 咸通時，歷小馬坊使。

translations.literal: In the Xiantong era he served successively as commissioner of the small horse ward.
translations.idiomatic: During the Xiantong years he served as commissioner of the small horse ward.

sentences.zh: 僖宗即位，擢令孜左神策軍中尉，是時西門匡範位右中尉，世號「東軍」、「西軍」。

translations.literal: When Emperor Xizong ascended the throne, Lingzi was promoted to Left Shence Army Commissioner; at that time Xi Men Kuangfan held the right commissionership — they were styled the East Army and the West Army.
translations.idiomatic: When Xizong took the throne, Lingzi was made Left Shence Army Commissioner while Ximen Kuangfan held the right post — they were known as the East Army and the West Army.

sentences.zh: 帝沖騃，喜鬥鵝走馬，數幸六王宅、興慶池與諸王鬥鵝，一鵝至五十錢。

translations.literal: The Emperor was childish and dull-witted, fond of cockfighting and horse-racing; he often visited the Six Princes' residence and Xingqing Pool to fight cocks with the princes — one cock could fetch fifty cash.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor was childish and dull, fond of cockfighting and horse-racing; he often visited the Six Princes' residence and Xingqing Pool to fight cocks with the princes, with a single bird fetching fifty cash.

sentences.zh: 與內園小兒尤昵狎，倚寵暴橫。

translations.literal: He was especially intimate and familiar with the inner-garden youths, who relied on favor to act with violence and arrogance.
translations.idiomatic: He was especially intimate with the inner-garden youths, who relied on favor to act with violence and arrogance.

sentences.zh: 始，帝為王時，與令孜同臥起，至是以其知書能處事，又帝資狂昏，故政事一委之，呼為「父」。

translations.literal: At first, when the Emperor was still a prince, he shared sleeping and rising with Lingzi; now, because Lingzi knew books and could handle affairs, and because the Emperor's nature was reckless and muddled, all government was entrusted to him and he was called Father.
translations.idiomatic: When the emperor had been a prince he had shared sleeping and rising with Lingzi; now, because Lingzi was literate and capable and the emperor reckless and muddled, all government was entrusted to him and he was called Father.

sentences.zh: 而荒酣無檢，發左藏、齊天諸庫金幣，賜伎子歌兒者日巨萬，國用耗盡。

translations.literal: Yet he was dissolute and drunken without restraint, drawing gold and coin from the Left Treasury, Qitian, and other storehouses, bestowing tens of thousands daily on performers and singers until state revenue was exhausted.
translations.idiomatic: Yet he was dissolute and drunken without restraint, drawing gold and coin from the Left Treasury and other storehouses and bestowing tens of thousands daily on performers until state revenue was exhausted.

sentences.zh: 令孜語內園小兒尹希復、王士成等，勸帝籍京師兩市蕃旅、華商寶貨舉送內庫，使者監櫃坊茶閣，有來訴者皆杖死京兆府。

translations.literal: Lingzi told the inner-garden youths Yin Xifu, Wang Shicheng, and others to urge the Emperor to register the goods of foreign merchants and Chinese traders in the capital's two markets and send them all to the inner treasury; envoys supervised the cabinet shops and tea houses; any who came to complain were beaten to death by the metropolitan prefecture.
translations.idiomatic: Lingzi told the inner-garden youths Yin Xifu and Wang Shicheng to urge the emperor to seize the goods of foreign and Chinese merchants in the capital's two markets for the inner treasury; envoys supervised the shops, and complainants were beaten to death by the metropolitan prefect.

sentences.zh: 令孜知帝不足憚，則販鬻官爵，除拜不待旨，假賜緋紫不以聞。

translations.literal: Knowing the Emperor was not to be feared, Lingzi then sold offices and ranks, making appointments without awaiting imperial command and granting scarlet and purple robes on false authority without reporting it.
translations.idiomatic: Knowing the emperor was not to be feared, Lingzi sold offices and ranks, made appointments without awaiting imperial command, and granted scarlet and purple robes on false authority without reporting it.

sentences.zh: 百度崩弛，內外垢玩。

translations.literal: The hundred offices collapsed and slackened; inside and outside the court grew filthy and dissolute.
translations.idiomatic: The hundred offices collapsed; inside and outside the court grew filthy and dissolute.

sentences.zh: 既所在盜起，上下相掩匿，帝不及知。

translations.literal: When bandits rose everywhere, superiors and subordinates concealed one another, and the Emperor never learned of it.
translations.idiomatic: When bandits rose everywhere, superiors and subordinates concealed one another, and the emperor never learned of it.

sentences.zh: 是時賢人無在者，惟佞鄙沓貪相與備員，偷安噤默而已。

translations.literal: At that time no worthy men remained; only the fawning, base, greedy, and grasping filled the posts, seeking ease in silence.
translations.idiomatic: At that time no worthy men remained; only the fawning, base, and greedy filled the posts in silence.

sentences.zh: 左拾遺侯昌蒙不勝憤，指言豎尹用權亂天下，疏入，賜死內侍省。

translations.literal: The Left Reminder Hou Changmeng, unable to bear his anger, pointed out that the eunuch chiefs abused power and threw the realm into disorder; when his memorial entered, he was ordered to die at the Palace Domestic Service.
translations.idiomatic: Left Reminder Hou Changmeng, unable to bear his anger, charged that the eunuch chiefs abused power and threw the realm into disorder; when his memorial entered, he was ordered to die at the Palace Domestic Service.

sentences.zh: 宰相盧攜素事令孜，每建白，必阿邑倡和。

translations.literal: Chief Minister Lu Xie had long served Lingzi; whenever he proposed a policy, he invariably flattered and echoed him.
translations.idiomatic: Chief Minister Lu Xie had long served Lingzi; whenever he proposed policy, he invariably flattered and echoed him.

sentences.zh: 初，黃巢求廣州，願罷兵，攜欲寵高駢，使有功，不聽賊。

translations.literal: At first Huang Chao sought Guangzhou and offered to cease hostilities; Xie wished to favor Gao Pian and let him win merit, and would not heed the rebels.
translations.idiomatic: At first Huang Chao sought Guangzhou and offered to cease hostilities; Xie wished to favor Gao Pian and let him win merit, and would not heed the rebels.

sentences.zh: 因又易置關東諸節度，賊乘之，陷東都。

translations.literal: He then also reshuffled the military governors east of the Pass; the rebels seized the opportunity and captured the Eastern Capital.
translations.idiomatic: He then reshuffled the military governors east of the Pass; the rebels seized the opportunity and captured the Eastern Capital.

sentences.zh: 令孜急，歸罪攜，奉帝西幸，步出金光門，至咸陽沙野，軍十餘騎呼曰：「巢為陛下除奸臣，乘輿今西，秦中父老何望？

translations.literal: Lingzi grew alarmed, blamed Xie, and escorted the Emperor west; they walked out through the Golden Light Gate; at the sandy wilds of Xianyang more than ten horsemen of the army cried, "Chao is removing wicked ministers for Your Majesty — the imperial carriage now goes west; what hope have the elders of Qin?
translations.idiomatic: Lingzi grew alarmed, blamed Xie, and escorted the emperor west on foot through the Golden Light Gate. At the sandy wilds of Xianyang more than ten horsemen cried, "Chao is removing wicked ministers for Your Majesty — the carriage goes west; what hope have the elders of Qin?

sentences.zh: 願還宮。」

translations.literal: We beg that you return to the palace."
translations.idiomatic: We beg that you return to the palace."

sentences.zh: 令孜叱之，以羽林騎馳斬，即以羽林白馬載帝，晝夜馳，舍駱谷。

translations.literal: Lingzi shouted them down and had the Imperial Guard cavalry gallop forth and behead them; then he had the Emperor borne on white Imperial Guard horses, galloping day and night, lodging at Luogu.
translations.idiomatic: Lingzi shouted them down and had the Imperial Guard cavalry behead them; then he had the emperor borne on white Imperial Guard horses, galloping day and night to Luogu.

sentences.zh: 時陳敬瑄方節度西川，令孜兄也，故請帝幸蜀。

translations.literal: At that time Chen Jingxuan was military governor of western Shu — Lingzi's elder brother — and therefore urged the Emperor to visit Shu.
translations.idiomatic: Chen Jingxuan was then military governor of western Shu — Lingzi's elder brother — and therefore urged the emperor to visit Shu.

sentences.zh: 有詔以令孜為十軍十二衛觀軍容制置左右神策護駕使。

translations.literal: An edict appointed Lingzi Commissioner for Observing Army Affairs and Director of the Ten Armies and Twelve Guards, with charge over the Left and Right Shence Armies as Protector of the Imperial Progress.
translations.idiomatic: An edict appointed Lingzi commissioner for observing army affairs and director of the Ten Armies and Twelve Guards, with charge over the Left and Right Shence Armies as protector of the imperial progress.

sentences.zh: 至成都，進左金吾衛上將軍，兼判四衛事，封晉國公。

translations.literal: On reaching Chengdu he was advanced to General-in-Chief of the Left Golden Guard and given concurrent charge of the Four Guards, enfeoffed as Duke of Jin.
translations.idiomatic: On reaching Chengdu he was made General-in-Chief of the Left Golden Guard with concurrent charge of the Four Guards and enfeoffed as Duke of Jin.

sentences.zh: 帝見蜀狹陋，稍郁郁，日與嬪侍博飲，時時攘袂北望，怊然流涕。

translations.literal: The Emperor, finding Shu cramped and mean, grew somewhat depressed; day after day he drank and gambled with consorts and attendants, often pushing up his sleeves to gaze north and weeping in distress.
translations.idiomatic: Finding Shu cramped and mean, the emperor grew depressed; day after day he drank and gambled with consorts and attendants, often pushing up his sleeves to gaze north and weep.

sentences.zh: 令孜伺間開釋，呼萬歲，帝為怡悅，因盛稱鄭畋、王鐸、程宗楚、李鋌、敬瑄方並力，賊不足虞。

translations.literal: Lingzi seized an opening to console him, shouting Long live the Emperor; the Emperor was pleased and Lingzi then lavishly praised Zheng Tian, Wang Duo, Cheng Zongchu, Li Di, and Jingxuan as joining forces, saying the rebels were not to be feared.
translations.idiomatic: Lingzi seized an opening to console him, shouting "Long live the emperor!" The emperor was pleased, and Lingzi lavishly praised Zheng Tian, Wang Duo, Cheng Zongchu, Li Di, and Jingxuan as joining forces, saying the rebels were not to be feared.

sentences.zh: 帝曰：「善。」

translations.literal: The Emperor said, "Good."
translations.idiomatic: The emperor said, "Good."

sentences.zh: 初，成都募陳許兵三千，服黃帽，名「黃頭軍」，以捍蠻。

translations.literal: At first Chengdu recruited three thousand troops from Chen and Xu, who wore yellow caps and were called the Yellow Cap Army, to resist the barbarians.
translations.idiomatic: Chengdu had recruited three thousand troops from Chen and Xu who wore yellow caps and were called the Yellow Cap Army to resist the barbarians.

sentences.zh: 帝至，大勞將士，扈從者已賜，而不及黃頭軍，皆竊怨令孜。

translations.literal: When the Emperor arrived he greatly rewarded the officers and soldiers; those who had escorted him were already given gifts, but the Yellow Cap Army was not included — all secretly resented Lingzi.
translations.idiomatic: When the emperor arrived he greatly rewarded the troops; escorts were already rewarded but the Yellow Cap Army was not — all secretly resented Lingzi.

sentences.zh: 令孜置酒會諸將，以黃金樽行酒，即賜之。

translations.literal: Lingzi set out wine and feasted the generals, serving wine in a golden goblet and then bestowing it on them.
translations.idiomatic: Lingzi feasted the generals, serving wine in a golden goblet and then bestowing it on them.

sentences.zh: 黃頭將郭琪不肯飲，曰：「軍容能易偏惠，均眾士，誠大願也。」

translations.literal: The Yellow Cap general Guo Qi refused to drink and said, "If the Army Commissioner could change partial favor and treat all the soldiers equally, that would indeed be a great wish."
translations.idiomatic: Yellow Cap general Guo Qi refused to drink and said, "If the army commissioner could treat all soldiers equally instead of showing partial favor, that would be a great wish."

sentences.zh: 令孜目曰：「君有功邪？」

translations.literal: Lingzi glared and said, "Have you merit?"
translations.idiomatic: Lingzi glared and said, "Have you merit?"

sentences.zh: 答曰：「戰党項，薄契丹，數十戰，此琪之功。」

translations.literal: He answered, "Fighting the Tangut, raiding the Khitan — several dozen battles; that is Qi's merit."
translations.idiomatic: He answered, "Fighting the Tangut and raiding the Khitan in several dozen battles — that is my merit."

sentences.zh: 令孜嘻，怒曰：「知之。」

translations.literal: Lingzi sneered and said angrily, "I know it."
translations.idiomatic: Lingzi sneered and said angrily, "I know it."

sentences.zh: 密以冘註酒中，琪飲已，馳歸，殺一婢，吮血得解。

translations.literal: He secretly poured poison into the wine; when Qi had drunk he galloped home, killed a maid, and sucked her blood to obtain the antidote.
translations.idiomatic: He secretly poisoned the wine; when Qi had drunk he galloped home, killed a maid, and sucked her blood for the antidote.

sentences.zh: 因夜燒營，剽城邑，敬瑄討敗之，奔廣都，遂走高駢所。

translations.literal: That night he burned the camp and raided towns; Jingxuan defeated him; he fled to Guangdu and then went to Gao Pian's territory.
translations.idiomatic: That night he burned the camp and raided towns; Jingxuan defeated him; he fled to Guangdu and then went to Gao Pian.

sentences.zh: 帝聞變，與令孜保東城自守，群臣不得見。

translations.literal: When the Emperor heard of the disturbance, he and Lingzi held the eastern city in defense; the ministers could not see him.
translations.idiomatic: When the emperor heard of the disturbance, he and Lingzi held the eastern city; the ministers could not see him.

sentences.zh: 左拾遺孟昭圖請對，不召，因上疏極陳：「君與臣一體相成，安則同寧，危則共難。

translations.literal: The Left Reminder Meng Zhaotu requested audience and was not summoned; he therefore submitted a memorial stating at length, "Sovereign and minister form one body together — in peace they share tranquility, in peril they share hardship.
translations.idiomatic: Left Reminder Meng Zhaotu requested audience and was not summoned; he submitted a memorial stating, "Sovereign and minister form one body — in peace they share tranquility, in peril they share hardship.

sentences.zh: 昔日西幸，不告南司，故宰相、御史中丞、京兆尹悉碎於賊，唯兩軍中尉以扈乘輿得全。

translations.literal: In former days on the western journey the southern offices were not informed; hence the chief minister, censor-in-chief, and metropolitan prefect were all destroyed by the rebels — only the two army commissioners, escorting the imperial carriage, escaped whole.
translations.idiomatic: On the earlier western journey the southern offices were not informed; the chief minister, censor-in-chief, and metropolitan prefect were all destroyed by the rebels — only the two army commissioners escorting the carriage escaped.

sentences.zh: 今百官之在者，率冒重險出百死者也。

translations.literal: The officials who remain now are mostly those who braved grave peril and escaped a hundred deaths.
translations.idiomatic: The officials who remain are mostly those who braved grave peril and escaped a hundred deaths.

sentences.zh: 昨昔黃頭亂，火照前殿，陛下惟與令孜閉城自守，不召宰相，不謀群臣，欲入不得，求對不許。

translations.literal: Yesterday when the Yellow Caps rebelled, fire lit the front hall; Your Majesty only shut the city with Lingzi in defense, did not summon the chief minister, did not consult the ministers — those wishing to enter could not, those seeking audience were refused.
translations.idiomatic: Yesterday when the Yellow Caps rebelled, fire lit the front hall; Your Majesty only shut the city with Lingzi, summoned no chief minister, consulted no ministers — those wishing to enter could not, those seeking audience were refused.

sentences.zh: 且天下者，高祖、太宗之天下，非北司之天下；

translations.literal: Moreover the realm is the realm of Gaozu and Taizong, not the realm of the northern offices;
translations.idiomatic: Moreover the realm is the realm of Gaozu and Taizong, not the realm of the northern offices;

sentences.zh: 陛下固九州天子，非北司之天子。

translations.literal: Your Majesty is surely Son of Heaven of the Nine Regions, not Son of Heaven of the northern offices.
translations.idiomatic: Your Majesty is Son of Heaven of the Nine Regions, not Son of Heaven of the northern offices.

sentences.zh: 北司豈悉忠於南司？

translations.literal: Are the northern offices all loyal to the southern offices?
translations.idiomatic: Are the northern offices all loyal to the southern offices?

sentences.zh: 廷臣豈無用於敕使？

translations.literal: Are court ministers of no use to the edict-bearers?
translations.idiomatic: Are court ministers of no use to the edict-bearers?

sentences.zh: 文宗時，宮中災，左右巡使不到，皆被顯責，安有天子播越，而宰相無所豫，群司百官棄若路人？

translations.literal: In Emperor Wenzong's time, when fire struck the palace, if the left and right patrol commissioners did not arrive they were all openly punished — how can there be a Son of Heaven cast adrift while the chief minister has no part and the hundred offices are abandoned like passers-by?
translations.idiomatic: Under Wenzong, when fire struck the palace, patrol commissioners who failed to arrive were openly punished — how can the emperor be cast adrift while the chief minister has no part and the hundred offices are abandoned like strangers?

sentences.zh: 已事誠不足諫，而來者冀可追也。」

translations.literal: What is past truly cannot be remonstrated about, but what is to come may yet be retrieved."
translations.idiomatic: What is past cannot be remonstrated about, but what is to come may yet be retrieved."

sentences.zh: 疏入，令孜匿不奏，矯詔貶昭圖嘉州司戶參軍，使人沈於蟆頤津。

translations.literal: When the memorial entered, Lingzi concealed it and did not present it; he forged an edict demoting Zhaotu to registrar of Jia prefecture and had him drowned at Maoyi Ford.
translations.idiomatic: When the memorial entered, Lingzi concealed it and forged an edict demoting Zhaotu to registrar of Jia prefecture and had him drowned at Maoyi Ford.

sentences.zh: 初，昭圖知正言必見害，謂家隸曰：「大盜未殄，宦豎離間君臣，吾以諫為官，不可坐觀覆亡，疏入必死，而能收吾骸乎？」

translations.literal: At first Zhaotu knew that upright speech would bring harm and told a household servant, "The great bandits are not yet destroyed; the eunuchs sunder sovereign and minister — my office is remonstrance; I cannot sit and watch ruin. When the memorial enters I shall surely die — can you recover my body?"
translations.idiomatic: Zhaotu knew upright speech would bring harm and told a household servant, "The great bandits are not yet destroyed; eunuchs sunder sovereign and minister. My office is remonstrance; I cannot sit and watch ruin. When the memorial enters I shall die — can you recover my body?"

sentences.zh: 隸許諾，卒葬其屍。

translations.literal: The servant promised, and in the end buried his corpse.
translations.idiomatic: The servant promised and in the end buried his body.

sentences.zh: 朝廷痛之。

translations.literal: The court grieved for him.
translations.idiomatic: The court grieved for him.

sentences.zh: 賊平，令孜以王鐸為儒臣且無功，而首謀召沙陀者，楊復光也，欲歸重北司，故罷鐸都統，以復光功第一。

translations.literal: When the rebels were pacified, Lingzi considered Wang Duo a Confucian minister without merit, while Yang Fuguang was the first to plot summoning the Shatuo; wishing to return credit to the northern offices, he therefore removed Duo from supreme command and ranked Fuguang's merit first.
translations.idiomatic: When the rebels were pacified, Lingzi considered Wang Duo a scholar without merit while Yang Fuguang had first plotted to summon the Shatuo; wishing to return credit to the northern offices, he removed Duo from supreme command and ranked Fuguang's merit first.

sentences.zh: 又忌復光且逼己，故薄其賞。

translations.literal: He also resented Fuguang as pressing upon himself and therefore stinted his reward.
translations.idiomatic: He also resented Fuguang as a rival and therefore stinted his reward.

sentences.zh: 自謂帷幄決勝，系王室輕重，出入倨甚。

translations.literal: He considered himself decisive within the tent curtains and holding the weight of the royal house; going in and out he was very arrogant.
translations.idiomatic: He considered himself decisive in council and holding the weight of the royal house; going in and out he was very arrogant.

sentences.zh: 會復光死，大喜，即罷復恭樞密使。

translations.literal: When Fuguang died he was greatly pleased and at once removed Fugong from the privy councilorship.
translations.idiomatic: When Fuguang died he was greatly pleased and at once removed Fugong from the privy councilorship.

sentences.zh: 中人曹知愨者，富家子，頗沈鷙。

translations.literal: The eunuch Cao Zhiyu was the son of a wealthy family and rather deep and fierce.
translations.idiomatic: The eunuch Cao Zhiyu was from a wealthy family and rather deep and fierce.

sentences.zh: 賊在長安，知愨以清、濁二谷之人倚山為屯，不屈賊。

translations.literal: While the rebels were in Chang'an, Zhiyu had the people of the Qing and Zhuo valleys rely on the mountains in encampments and would not submit to the rebels.
translations.idiomatic: While the rebels held Chang'an, Zhiyu had the people of the Qing and Zhuo valleys camp in the mountains and refuse to submit.

sentences.zh: 陰教士卒變衣服、言語與賊類者，夜入長安攻賊營，賊大懼。

translations.literal: He secretly taught soldiers to change clothes and speech to resemble the rebels, enter Chang'an by night, and attack rebel camps; the rebels were greatly afraid.
translations.idiomatic: He secretly taught soldiers to disguise themselves as rebels, enter Chang'an by night, and attack rebel camps; the rebels were greatly afraid.

sentences.zh: 帝聞，賜金紫，擢內常侍。

translations.literal: When the Emperor heard, he bestowed gold and purple and promoted him to Inner Regular Attendant.
translations.idiomatic: When the emperor heard, he bestowed gold and purple and promoted him to Inner Regular Attendant.

sentences.zh: 聞帝將還，因大言：「我且擁眾大散關下，閱群臣可歸者納之。」

translations.literal: Hearing the Emperor would return, he spoke boldly, "I shall gather troops below Dasan Pass and review which ministers may return and take them in."
translations.idiomatic: Hearing the emperor would return, he spoke boldly, "I shall gather troops below Dasan Pass and take in whichever ministers may return."

sentences.zh: 令孜謂然，密令王行瑜以邠州兵度嵯峨山，襲殺其眾。

translations.literal: Lingzi thought this plausible and secretly ordered Wang Xingyu to lead Binzhou troops over Cuoe Mountain and attack and kill his followers.
translations.idiomatic: Lingzi agreed and secretly ordered Wang Xingyu to lead Binzhou troops over Cuoe Mountain and attack and kill his followers.

sentences.zh: 由是益自肆，禁制天子不得有所主斷。

translations.literal: From this he grew still more unrestrained, restraining the Son of Heaven so he could make no decisions of his own.
translations.idiomatic: From this he grew still more unrestrained, restraining the emperor so he could make no decisions of his own.

sentences.zh: 帝以其專，語左右輒流涕。

translations.literal: Because of his monopoly the Emperor, speaking to those at his side, would often weep.
translations.idiomatic: Because of his monopoly the emperor would often weep when speaking to those at his side.

sentences.zh: 復光部將鹿晏弘、王建等，以八都眾二萬取金、洋等州，進攻興元，節度使牛頊奔龍州，晏弘自為留後，以建及張造、韓建等為部刺史。

translations.literal: Fuguang's subordinates Lu Yanhong, Wang Jian, and others, with twenty thousand men of the eight commands, seized Jin, Yang, and other prefectures and advanced on Xingyuan; the military governor Niu Xu fled to Longzhou; Yanhong made himself acting governor and appointed Jian, Zhang Zao, Han Jian, and others as command prefects.
translations.idiomatic: Fuguang's subordinates Lu Yanhong and Wang Jian, with twenty thousand men of the eight commands, seized Jin, Yang, and other prefectures and advanced on Xingyuan; military governor Niu Xu fled to Longzhou; Yanhong made himself acting governor and appointed Jian, Zhang Zao, Han Jian, and others command prefects.

sentences.zh: 帝還，懼見討，引兵走許州。

translations.literal: When the Emperor returned, fearing punishment, he led his troops and fled to Xuzhou.
translations.idiomatic: When the emperor returned, fearing punishment, he led his troops to Xuzhou.

sentences.zh: 王建率義勇四軍迎帝西縣，復以建及韓建等主之，號「隨駕五都。」

translations.literal: Wang Jian led the four volunteer armies to welcome the Emperor at Xi county; Lingzi again put Jian and Han Jian in command of them, styling them the Five Commands Escorting the Carriage."
translations.idiomatic: Wang Jian led the four volunteer armies to welcome the emperor at Xi county; Lingzi again put Jian and Han Jian in command, styling them the Five Commands Escorting the Carriage."

sentences.zh: 令孜以復光故，才授諸衛將軍，皆養為子。

translations.literal: Because of Fuguang, Lingzi only granted them generals of the guards and adopted them all as sons.
translations.idiomatic: Because of Fuguang, Lingzi only granted them guard generalships and adopted them all as sons.

sentences.zh: 別募神策新軍，以千人為都，凡五十四都，分左右為十軍統之。

translations.literal: He separately recruited a new Shence army, with one thousand men per command, fifty-four commands in all, divided left and right into ten armies to command them.
translations.idiomatic: He separately recruited a new Shence army of fifty-four commands of one thousand men each, divided left and right into ten armies.

sentences.zh: 又遣親信覘諸鎮，不附己者以罪除徙。

translations.literal: He also sent trusted agents to observe the military districts; those not attached to him were removed and transferred on fabricated charges.
translations.idiomatic: He also sent trusted agents to observe the districts; those not attached to him were removed and transferred on fabricated charges.

sentences.zh: 養子匡祐宣慰河中，王重榮厚為禮，基祐傲甚，舉軍怒，重榮因數令孜罪，責其無禮，監軍和解乃去。

translations.literal: His adopted son Kuangyou went as envoy to console Hezhong; Wang Chongrong treated him with great courtesy, but Kuangyou was very arrogant; the whole army grew angry; Chongrong therefore enumerated Lingzi's crimes and rebuked his lack of courtesy; the army commissioner mediated and he then departed.
translations.idiomatic: His adopted son Kuangyou went as envoy to console Hezhong; Wang Chongrong treated him with great courtesy, but Kuangyou was very arrogant and the whole army grew angry; Chongrong enumerated Lingzi's crimes and rebuked his lack of courtesy; the army commissioner mediated and he departed.

sentences.zh: 匡祐還，訴令孜，且勸圖之。

translations.literal: Kuangyou on returning complained to Lingzi and also urged plotting against Chongrong.
translations.idiomatic: Kuangyou on returning complained to Lingzi and urged plotting against Chongrong.

sentences.zh: 令孜白以兩鹽池歸鹽鐵使，即自兼兩池榷鹽使。

translations.literal: Lingzi reported that the two salt ponds should revert to the salt and iron commissioner, then concurrently took the salt monopoly commissionership of both ponds himself.
translations.idiomatic: Lingzi reported that the two salt ponds should revert to the salt and iron commissioner, then took the salt monopoly of both ponds himself.

sentences.zh: 重榮不奉詔，表暴令孜十罪。

translations.literal: Chongrong did not obey the edict and memorialized exposing ten crimes of Lingzi.
translations.idiomatic: Chongrong did not obey the edict and memorialized exposing ten crimes of Lingzi.

sentences.zh: 令孜自將討重榮，率邠寧朱玫、鳳翔李昌符，合鄜、延、靈、夏等兵凡三萬，壁沙苑。

translations.literal: Lingzi personally led the campaign against Chongrong, commanding Zhu Mei of Binning, Li Changfu of Fengxiang, and combining troops from Fu, Yan, Ling, Xia, and elsewhere — thirty thousand in all — encamped at Shayuan.
translations.idiomatic: Lingzi personally led the campaign against Chongrong with Zhu Mei of Binning, Li Changfu of Fengxiang, and troops from Fu, Yan, Ling, Xia, and elsewhere — thirty thousand in all — encamped at Shayuan.

sentences.zh: 重榮說太原李克用連和，克用上書請誅令孜、玫，帝和之，不從。

translations.literal: Chongrong persuaded Li Keyong of Taiyuan to join in alliance; Keyong submitted a memorial requesting execution of Lingzi and Mei; the Emperor reconciled them but did not consent.
translations.idiomatic: Chongrong persuaded Li Keyong of Taiyuan to ally with him; Keyong memorialized requesting execution of Lingzi and Mei; the emperor sought reconciliation but did not consent.

sentences.zh: 大戰沙苑，王師敗。

translations.literal: A great battle was fought at Shayuan and the imperial army was defeated.
translations.idiomatic: A great battle was fought at Shayuan and the imperial army was defeated.

sentences.zh: 玫走還邠州，與昌符皆恥為令孜用，還與重榮合。

translations.literal: Mei fled back to Binzhou; he and Changfu were both ashamed to be used by Lingzi and in turn joined Chongrong.
translations.idiomatic: Mei fled back to Binzhou; he and Changfu were both ashamed to be used by Lingzi and joined Chongrong.

sentences.zh: 神策兵潰還，略所過皆盡。

translations.literal: The Shence troops broke and returned, plundering everything along their route.
translations.idiomatic: The Shence troops broke and returned, plundering everything along their route.

sentences.zh: 克用逼京師，令孜計窮，乃焚坊市，劫帝夜啟開遠門出奔。

translations.literal: Keyong pressed the capital; Lingzi's plans were exhausted; he burned the wards and markets and seized the Emperor, opening the Kaiyuan Gate by night to flee.
translations.idiomatic: Keyong pressed the capital; Lingzi's plans were exhausted; he burned the wards and markets and seized the emperor, opening the Kaiyuan Gate by night to flee.

sentences.zh: 自賊破長安，火宮室、舍廬十七，後京兆王徽葺復粗完，至是令孜唱曰：「王重榮反。」

translations.literal: Since the rebels had broken Chang'an, seventeen palace halls and lodges had burned; later the metropolitan prefect Wang Hui had roughly restored them — now Lingzi proclaimed, "Wang Chongrong has rebelled."
translations.idiomatic: Since the rebels had broken Chang'an, seventeen palace halls had burned; later metropolitan prefect Wang Hui had roughly restored them — now Lingzi proclaimed, "Wang Chongrong has rebelled."

sentences.zh: 命火宮城，唯昭陽、蓬萊三宮僅存。

translations.literal: He ordered the palace city set afire; only the Zhaoyang and Penglai palaces among the three barely survived.
translations.idiomatic: He ordered the palace city set afire; only the Zhaoyang and Penglai palaces barely survived.

sentences.zh: 王建以義勇四軍扈帝，夜亂牢水，遂次陳倉。

translations.literal: Wang Jian with the four volunteer armies escorted the Emperor; by night they were thrown into disorder at Lao River and then halted at Chencang.
translations.idiomatic: Wang Jian with the four volunteer armies escorted the emperor; by night they were thrown into disorder at Lao River and halted at Chencang.

sentences.zh: 克用還河中，玫畏克用且偪，與重榮連章請誅令孜，而駐鳳翔。

translations.literal: Keyong returned to Hezhong; Mei feared Keyong's pressure and jointly memorialized with Chongrong requesting execution of Lingzi, while encamping at Fengxiang.
translations.idiomatic: Keyong returned to Hezhong; Mei feared Keyong's pressure and jointly memorialized with Chongrong requesting execution of Lingzi while encamping at Fengxiang.

sentences.zh: 令孜請帝幸興元，帝不從，令孜以兵入寢，逼帝夜出，郡臣無知者，宰相蕭遘等皆不及從。

translations.literal: Lingzi urged the Emperor to visit Xingyuan; the Emperor would not agree; Lingzi entered the sleeping quarters with troops and forced the Emperor out by night; the prefectural ministers knew nothing; Chief Minister Xiao Gou and others could not accompany him.
translations.idiomatic: Lingzi urged the emperor to visit Xingyuan; the emperor refused; Lingzi entered the sleeping quarters with troops and forced the emperor out by night; the prefectural ministers knew nothing; Chief Minister Xiao Gou and others could not accompany him.

sentences.zh: 玫勸興元節度使石君涉焚閣道，絕帝西意。

translations.literal: Mei urged Xingyuan military governor Shi Junshe to burn the plank road and cut off the Emperor's intent to go west.
translations.idiomatic: Mei urged Xingyuan military governor Shi Junshe to burn the plank road and cut off the emperor's intent to go west.

sentences.zh: 遘惡令孜劫質天子，生方鎮之難，使玫進迎乘輿。

translations.literal: Gou hated Lingzi for seizing the Son of Heaven as hostage and creating difficulties for the regional commanders; he had Mei advance to welcome the imperial carriage.
translations.idiomatic: Gou hated Lingzi for seizing the emperor as hostage and creating difficulties for the regional commanders; he had Mei advance to welcome the imperial carriage.

sentences.zh: 玫引兵追行在，敗興鳳楊晟軍，帝次梁、洋，稍引而南，玫兵及中營，左右被剽戮者不勝計。

translations.literal: Mei led troops in pursuit of the imperial progress, defeated Yang Sheng's Xingfeng army; the Emperor halted at Liang and Yang, then gradually moved south; Mei's troops reached the central camp and those at the Emperor's side who were slaughtered and plundered were beyond counting.
translations.idiomatic: Mei led troops in pursuit, defeated Yang Sheng's Xingfeng army; the emperor halted at Liang and Yang, then moved south; Mei's troops reached the central camp and those at the emperor's side slaughtered were beyond counting.

sentences.zh: 令孜懼人圖己，蒙面以行。

translations.literal: Lingzi feared men would plot against him and traveled with his face covered.
translations.idiomatic: Lingzi feared assassination and traveled with his face covered.

sentences.zh: 使王建長劍五百清道，囊傳國璽授之。

translations.literal: He had Wang Jian with five hundred long swords clear the road and gave him the imperial seal in a bag.
translations.idiomatic: He had Wang Jian with five hundred long swords clear the road and gave him the imperial seal in a bag.

sentences.zh: 次大散關，道險澀，帝危及難數矣。

translations.literal: When they halted at Dasan Pass the road was perilous and difficult; the Emperor was several times in danger and distress.
translations.idiomatic: At Dasan Pass the road was perilous; the emperor was several times in danger and distress.

sentences.zh: 分軍守靈壁，亢追兵。

translations.literal: Troops were divided to hold Lingbi and resist the pursuing army.
translations.idiomatic: Troops were divided to hold Lingbi and resist the pursuers.

sentences.zh: 玫長驅躡帝，帝以閣道毀，走它道，困甚，枕王建膝且寐，覺而飯，僅能至興元。

translations.literal: Mei drove hard in pursuit; the plank road was destroyed and the Emperor took another route, utterly exhausted; he slept with his head on Wang Jian's knee, woke and ate, and barely reached Xingyuan.
translations.idiomatic: Mei drove hard in pursuit; the plank road was destroyed and the emperor took another route, utterly exhausted; he slept with his head on Wang Jian's knee, woke and ate, and barely reached Xingyuan.

sentences.zh: 玫、重榮表誅令孜，安尉群臣。

translations.literal: Mei and Chongrong memorialized requesting execution of Lingzi and reassuring the ministers.
translations.idiomatic: Mei and Chongrong memorialized requesting execution of Lingzi and reassuring the ministers.

sentences.zh: 詔以令孜為劍南監軍使，留不去。

translations.literal: An edict appointed Lingzi army commissioner of Jiannan, but he remained and would not leave.
translations.idiomatic: An edict appointed Lingzi army commissioner of Jiannan, but he remained and would not leave.

sentences.zh: 重榮請幸河中，令孜沮而止。

translations.literal: Chongrong requested that the Emperor visit Hezhong; Lingzi obstructed it and stopped it.
translations.idiomatic: Chongrong requested that the emperor visit Hezhong; Lingzi obstructed it and stopped it.

sentences.zh: 宰相遘率群臣在鳳翔者表令孜顓國煽禍，惑小人計，交亂群帥，請誅之。

translations.literal: Chief Minister Gou led the ministers at Fengxiang in memorializing that Lingzi monopolized the state and fanned calamity, beguiled petty men's schemes, and threw the commanders into mutual disorder, requesting his execution.
translations.idiomatic: Chief Minister Gou led the ministers at Fengxiang in memorializing that Lingzi monopolized the state and fanned calamity, beguiled petty schemes, and threw the commanders into disorder, requesting his execution.

sentences.zh: 帝不及省，且詔重榮餉糧十五萬斛給行在，重榮以令孜在，不奉命。

translations.literal: The Emperor had no time to examine it and also ordered Chongrong to supply one hundred fifty thousand piculs of grain to the imperial progress; Chongrong, because Lingzi was present, did not obey.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor had no time to examine it and ordered Chongrong to supply one hundred fifty thousand piculs of grain to the imperial progress; Chongrong, because Lingzi was present, refused.

sentences.zh: 玫乃奉嗣襄王煴即偽位。

translations.literal: Mei then installed the heir Prince of Xiang, Li Yun, in the false position.
translations.idiomatic: Mei then installed the heir Prince of Xiang, Li Yun, on the false throne.

sentences.zh: 玫敗，帝乃得還京師。

translations.literal: When Mei was defeated the Emperor was able to return to the capital.
translations.idiomatic: When Mei was defeated the emperor was able to return to the capital.

sentences.zh: 始，帝入蜀，諸王徒步以從，壽王至斜谷不能進，令孜驅使前，王謝足且拘，得馬可濟。

translations.literal: At first when the Emperor entered Shu, the princes followed on foot; when the Prince of Shou reached Xiegu he could not advance; Lingzi drove him forward; the Prince apologized that his feet were sore and cramped and that with a horse he could manage.
translations.idiomatic: When the emperor first entered Shu, the princes followed on foot; at Xiegu the Prince of Shou could not advance; Lingzi drove him forward; the prince said his feet were sore and cramped and that with a horse he could manage.

sentences.zh: 令孜怒抶王，強之行，王恥之。

translations.literal: Lingzi in anger beat the Prince and forced him onward; the Prince was shamed.
translations.idiomatic: Lingzi in anger beat the prince and forced him onward; the prince was shamed.

sentences.zh: 及帝病，中外屬壽王，令孜入候帝曰：「陛下記臣否？」

translations.literal: When the Emperor fell ill, inside and outside the court looked to the Prince of Shou; Lingzi entered to attend the Emperor and said, "Does Your Majesty remember your servant?
translations.idiomatic: When the emperor fell ill, court and capital looked to the Prince of Shou; Lingzi entered to attend the emperor and said, "Does Your Majesty remember your servant?

sentences.zh: 帝直視不能語。

translations.literal: The Emperor stared straight ahead and could not speak.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor stared straight ahead and could not speak.

sentences.zh: 令孜自署劍南監軍使，閱拱宸奉鑾軍自衛，晝夜馳入成都，固表解官求醫藥，詔可。

translations.literal: Lingzi appointed himself military commissioner of Jiannan, reviewed the Gongchen Imperial Guard army to protect himself, raced day and night into Chengdu, repeatedly submitted memorials resigning his post and seeking medicine, and an edict approved.
translations.idiomatic: Lingzi appointed himself military commissioner of Jiannan, mustered the Gongchen Imperial Guard for his own protection, and raced day and night into Chengdu; he repeatedly memorialized to resign his post and seek medical treatment, and the court approved.

sentences.zh: 俄削官爵，長流儋州，然猶依敬瑄不行。

translations.literal: Soon his ranks and titles were stripped and he was exiled far to Danzhou, yet he still relied on Chen Jingxuan and did not go.
translations.idiomatic: Soon his ranks and titles were stripped and he was banished to distant Danzhou, yet he still relied on Chen Jingxuan and refused to go.

sentences.zh: 王即位，是為昭宗。

translations.literal: The prince ascended the throne; this was Emperor Zhaozong.
translations.idiomatic: The prince ascended the throne — this was Emperor Zhaozong.

sentences.zh: 楊復恭代為觀軍容使，出王建為壁州刺史。
