translations.literal: Yang Fugong replaced him as Army Supervision Commissioner and sent Wang Jian out as prefect of Bizhou.
translations.idiomatic: Yang Fugong replaced him as Army Supervision Commissioner and sent Wang Jian out to serve as prefect of Bizhou.

sentences.zh: 建取利州，自署防禦使，因略定閬、邛、蜀、黎、雅等州，詔即置永平軍，拜建節度使。

translations.literal: Jian seized Lizhou, appointed himself defense commissioner, and thereby subdued Lang, Qiong, Shu, Li, Ya, and other prefectures; an edict immediately established the Yongping Army and appointed Jian military commissioner.
translations.idiomatic: Jian seized Lizhou and appointed himself defense commissioner; he then subdued Lang, Qiong, Shu, Li, Ya, and other prefectures. An edict promptly established the Yongping Army and appointed Jian its military commissioner.

sentences.zh: 令孜謀與建連衡亢朝廷，且曰「吾子也」，書召之。

translations.literal: Lingzi plotted to ally with Jian in mutual support against the court, saying moreover, "You are my son," and summoned him by letter.
translations.idiomatic: Lingzi plotted to ally with Jian against the court, declaring, "You are my son," and summoned him by letter.

sentences.zh: 建喜，將至，復卻之。

translations.literal: Jian was delighted and was about to arrive, but then was turned back.
translations.idiomatic: Jian was delighted and set out to come, but was then turned back.

sentences.zh: 建怒，進圍成都。

translations.literal: Jian in anger advanced and besieged Chengdu.
translations.idiomatic: Enraged, Jian advanced and besieged Chengdu.

sentences.zh: 令孜登城謝建曰：「老夫久相厚，何見困？」

translations.literal: Lingzi mounted the wall and apologized to Jian, saying, "This old man has long been on close terms with you — why are you putting me in straits?
translations.idiomatic: Lingzi mounted the wall and apologized to Jian: "We have long been on close terms — why are you putting me in straits?

sentences.zh: 答曰：「父子恩，何敢忘！

translations.literal: He replied, "The grace between father and son — how dare I forget it!
translations.idiomatic: He replied, "The bond between father and son — how could I forget it!

sentences.zh: 顧父自絕朝廷，茍改圖，則父子如初。」

translations.literal: But father, you have cut yourself off from the court; if you would change your course, then father and son would be as before."
translations.idiomatic: But you have cut yourself off from the court. If you change course, we can be as we were before."

sentences.zh: 令孜曰：「吾欲面計事。」

translations.literal: Lingzi said, "I wish to meet face to face to discuss affairs."
translations.idiomatic: Lingzi said, "I wish to meet you face to face to discuss matters."

sentences.zh: 建然許，令孜夜負印節授建，明日入成都，囚令孜碧雞坊。

translations.literal: Jian agreed; that night Lingzi carried his seal and credentials on his back and handed them to Jian; the next day he entered Chengdu and imprisoned Lingzi in Biji Lane.
translations.idiomatic: Jian agreed. That night Lingzi strapped his seal and credentials to his back and surrendered them to Jian; the next day Jian entered Chengdu and imprisoned Lingzi in Biji Lane.

sentences.zh: 始，右神策統軍宋文通為諸軍所疾，令孜因事召見，欲殺之。

translations.literal: At first Song Wentong, commander of the Right Shence Army, was resented by the various armies; Lingzi summoned him on a pretext and wished to kill him.
translations.idiomatic: Earlier, Song Wentong, commander of the Right Shence Army, had been resented by the other armies. Lingzi summoned him on a pretext, intending to kill him.

sentences.zh: 既見，乃欣然更養為子，名彥賓，即李茂貞也，故獨上書雪其罪，詔為湖南監軍。

translations.literal: Once he saw him, he instead gladly adopted him as a son, naming him Yanbin — this was Li Maozhen — therefore [Maozhen] alone submitted a memorial clearing his guilt, and an edict appointed [Lingzi] supervisor of the Hunan armies.
translations.idiomatic: When he saw him, he instead gladly adopted him as a son and named him Yanbin — this was Li Maozhen. Later Maozhen alone submitted a memorial clearing Lingzi's guilt, and an edict appointed Lingzi supervisor of the Hunan armies.

sentences.zh: 凡二歲，與敬瑄同日死。

translations.literal: After two years in all, he died on the same day as Chen Jingxuan.
translations.idiomatic: Two years later, he died on the same day as Chen Jingxuan.

sentences.zh: 臨刑，裂帛為縆，授行刑者曰：「吾嘗位十軍容，殺我庸有禮！」

translations.literal: Facing execution, he tore silk into a cord, gave it to the executioner, and said, "I once held the rank of commander of ten armies — to kill me you ought to observe proper rites!
translations.idiomatic: Facing execution, he tore silk into a cord, handed it to the executioner, and said, "I once held the rank of commander of ten armies — you ought to kill me with proper ceremony!

sentences.zh: 因教縊人法，既死，而色不變。

translations.literal: He then taught the method of strangling a person; once dead, his complexion did not change.
translations.idiomatic: He then instructed them in the proper method of strangulation; after he died, his complexion did not change.

sentences.zh: 乾寧中，詔復官爵。

translations.literal: In the Qianning era, an edict restored his ranks and titles.
translations.idiomatic: During the Qianning era, an edict restored his ranks and titles.

sentences.zh: 楊復恭，字子恪，本林氏子，楊復光從兄也。

translations.literal: Yang Fugong, courtesy name Zike, was originally a son of the Lin clan; he was a cousin of Yang Fuguang.
translations.idiomatic: Yang Fugong, courtesy name Zike, was originally a son of the Lin clan and a cousin of Yang Fuguang.

sentences.zh: 宦父玄翼，咸通中領樞密，世為權家。

translations.literal: His eunuch father Xuanyi in the Xiantong era headed the Privy Council; for generations the family were power-holders.
translations.idiomatic: His eunuch father Xuanyi had headed the Privy Council during the Xiantong era; for generations the family had been a power in the court.

sentences.zh: 復恭略涉學術，監諸鎮兵。

translations.literal: Fugong had a slight acquaintance with scholarship and supervised the armies of the various commands.
translations.idiomatic: Fugong had some learning and supervised the armies of the various military commands.

sentences.zh: 龐勛亂，戰有功，自河陽監軍入拜宣徽使，擢樞密使。

translations.literal: During the Pang Xun rebellion he won merit in battle; from military commissioner of Heyang he entered the capital as Commissioner of the Palace Secretariat and was promoted to Privy Councilor.
translations.idiomatic: During the Pang Xun rebellion he distinguished himself in battle; from military commissioner of Heyang he entered the capital as Commissioner of the Palace Secretariat and was promoted to Privy Councilor.

sentences.zh: 黃巢盜京師，令孜顓威福，斫喪天下，中外莫敢亢，惟復恭屢與爭得失，令孜怒，下遷飛龍使，復恭乃臥疾藍田。

translations.literal: When Huang Chao plundered the capital, Lingzi monopolized power and fortune, cutting down and ruining the realm; inside and outside the court none dared oppose him — only Fugong repeatedly contested gains and losses with him; Lingzi in anger demoted him to commissioner of the Flying Dragon Corps; Fugong then took to his bed ill in Lantian.
translations.idiomatic: When Huang Chao plundered the capital, Lingzi monopolized power and ruined the realm; none at court or beyond dared oppose him — only Fugong repeatedly challenged him. Lingzi in anger demoted him to commissioner of the Flying Dragon Corps, and Fugong fell ill and retired to Lantian.

sentences.zh: 僖宗出居興元，復為樞密使，制置經略，多更其手。

translations.literal: When Emperor Xizong went out to dwell at Xingyuan, [Fugong] again became Privy Councilor; strategic arrangements and frontier commissions mostly passed through his hands.
translations.idiomatic: When Emperor Xizong withdrew to Xingyuan, Fugong again became Privy Councilor; most strategic arrangements and frontier commissions passed through his hands.

sentences.zh: 車駕還，遂代令孜為左神策中尉、六軍十二衛觀軍容使，封魏國公，實戶八百，賜號「忠貞啟聖定國功臣」。

translations.literal: When the imperial carriage returned, he then replaced Lingzi as Left Shence Army Commissioner and Army Supervision Commissioner of the Six Armies and Twelve Guards, was enfeoffed as Duke of Wei with eight hundred households of actual fief income, and granted the title "Meritorious Servant Who Is Loyal, Chaste, and Opens the Sage, Who Settles the State."
translations.idiomatic: When the imperial carriage returned, he replaced Lingzi as Left Shence Army Commissioner and Army Supervision Commissioner of the Six Armies and Twelve Guards, was enfeoffed as Duke of Wei with eight hundred households of actual fief income, and granted the title "Meritorious Servant Who Is Loyal, Chaste, and Opens the Sage, Who Settles the State."

sentences.zh: 帝崩，定冊立昭宗，賜鐵券，加金吾上將軍，稍攘取朝政。

translations.literal: When the emperor died, he settled the succession and enthroned Emperor Zhaozong, was granted an iron certificate, was promoted to General-in-Chief of the Golden Guard, and gradually seized hold of court governance.
translations.idiomatic: When the emperor died, he settled the succession and enthroned Emperor Zhaozong, was granted an iron certificate, was promoted to General-in-Chief of the Golden Guard, and gradually took control of court governance.

sentences.zh: 帝嘗曰：「朕不德，爾援立我矣，當減省侈長示天下。

translations.literal: The emperor once said, "I lack virtue — you supported and enthroned me; I should reduce extravagance and excess to show the realm.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor once said, "I lack virtue — you supported and enthroned me. I should cut back on extravagance and set an example for the realm.

sentences.zh: 我見故事，尚衣上御服日一襲，太常新曲日一解，今可禁止。」

translations.literal: I see in precedent that the Wardrobe Office presented one set of imperial robes per day, and the Court of Imperial Sacrifices one new tune per day — these may now be forbidden.
translations.idiomatic: I see from precedent that the Wardrobe Office presented the emperor with a new set of robes every day, and the Court of Imperial Sacrifices a new tune every day — such practices should now be forbidden.

sentences.zh: 復恭頓首稱善。

translations.literal: Fugong kowtowed and praised the idea.
translations.idiomatic: Fugong kowtowed and praised the proposal.

sentences.zh: 帝遂問遊幸費，對曰：「聞懿宗以來，每行幸無慮用錢十萬，金帛五車，十部樂工五百，犢車、紅網朱網畫香車百乘，諸衛士三千。

translations.literal: The emperor then asked about the cost of imperial tours; he replied, "I hear that since Emperor Yizong, each tour invariably cost no less than one hundred thousand strings of cash, five cartloads of gold and silk, five hundred musicians from ten ensembles, one hundred ox-carts and scented carriages painted with red nets and vermilion nets, and three thousand guards.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor then asked about the cost of imperial tours. Fugong replied, "Since Emperor Yizong's reign, each tour has cost at least one hundred thousand strings of cash, five cartloads of gold and silk, five hundred musicians from ten ensembles, one hundred ox-carts and painted scented carriages draped in red and vermilion nets, and three thousand guards.

sentences.zh: 凡曲江、溫湯若畋獵曰大行從，宮中、苑中曰小行從。」

translations.literal: At Qujiang, hot springs, or when hunting it was called the great travel retinue; within the palace or park it was called the small travel retinue.
translations.idiomatic: Tours to Qujiang, the hot springs, or the hunting grounds were called the great travel retinue; excursions within the palace or park were called the small travel retinue.

sentences.zh: 帝乃詔類減半。

translations.literal: The emperor then issued an edict cutting such expenses roughly in half.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor then issued an edict cutting such expenses roughly in half.

sentences.zh: 於是宰相韋昭度、張浚、杜讓能等為帝言大中故事，抑宦官不假借，帝亦稍厭復恭橫恣。

translations.literal: Thereupon the chief ministers Wei Zhaodu, Zhang Jun, and Du Rangneng told the emperor stories from the Dahe reign, repressing eunuchs without indulgence; the emperor also gradually grew weary of Fugong's arrogance and license.
translations.idiomatic: Thereupon the chief ministers Wei Zhaodu, Zhang Jun, and Du Rangneng cited precedents from the Dahe reign for restraining eunuchs without indulgence, and the emperor also gradually grew weary of Fugong's arrogance and overbearing conduct.

sentences.zh: 王瑰者，惠安太后弟，求節度使，帝問復恭，對曰：「產、祿傾漢，三思危唐，後族不可封拜。

translations.literal: Wang Gui was the younger brother of Empress Dowager Huian; he sought to be made military commissioner; the emperor asked Fugong, who replied, "Lü Chan and Lü Lu overturned Han, and Wu Sansi endangered Tang — consort clans must not be enfeoffed and promoted.
translations.idiomatic: Wang Gui was the younger brother of Empress Dowager Huian and sought a military commission. When the emperor asked Fugong, he replied, "Lü Chan and Lü Lu overturned Han, and Wu Sansi endangered Tang — consort clans must not be enfeoffed and promoted.

sentences.zh: 陛下誠愛瑰，任以它職可也，不宜假節外藩，恐負勢顓地不可制。」

translations.literal: If Your Majesty truly loves Gui, appoint him to another office — that is acceptable; you should not grant him credentials to govern an outer province, lest he rely on power to dominate territory beyond control.
translations.idiomatic: If Your Majesty truly favors Gui, you may appoint him to another office, but you should not grant him military credentials to govern a frontier province, lest he grow too powerful to control.

sentences.zh: 帝乃止。

translations.literal: The emperor then desisted.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor then dropped the matter.

sentences.zh: 瑰聞，怒甚，至禁中見復恭詬辱之，遂居中任事。

translations.literal: When Gui heard of it he was furious; he entered the inner palace, saw Fugong and reviled and insulted him, then took charge of affairs at court center.
translations.idiomatic: When Gui heard of this he was furious; he entered the inner palace, confronted Fugong, and reviled and insulted him, then took charge of affairs at court.

sentences.zh: 復恭不欲分己權，白為黔南節度使，道興元，而兄子守亮方領節度，陰勒利州刺史覆瑰舟於江，宗屬賓客皆死，以舟自敗聞。

translations.literal: Fugong did not wish to share his own power; he had [Gui] appointed military commissioner of Qiannan; when [Gui] passed through Xingyuan, Fugong's nephew Shouliang was then holding a military commission and secretly urged the prefect of Lizhou to capsize Gui's boat on the river — clansmen and guests all died; it was reported that the boat had foundered on its own.
translations.idiomatic: Fugong did not wish to share his power and had Gui appointed military commissioner of Qiannan. When Gui passed through Xingyuan, Fugong's nephew Shouliang, who then held a military commission, secretly ordered the prefect of Lizhou to capsize Gui's boat on the river. Gui's clansmen and guests all perished, and the report claimed the boat had foundered on its own.

sentences.zh: 帝知復恭謀，繇是深銜之。

translations.literal: The emperor knew of Fugong's plot and from this deeply resented him.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor learned of Fugong's plot and from that point deeply resented him.

sentences.zh: 復恭以諸子為州刺史，號「外宅郎君」；

translations.literal: Fugong had his various sons serve as prefects, styled "Gentlemen of the Outer Residences";
translations.idiomatic: Fugong appointed his sons as prefects, styling them "Gentlemen of the Outer Residences";

sentences.zh: 又養子六百人，監諸道軍。

translations.literal: he also had six hundred adoptive sons supervising the armies of the various circuits.
translations.idiomatic: he also had six hundred adoptive sons supervising the armies of the various circuits.

sentences.zh: 天下威勢，舉歸其門。

translations.literal: The authority of the realm all gathered at his gate.
translations.idiomatic: The power of the realm all flowed to his household.

sentences.zh: 守立為天威軍使，本胡弘立也，勇武冠軍，人畏之。

translations.literal: Shouli was commissioner of the Tianwei Army; originally Hu Hongli, his valor and martial prowess topped the armies, and people feared him.
translations.idiomatic: Shouli, originally named Hu Hongli, was commissioner of the Tianwei Army; his valor and martial prowess topped the armies, and people feared him.

sentences.zh: 帝欲斥復恭，懼為亂，乃好謂曰：「卿家胡子安在？

translations.literal: The emperor wished to dismiss Fugong but feared he would cause turmoil; he therefore spoke kindly to him, saying, "Where is that Hu-family lad of yours?
translations.idiomatic: The emperor wished to dismiss Fugong but feared he would cause unrest; he therefore spoke kindly to him: "Where is that Hu-family lad of yours?

sentences.zh: 吾欲令衛殿內。」

translations.literal: I wish to have him guard within the palace halls.
translations.idiomatic: I wish to have him serve as a guard within the palace.

sentences.zh: 復恭以守立見帝，賜姓李，名順節，使掌六軍管鑰，光寵甚。

translations.literal: Fugong presented Shouli to the emperor; he was granted the surname Li and the name Shunjie, and was made to hold the keys to the Six Armies — his glory and favor were very great.
translations.idiomatic: Fugong presented Shouli to the emperor; he was granted the surname Li and the name Shunjie, and was put in charge of the keys to the Six Armies — his glory and favor were immense.

sentences.zh: 既勢鈞，遂與復恭爭恨相中傷，暴發其私。

translations.literal: Once their power was equal, he then contended with Fugong in mutual hatred, slandering each other, and exposed Fugong's private affairs.
translations.idiomatic: Once their power was equal, he and Fugong turned on each other in mutual hatred, trading slanders and exposing each other's secrets.

sentences.zh: 復恭常肩輿抵太極殿。

translations.literal: Fugong regularly arrived by sedan chair at the Hall of Supreme Ultimate.
translations.idiomatic: Fugong regularly arrived by sedan chair at the Hall of Supreme Ultimate.

sentences.zh: 宰相對延英，論叛臣事，孔緯曰：「陛下左右有將反者。」

translations.literal: When the chief ministers met the emperor at Yanying, discussing rebel ministers, Kong Wei said, "At Your Majesty's side is someone who is about to rebel.
translations.idiomatic: When the chief ministers met the emperor at Yanying to discuss rebel ministers, Kong Wei said, "There is someone at Your Majesty's side who is about to rebel.

sentences.zh: 帝矍然。

translations.literal: The emperor started in alarm.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor started in alarm.

sentences.zh: 緯指復恭。

translations.literal: Wei pointed at Fugong.
translations.idiomatic: Wei pointed at Fugong.

sentences.zh: 復恭曰：「臣豈負陛下者？」

translations.literal: Fugong said, "How could I ever betray Your Majesty?
translations.idiomatic: Fugong said, "How could I ever betray Your Majesty?

sentences.zh: 緯曰：「復恭，陛下家奴，而肩輿至前殿。

translations.literal: Wei said, "Fugong — you are Your Majesty's household slave, yet you come by sedan chair to the front hall.
translations.idiomatic: Wei said, "Fugong, you are Your Majesty's household slave, yet you arrive by sedan chair at the front hall.

sentences.zh: 廣樹不逞皆姓楊，非反邪？」

translations.literal: You have widely planted unruly men all surnamed Yang — is that not rebellion?"
translations.idiomatic: You have planted unruly men everywhere, all surnamed Yang — is that not rebellion?"

sentences.zh: 復恭曰：「欲收士心輔天子。」

translations.literal: Fugong said, "I wished to win the hearts of warriors to assist the Son of Heaven."
translations.idiomatic: Fugong said, "I wished to win the loyalty of warriors to assist the Son of Heaven."

sentences.zh: 帝曰：「誠欲收士心，胡不假李姓乎？」

translations.literal: The emperor said, "If you truly wished to win warriors' hearts, why not grant them the surname Li?"
translations.idiomatic: The emperor said, "If you truly wished to win warriors' loyalty, why not grant them the imperial surname Li?"

sentences.zh: 復恭無以對。

translations.literal: Fugong had nothing with which to reply.
translations.idiomatic: Fugong had no reply.

sentences.zh: 會緯出守江陵，乃使人劫之長樂坡，斬其旌節，貲貯皆盡，緯僅免。

translations.literal: When Wei went out to govern Jiangling, [Fugong] sent men to waylay him at Changle Slope, cut down his banner and credentials, and plundered all his goods and stores — Wei barely escaped.
translations.idiomatic: When Wei went out to govern Jiangling, Fugong sent men to waylay him at Changle Slope, cut down his banner and credentials, and plundered all his goods and stores. Wei barely escaped with his life.

sentences.zh: 復恭子守貞為龍劍節度使，守忠洋州節度使，皆自擅貢賦，上書訕薄朝政。

translations.literal: Fugong's sons Shouzhen was military commissioner of Longjian and Shouzhong military commissioner of Yangzhou — both on their own seized tribute and taxes and submitted memorials mocking and slighting court governance.
translations.idiomatic: Fugong's sons Shouzhen and Shouzhong served as military commissioners of Longjian and Yangzhou respectively; both seized tribute and taxes on their own authority and submitted memorials mocking and denigrating the court.

sentences.zh: 大順二年，罷復恭兵，出為鳳翔監軍，不肯行，因丐致仕，詔可，遷上將軍，賜几杖。

translations.literal: In the second year of Dashun, Fugong was stripped of military command and sent out as military commissioner of Fengxiang; he refused to go and requested retirement — an edict approved; he was transferred to General-in-Chief and granted ceremonial staff and cane.
translations.idiomatic: In the second year of Dashun, Fugong was stripped of military command and ordered out as military commissioner of Fengxiang. He refused to go and requested retirement; the court approved and transferred him to General-in-Chief, granting him ceremonial staff and cane.

sentences.zh: 使者還，遣腹心殺使者於道，遁居商山。

translations.literal: When the envoy returned, he sent trusted agents to kill the envoy on the road and fled to dwell on Mount Shang.
translations.idiomatic: When the envoy returned, Fugong sent trusted agents to kill him on the road and fled to Mount Shang.

sentences.zh: 俄入居昭化坊第，第近玉山營，而子守信為軍使，數省候出入。

translations.literal: Soon he entered and occupied his residence in Zhaohua Ward; the residence was near Yushan Camp, and his son Shouxin was army commissioner — he often came to visit and attend to comings and goings.
translations.idiomatic: Soon he moved into his residence in Zhaohua Ward, near Yushan Camp. His son Shouxin was army commissioner and often came to visit and attend to his comings and goings.

sentences.zh: 或告父子且謀亂，時順節遙領鎮海軍節度使、同中書門下平章事，詔與神策軍使李守節率衛兵攻復恭，治殺使者罪，帝御延喜樓須之。

translations.literal: Someone reported that father and son were about to plot rebellion; at the time Shunjie remotely held the post of military commissioner of the Zhenhai Army and Concurrent Grand Councilor; an edict ordered him and Shence Army Commissioner Li Shoujie to lead palace guards to attack Fugong and punish the crime of killing the envoy; the emperor mounted the Yanxi Tower to await the outcome.
translations.idiomatic: Someone reported that father and son were plotting rebellion. Shunjie then held the remote post of military commissioner of the Zhenhai Army and Concurrent Grand Councilor. An edict ordered him and Shence Army Commissioner Li Shoujie to lead palace guards against Fugong to punish the murder of the envoy, while the emperor mounted the Yanxi Tower to await the outcome.

sentences.zh: 家人拒戰，守信亦率兵至昌化里，陣以待。

translations.literal: The household retainers resisted in battle; Shouxin also led troops to Changhua Quarter and formed ranks to await them.
translations.idiomatic: The household retainers resisted; Shouxin also led troops to Changhua Quarter and formed battle lines to await the attack.

sentences.zh: 會日入，復恭與守信舉族出奔，遂走興元。

translations.literal: When the sun set, Fugong and Shouxin fled with their entire clans and ran to Xingyuan.
translations.idiomatic: At sunset Fugong and Shouxin fled with their entire clans and made for Xingyuan.

sentences.zh: 順節已斥復恭，則橫暴，出入以兵從，兩軍中尉劉景宣、西門重遂察其意非常，以狀聞。

translations.literal: Shunjie, having already turned against Fugong, then became violent and overbearing, going in and out with troops in attendance; the two army commissioners Liu Jingxuan and Ximen Chongsui perceived his intentions were abnormal and reported the situation.
translations.idiomatic: Having already turned against Fugong, Shunjie became violent and overbearing, traveling everywhere with armed escorts. The two army commissioners Liu Jingxuan and Ximen Chongsui perceived his intentions were dangerous and reported the matter.

sentences.zh: 有詔召順節，輒以甲士三百入，至銀臺門，何止之，景宣引順節坐殿廡，部將嗣光審出斬之，從者大噪，出延喜門，剽永寧里，盡夕止。

translations.literal: There was an edict summoning Shunjie; he immediately entered with three hundred armored soldiers; at the Yintai Gate, He Zh stopped them; Jingxuan led Shunjie to sit in the portico of the hall; his subordinate general Siguang Shen came out and beheaded him; the followers raised a great clamor, went out the Yanxi Gate, and plundered Yongning Quarter — they did not stop until evening.
translations.idiomatic: An edict summoned Shunjie, but he entered with three hundred armored soldiers. At the Yintai Gate, He Zh stopped them. Jingxuan led Shunjie to sit in the hall portico, where his subordinate general Siguang Shen came out and beheaded him. Shunjie's followers raised a great clamor, went out through the Yanxi Gate, and plundered Yongning Quarter until evening.

sentences.zh: 賈德晟與順節皆為天威軍使，順節誅，頗嗟憤，重遂亦奏誅之。

translations.literal: Jia Desheng and Shunjie had both been commissioners of the Tianwei Army; when Shunjie was executed, Desheng sighed and was indignant; Chongsui also memorialized for his execution.
translations.idiomatic: Jia Desheng and Shunjie had both served as commissioners of the Tianwei Army. When Shunjie was executed, Desheng was deeply aggrieved; Chongsui also memorialized for his execution.

sentences.zh: 於是鳳翔李茂貞、邠州王行瑜、華州韓建、同州王行約、秦州李茂莊同劾守亮納叛臣，請出兵討罪，軍餉不仰度支。

translations.literal: Thereupon Li Maozhen of Fengxiang, Wang Xingyu of Binzhou, Han Jian of Huazhou, Wang Xingyue of Tongzhou, and Li Maozhuang of Qinzhou jointly impeached Shouliang for harboring rebel ministers, requested to lead troops to punish the crime, and [said] army provisions would not depend on the Ministry of Revenue.
translations.idiomatic: Thereupon Li Maozhen of Fengxiang, Wang Xingyu of Binzhou, Han Jian of Huazhou, Wang Xingyue of Tongzhou, and Li Maozhuang of Qinzhou jointly impeached Shouliang for harboring rebel ministers, requested permission to lead troops against him, and pledged not to rely on the Ministry of Revenue for army provisions.

sentences.zh: 茂貞請假山南招討使。

translations.literal: Maozhen requested to be appointed provisional Commissioner for Pacification of the South of the Mountains.
translations.idiomatic: Maozhen requested appointment as provisional Commissioner for Pacification of the South of the Mountains.

sentences.zh: 宦尹惜類執不可，帝亦謂茂貞得山南必難制，詔兩解之。

translations.literal: The eunuch Yin Xilei held that this was impermissible; the emperor also said that if Maozhen obtained the South of the Mountains he would surely be hard to control — an edict dissolved both [requests].
translations.idiomatic: The eunuch Yin Xilei objected that this was impermissible, and the emperor also said that if Maozhen gained the South of the Mountains he would be impossible to control. An edict denied both requests.

sentences.zh: 茂貞劾復恭自謂隋諸孫，以恭帝禪唐，故名復恭，逆狀明白，且請削守亮官爵。

translations.literal: Maozhen impeached Fugong for claiming to be a descendant of the Sui — because Emperor Gong of Sui abdicated to Tang, he was named Fugong — his treasonous conduct was clear; he also requested stripping Shouliang of rank and title.
translations.idiomatic: Maozhen impeached Fugong for claiming to be a descendant of the Sui — saying he was named Fugong because Emperor Gong of Sui had abdicated to Tang — and declared his treason clear; he also requested that Shouliang be stripped of rank and title.

sentences.zh: 遂擅與行瑜出討，自號興元節度使，詒宰相書，慢悖不臣。

translations.literal: He then on his own authority joined Xingyu in leading a punitive expedition, styled himself military commissioner of Xingyuan, and sent a letter to the chief minister — insolent, rebellious, and disloyal.
translations.idiomatic: He then on his own authority joined Xingyu in a punitive expedition, styled himself military commissioner of Xingyuan, and sent a letter to the chief minister that was insolent, rebellious, and disloyal.

sentences.zh: 帝為下詔，令茂貞、行瑜討之。

translations.literal: The emperor issued an edict ordering Maozhen and Xingyu to punish him.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor issued an edict ordering Maozhen and Xingyu to punish him.

sentences.zh: 景福元年，破其城，復恭、守亮、守信奔閬州，茂貞以子繼密守興元。

translations.literal: In the first year of Jingfu, they broke his city; Fugong, Shouliang, and Shouxin fled to Langzhou; Maozhen left his son Jimi to guard Xingyuan.
translations.idiomatic: In the first year of Jingfu they captured the city. Fugong, Shouliang, and Shouxin fled to Langzhou, while Maozhen left his son Jimi to guard Xingyuan.

sentences.zh: 詔吏部尚書徐彥若為鳳翔節度使，而以茂貞帥興元，不拜，請繼密為留後。

translations.literal: An edict appointed Xu Yanruo, Minister of Civil Appointments, as military commissioner of Fengxiang, and made Maozhen commander of Xingyuan — he did not accept the appointment and requested Jimi as acting commissioner.
translations.idiomatic: An edict appointed Xu Yanruo, Minister of Civil Appointments, as military commissioner of Fengxiang and made Maozhen commander of Xingyuan. Maozhen refused the appointment and requested Jimi as acting commissioner.

sentences.zh: 帝不得已，授以節度使，自是茂貞始強大。

translations.literal: The emperor had no alternative and granted him the military commission; from this Maozhen first grew powerful.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor had no choice but to grant him the military commission, and from that point Maozhen first grew truly powerful.

sentences.zh: 復恭與守亮等自閬州將北奔太原，趨商山，至乾元，為韓建邏士所禽，即斬復恭、守信，檻車送守亮京師，梟首長安市。

translations.literal: Fugong and Shouliang and the rest, from Langzhou intending to flee north to Taiyuan, headed for Mount Shang; at Qianyuan they were captured by Han Jian's patrol soldiers; Fugong and Shouxin were immediately beheaded; Shouliang was sent to the capital in a caged cart and his head was displayed in the Chang'an market.
translations.idiomatic: Fugong, Shouliang, and the others, intending to flee north from Langzhou to Taiyuan, headed for Mount Shang. At Qianyuan they were captured by Han Jian's patrol soldiers. Fugong and Shouxin were immediately beheaded; Shouliang was sent to the capital in a caged cart, and his head was displayed in the Chang'an market.

sentences.zh: 茂貞上復恭與守亮書曰：「承天門者，隋家舊業也，兒但積粟訓兵，何進奉為？

translations.literal: Maozhen submitted the letters between Fugong and Shouliang: "The Chengtian Gate — that is the old estate of the Sui house; my son, just stock grain and train troops — why submit tribute?
translations.idiomatic: Maozhen submitted letters exchanged between Fugong and Shouliang: "The Chengtian Gate is the old estate of the Sui house. My son, just stock grain and train troops — why bother with tribute?

sentences.zh: 吾披荊榛立天子，既得位，乃廢定策國老，奈負心門生何！」

translations.literal: I cleared brambles and thorns to establish the Son of Heaven; once he obtained the throne, he cast aside the elder statesman who settled the succession — how does he answer for betraying his patron-disciple!"
translations.idiomatic: I cleared the wilderness to establish the Son of Heaven. Once he took the throne, he cast aside the elder statesman who settled the succession — how does he answer for betraying his patron?"

sentences.zh: 門生，謂天子也，其不臣類此。

translations.literal: Patron-disciple" meant the Son of Heaven — his disloyalty was of this sort.
translations.idiomatic: Patron-disciple" here meant the Son of Heaven — his disloyalty was of this sort.

sentences.zh: 假子彥博奔太原收葬其屍，李克用為申雪，詔復官爵。

translations.literal: The adoptive son Yanbo fled to Taiyuan to gather and bury his corpse; Li Keyong pleaded to clear his name — an edict restored his ranks and titles.
translations.idiomatic: The adoptive son Yanbo fled to Taiyuan to recover and bury his body. Li Keyong petitioned to clear his name, and an edict restored his ranks and titles.

sentences.zh: 劉季述者，本微單，稍顯於僖、昭間，擢累樞密使。

translations.literal: Liu Jishu was originally of humble and obscure origin; he gradually rose to prominence between the Xizong and Zhaozong reigns, and was repeatedly promoted to Privy Councilor.
translations.idiomatic: Liu Jishu came from humble and obscure origins; he gradually rose to prominence between the reigns of Emperors Xizong and Zhaozong and was repeatedly promoted to Privy Councilor.

sentences.zh: 楊復恭之斥，帝以西門重遂為右神策軍中尉、觀軍容使。

translations.literal: When Yang Fugong was dismissed, the emperor appointed Ximen Chongsui as Right Shence Army Commissioner and Army Supervision Commissioner.
translations.idiomatic: When Yang Fugong was dismissed, the emperor appointed Ximen Chongsui as Right Shence Army Commissioner and Army Supervision Commissioner.

sentences.zh: 時李茂貞得興元，愈跋扈不軌，宰相杜讓能與內樞密使李周𧬤及重遂謀誅之，乃興師，以嗣覃王戒丕為京西招討使，神策大將軍李鐬副之。

translations.literal: At the time Li Maozhen had obtained Xingyuan and grew ever more overbearing and disloyal; Chief Minister Du Rangneng, Inner Privy Councilor Li Zhouhan, and Chongsui plotted to execute him — they raised an army, appointing the heir Prince of Tan, Li Jiepi, as Commissioner for Pacification of the Western Capital, with Shence Army Grand General Li Juan as his deputy.
translations.idiomatic: At the time Li Maozhen held Xingyuan and grew ever more overbearing and disloyal. Chief Minister Du Rangneng, Inner Privy Councilor Li Zhouhan, and Chongsui plotted to kill him and raised an army, appointing the heir Prince of Tan, Li Jiepi, as Commissioner for Pacification of the Western Capital, with Shence Army Grand General Li Juan as his deputy.

sentences.zh: 茂貞引兵迎壁盩厔，薄興平，王師潰。

translations.literal: Maozhen led troops to meet them and entrenched at Zhaozhi; he pressed close at Xingping and the imperial army collapsed.
translations.idiomatic: Maozhen led troops to meet them and entrenched at Zhaozhi; he pressed close at Xingping and the imperial army collapsed.

sentences.zh: 遂逼臨臯以陣，暴言讓能等罪，京師震恐，帝坐安福門，斬重遂、周𧬤以謝茂貞，更以駱全瓘、劉景宣代為兩中尉。

translations.literal: He then pressed his formation at Lingao and loudly proclaimed the crimes of Rangneng and the others; the capital was shaken with fear; the emperor sat at Anfu Gate and beheaded Chongsui and Zhouhan to appease Maozhen, replacing them with Luo Quanjin and Liu Jingxuan as the two army commissioners.
translations.idiomatic: He then pressed his formation at Lingao and loudly proclaimed the crimes of Rangneng and the others. The capital was shaken with fear. The emperor sat at Anfu Gate and beheaded Chongsui and Zhouhan to appease Maozhen, replacing them with Luo Quanjin and Liu Jingxuan as the two army commissioners.

sentences.zh: 乾寧二年，茂貞與王行瑜、韓建以兵入朝，李克用率師討茂貞，次渭北。

translations.literal: In the second year of Qianning, Maozhen, Wang Xingyu, and Han Jian entered the court with troops; Li Keyong led an army to punish Maozhen and halted north of the Wei River.
translations.idiomatic: In the second year of Qianning, Maozhen, Wang Xingyu, and Han Jian entered the capital with troops. Li Keyong led an army against Maozhen and halted north of the Wei River.

sentences.zh: 同州節度使王行實奔京師，謂景宣等曰：「沙陀十萬至矣，請奉天子出幸避其鋒。」

translations.literal: Wang Xingshi, military commissioner of Tongzhou, raced to the capital and said to Jingxuan and the others, "One hundred thousand Shatuo troops have arrived — I beg that we escort the Son of Heaven on a progress to avoid their sharp edge.
translations.idiomatic: Wang Xingshi, military commissioner of Tongzhou, raced to the capital and said to Jingxuan and the others, "One hundred thousand Shatuo troops have arrived. I beg that we escort the Son of Heaven away from the capital to avoid their assault.

sentences.zh: 景宣方與茂貞睦，故全瓘與鳳翔衛將閻圭共脅帝狩岐，王行實及景宣子繼晟縱火剽東市，帝登承天門，矢著樓闔。

translations.literal: Jingxuan was then on friendly terms with Maozhen; so Quanjin and the Fengxiang guard general Yan Gui together coerced the emperor to hunt at Qi; Wang Xingshi and Jingxuan's son Jicheng set fires and plundered the Eastern Market; the emperor mounted Chengtian Gate and an arrow struck the gate tower.
translations.idiomatic: Jingxuan was then on friendly terms with Maozhen, so Quanjin and the Fengxiang guard general Yan Gui together coerced the emperor to withdraw to Qi. Wang Xingshi and Jingxuan's son Jicheng set fires and plundered the Eastern Market. The emperor mounted Chengtian Gate, and an arrow struck the gate tower.

sentences.zh: 帝懼，暮出莎城，士民從者數十萬。

translations.literal: The emperor in fear at dusk left through Sha Gate; commoners and officials who followed numbered several hundred thousand.
translations.idiomatic: Terrified, the emperor at dusk left through Sha Gate, followed by several hundred thousand officials and commoners.

sentences.zh: 至谷口，人暍死十三，夜為盜掠，哭聲殷山。

translations.literal: At the valley mouth thirteen people died of heatstroke; by night they were plundered by robbers — wailing filled the mountains.
translations.idiomatic: At the valley mouth thirteen people died of heatstroke. By night they were plundered by bandits, and wailing filled the mountains.

sentences.zh: 徙駐石門。

translations.literal: They moved and encamped at Shimen.
translations.idiomatic: They moved and encamped at Shimen.

sentences.zh: 茂貞恐，乃殺全瓘、景宣及圭自解。

translations.literal: Maozhen grew fearful and then killed Quanjin, Jingxuan, and Gui to clear himself.
translations.idiomatic: Maozhen grew fearful and killed Quanjin, Jingxuan, and Gui to clear himself.

sentences.zh: 天子還京師，以景務脩、宋道弼代之，俄專國。

translations.literal: The Son of Heaven returned to the capital; Jing Wuxiu and Song Daobi replaced them, and soon monopolized state affairs.
translations.idiomatic: The Son of Heaven returned to the capital. Jing Wuxiu and Song Daobi replaced them and soon monopolized state affairs.

sentences.zh: 宰相崔胤惡之，徐彥若、王摶懼禍不解，稍抑胤以和北軍。

translations.literal: Chief Minister Cui Yin hated them; Xu Yanruo and Wang Tuan feared disaster would not end and slightly reined in Yin to make peace with the northern armies.
translations.idiomatic: Chief Minister Cui Yin hated them. Xu Yanruo and Wang Tuan feared the crisis would not end and slightly reined in Yin to make peace with the northern armies.

sentences.zh: 胤怒，劾摶黨宦豎，不忠，罷去，俄賜死；

translations.literal: Yin in anger impeached Tuan for siding with eunuch henchmen — disloyal — he was dismissed, and soon granted death by suicide;
translations.idiomatic: Yin in anger impeached Tuan for siding with eunuch henchmen and disloyalty; Tuan was dismissed and soon ordered to take his own life;

sentences.zh: 流道弼州，務脩愛州，並死灞橋；

translations.literal: Daobi was exiled to Daobizhou, Wuxiu to Aizhou — both died at Ba Bridge;
translations.idiomatic: Daobi was exiled to Daobizhou and Wuxiu to Aizhou — both died at Ba Bridge;

sentences.zh: 逐彥若於南海。

translations.literal: Yanruo was exiled to Nanhai.
translations.idiomatic: Yanruo was exiled to Nanhai.

sentences.zh: 乃以季述、王仲先為左右中尉，疾胤尤甚。

translations.literal: Thereupon Jishu and Wang Zhongxian were made left and right army commissioners; they especially hated Yin.
translations.idiomatic: Jishu and Wang Zhongxian were then appointed left and right army commissioners, and they especially hated Yin.

sentences.zh: 時帝嗜酒，怒責左右不常，季述等愈自危。

translations.literal: At the time the emperor was fond of wine and irregularly flew into rage and blamed those around him; Jishu and the others grew ever more fearful for themselves.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor was then fond of wine and would fly into unpredictable rages, blaming those around him. Jishu and his allies grew ever more fearful for their own lives.

sentences.zh: 先是，王子病，季述引內醫工車讓、謝筠，久不出，季述等共白帝，宮中不可妄處人。

translations.literal: Earlier a prince fell ill; Jishu brought in palace physicians Che Rang and Xie Yun, who stayed long without leaving; Jishu and the others together reported to the emperor that people should not be placed in the palace at random.
translations.idiomatic: Earlier, when a prince fell ill, Jishu brought in the palace physicians Che Rang and Xie Yun, who remained inside for a long time. Jishu and his allies jointly reported to the emperor that unauthorized persons should not be allowed to stay in the palace.

sentences.zh: 帝不納，詔著籍不禁。

translations.literal: The emperor did not accept this; an edict ordered that registered persons were not to be restricted.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor rejected the advice and issued an edict that registered personnel were not to be barred from the palace.

sentences.zh: 由是疑帝與有謀，乃外約朱全忠為兄弟，遣從子希正與汴邸官程巖謀廢帝。

translations.literal: Thereupon they suspected the emperor was plotting with them; they then formed an external pact with Zhu Quanzhong as sworn brothers and sent his nephew Xi Zheng and Bian prefecture official Cheng Yan to plot deposing the emperor.
translations.idiomatic: They then suspected the emperor was conspiring with the physicians. Jishu swore brotherhood with Zhu Quanzhong on the outside and sent his nephew Xi Zheng and the Bian prefecture official Cheng Yan to plot the emperor's deposition.

sentences.zh: 會全忠遣天平節度副使李振上計京師，巖因曰：「主上嚴急，內外惴恐，左軍中尉欲廢昏立明，若何？」

translations.literal: It happened that Quanzhong sent Pingyi deputy military commissioner Li Zhen to the capital to present accounts; Yan therefore said, "The sovereign is stern and harsh; inside and outside all tremble with fear; the Left Army Commissioner wishes to depose the dim and establish the clear — what do you think?
translations.idiomatic: When Quanzhong sent Li Zhen, deputy commissioner of the Pingyi circuit, to the capital to present accounts, Cheng Yan said to him, "The sovereign is harsh and unpredictable; court and capital alike live in dread. The Left Army Commissioner wishes to depose a dim ruler and install a clear one — what do you say?

sentences.zh: 振曰：「百歲奴事三歲郎主，常也。

translations.literal: Li Zhen said, "For a hundred-year-old slave to serve a three-year-old master-lord — that is the norm.
translations.idiomatic: Li Zhen replied, "For a hundred-year-old slave to serve a three-year-old master — that is only natural.

sentences.zh: 亂國不義，廢君不祥，非吾敢聞。」

translations.literal: To disturb the state is unrighteous; to depose the sovereign is inauspicious — this is not something I dare hear of."
translations.idiomatic: To throw the state into chaos is unrighteous; to depose the sovereign is inauspicious. This is not something I dare even hear discussed."

sentences.zh: 希正大沮。

translations.literal: Xi Zheng was greatly discouraged.
translations.idiomatic: Xi Zheng was deeply discouraged.

sentences.zh: 帝夜獵苑中，醉殺侍女三人，明日午漏上，門不啟。

translations.literal: The emperor hunted in the park at night, drunkenly killed three maidservants; the next day when the noon clepsydra had passed, the gates did not open.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor hunted in the park at night and, in a drunken rage, killed three maidservants. The next day, after the noon hour had passed, the palace gates still did not open.

sentences.zh: 季述見胤曰：「宮中殆不測。」

translations.literal: Jishu saw Yin and said, "Within the palace disaster is likely imminent.
translations.idiomatic: Jishu went to see Yin and said, "Something terrible may have happened in the palace.

sentences.zh: 與仲先率王彥範、薛齊偓、李師虔、徐彥回總衛士千人毀關入，謀所立，未決。

translations.literal: With Zhongxian he led Wang Yanfan, Xue Qiwo, Li Shiqian, and Xu Yanhui, mustered a thousand guardsmen, broke through the gate and entered; they deliberated whom to install but had not decided.
translations.idiomatic: He and Zhongxian then led Wang Yanfan, Xue Qiwo, Li Shiqian, and Xu Yanhui, gathered a thousand guardsmen, broke through the gate, and entered. They debated whom to install as ruler but could not settle on a choice.

sentences.zh: 是夜，宮監竊取太子以入，季述等因矯皇后令曰：「車讓、謝筠勸上殺人，禳塞災咎，皆大不道。

translations.literal: That night a palace intendant secretly fetched the crown prince and brought him in; Jishu and the others thereupon forged an order from the empress: "Che Rang and Xie Yun urged the sovereign to kill people to avert and block calamities — all grossly unfilial and rebellious conduct.
translations.idiomatic: That night a palace intendant secretly brought in the crown prince. Jishu and his allies then forged an order from the empress: "Che Rang and Xie Yun urged the sovereign to kill people to avert disaster — all grossly unfilial and rebellious conduct.

sentences.zh: 兩軍軍容知之，今立皇太子，以主社稷。」

translations.literal: The army supervision commissioners of both armies know of this; we now establish the crown prince to preside over the altars of state.
translations.idiomatic: The army supervision commissioners of both armies are aware of this. We now install the crown prince to preside over the altars of state.

sentences.zh: 黎明，陳兵廷中，謂宰相曰：「上所為如此，非社稷主，今當以太子見群臣。」

translations.literal: At dawn they deployed troops in the court and said to the chief ministers, "The sovereign's conduct is like this — he is no lord of the altars of state; we should now present the crown prince to the officials."
translations.idiomatic: At dawn they arrayed troops in the court and told the chief ministers, "The sovereign's conduct is unworthy of one who holds the altars of state. We must now present the crown prince to the officials."

sentences.zh: 即召百官署奏，胤不得對。

translations.literal: They immediately summoned all officials to affix their names to a memorial; Yin could not respond.
translations.idiomatic: They immediately summoned all officials to sign a memorial. Yin could offer no reply.

sentences.zh: 季述衛皇太子至紫廷院，左右軍及十道邸官俞潭、程巖等詣思玄門請對，士皆呼萬歲。

translations.literal: Jishu escorted the crown prince to Ziting Courtyard; the left and right armies and the ten-circuit lodging officials Yu Tan, Cheng Yan, and others went to Sixuan Gate to request audience; the soldiers all shouted "Ten thousand years!"
translations.idiomatic: Jishu escorted the crown prince to Ziting Courtyard. The left and right armies and the lodging officials of the ten circuits, including Yu Tan and Cheng Yan, went to Sixuan Gate to request an audience, and the soldiers all shouted "Long live the sovereign!"

sentences.zh: 入思政殿，遇者輒殺。

translations.literal: Entering Sizheng Hall, they killed whomever they met.
translations.idiomatic: They entered Sizheng Hall and killed everyone they encountered.

sentences.zh: 帝方坐乞巧樓，見兵入，驚墮於床，將走，季述、仲先持帝坐，以所持釦杖畫地責帝曰：「某日某事爾不從我，罪一也。」

translations.literal: The emperor was just sitting in the Qiqiao Tower; seeing troops enter he startled and fell from his couch; as he was about to flee, Jishu and Zhongxian seized him and forced him to sit; with the clasp-staffs they held they scratched on the ground and rebuked the emperor: "On such-and-such a day, in such-and-such a matter you did not obey me — that is crime one.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor was sitting in the Qiqiao Tower when he saw troops enter. Startled, he fell from his couch and tried to flee. Jishu and Zhongxian seized him and forced him to sit. Scratching on the ground with their clasp-staffs, they rebuked him: "On such-and-such a day, in such-and-such a matter you did not obey me — that is your first offense.

sentences.zh: 至數十未止。

translations.literal: They reached several dozen and still did not stop.
translations.idiomatic: They listed dozens of offenses and still did not stop.

sentences.zh: 皇后出，遍拜曰：「護宅家，勿使怖，若有罪，惟軍容議。」

translations.literal: The empress came out and bowed all around, saying, "Protect the householder; do not frighten him; if there is guilt, let the Army Supervision Commissioner decide.
translations.idiomatic: The empress came out and bowed to them all, saying, "Protect the householder. Do not frighten him. If there is guilt, let the Army Supervision Commissioner decide.

sentences.zh: 季述出百官奏，曰：「陛下瞀，倦於勤，願奉太子監國，陛下自頤東宮。」

translations.literal: Jishu produced the officials' memorial and said, "Your Majesty is dim-sighted and weary of diligence; we wish to install the crown prince as regent; Your Majesty should retire to the Eastern Palace to recuperate."
translations.idiomatic: Jishu produced the officials' memorial and said, "Your Majesty's sight is failing and you are weary of governing. We wish to install the crown prince as regent. Your Majesty should retire to the Eastern Palace to convalesce."

sentences.zh: 帝曰：「昨與而等飲甚樂，何至是？」

translations.literal: The emperor said, "Yesterday I drank with you all in great pleasure — how did it come to this?"
translations.idiomatic: The emperor said, "Yesterday I drank with you in great pleasure. How did it come to this?"

sentences.zh: 後曰：「陛下如軍容語。」

translations.literal: The empress said, "Your Majesty should do as the Army Supervision Commissioner says."
translations.idiomatic: The empress said, "Your Majesty should do as the Army Supervision Commissioner says."

sentences.zh: 宮監掖帝出思政殿，後倡言曰：「軍容一心輔持，請上養疾。」

translations.literal: A palace intendant helped the emperor out of Sizheng Hall; the empress proclaimed, "The Army Supervision Commissioner devotes himself wholeheartedly to supporting Your Majesty — we beg the sovereign to convalesce."
translations.idiomatic: A palace intendant helped the emperor out of Sizheng Hall. The empress proclaimed, "The Army Supervision Commissioner is wholly devoted to supporting Your Majesty. We beg the sovereign to convalesce."

sentences.zh: 帝亦曰：「朕久疾，令太子監國。」

translations.literal: The emperor also said, "I have long been ill; let the crown prince govern as regent."
translations.idiomatic: The emperor also said, "I have long been ill. Let the crown prince govern as regent."

sentences.zh: 巖等皆呼萬歲。

translations.literal: Yan and the others all shouted "Ten thousand years!"
translations.idiomatic: Cheng Yan and the others all shouted "Long live the sovereign!"

sentences.zh: 後以傳國寶授季述，就帝輦，左右十餘人，入囚少陽院。

translations.literal: The empress handed the imperial succession seal to Jishu; they placed the emperor in his carriage with a dozen or so attendants and imprisoned him in Shaoyang Courtyard.
translations.idiomatic: The empress handed the imperial succession seal to Jishu. They placed the emperor in his carriage with a dozen attendants and imprisoned him in Shaoyang Courtyard.

sentences.zh: 季述液金以完鐍，師虔以兵守。

translations.literal: Jishu poured molten metal to complete the lock; Shiqian guarded with troops.
translations.idiomatic: Jishu poured molten metal to seal the lock shut, and Shiqian guarded the courtyard with troops.

sentences.zh: 太子即位於武德殿，帝號太上皇，皇后為太上皇后，大赦天下，東宮官屬三品賜爵一級，四品以下一階，天下為父後者爵一級，群臣加爵秩厚賜，欲媚附上下。

translations.literal: The crown prince ascended the throne at Wude Hall; the emperor was styled Retired Emperor, the empress Retired Empress; a general amnesty was proclaimed; Eastern Palace officials of third rank received one grade of nobility, those of fourth rank and below one step; all who were heirs to their fathers throughout the realm received one grade of nobility; all officials were given added ranks and generous gifts — intending to win over court and capital alike.
translations.idiomatic: The crown prince ascended the throne at Wude Hall. The emperor was styled Retired Emperor and the empress Retired Empress. A general amnesty was proclaimed. Eastern Palace officials of third rank received one grade of nobility, those of fourth rank and below one step, and heirs throughout the realm one grade of nobility. Officials were given added ranks and lavish gifts, all to win over court and capital.

sentences.zh: 改東宮為問安宮。

translations.literal: The Eastern Palace was renamed the Inquiring-after-Health Palace.
translations.idiomatic: The Eastern Palace was renamed the Palace of Inquiring after Health.

sentences.zh: 季述等皆先誅戮以立威，夜鞭笞，晝出屍十輦，凡有寵於帝，悉榜殺之。

translations.literal: Jishu and the others first executed people to establish their authority; they flogged by night, and by day ten carts of corpses were brought out; all who had enjoyed the emperor's favor were posted for execution and killed.
translations.idiomatic: Jishu and his allies first executed people to establish their authority. They flogged victims by night, and by day ten carts of corpses were brought out. Everyone who had enjoyed the emperor's favor was posted for execution and killed.

sentences.zh: 殺帝弟睦王。

translations.literal: They killed the emperor's younger brother, the Prince of Mu.
translations.idiomatic: They killed the emperor's younger brother, the Prince of Mu.

sentences.zh: 師虔尤苛察，左右出入搜索，天子動靜輒白季述。

translations.literal: Shiqian was especially harsh and scrutinizing; those who entered and left were searched; the Son of Heaven's every movement was reported to Jishu.
translations.idiomatic: Shiqian was especially harsh and suspicious. Everyone who entered or left was searched, and the emperor's every movement was reported to Jishu.

sentences.zh: 帝衣晝服夜浣，食自竇進，下至筆紙銅鐵，疑作詔書兵器，皆不與。

translations.literal: The emperor wore his robes by day and washed them at night; food was brought in through a hole; down to brush, paper, copper, and iron — anything suspected of being used to draft edicts or make weapons was withheld.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor wore his robes by day and washed them at night. Food was passed in through a hole in the wall. Brush, paper, copper, iron — anything that might be used to draft edicts or fashion weapons — was withheld.

sentences.zh: 方寒，公主嬪御無衾纊，哀聞外廷。

translations.literal: It was cold; princesses and consorts had no quilts or cotton — their wailing could be heard in the outer court.
translations.idiomatic: It was cold, and the princesses and consorts had no quilts or cotton padding. Their wailing could be heard in the outer court.

sentences.zh: 胤告難於朱全忠，使以兵除君側，全忠封胤書與季述曰：「彼翻覆，宜圖之。」

translations.literal: Yin reported the crisis to Zhu Quanzhong and asked him to use troops to remove those at the sovereign's side; Quanzhong enclosed Yin's letter and sent it to Jishu, saying, "He is treacherous — you should deal with him.
translations.idiomatic: Yin reported the crisis to Zhu Quanzhong and asked him to use troops to remove the emperor's captors. Quanzhong enclosed Yin's letter and sent it to Jishu, saying, "He is treacherous — you should deal with him.

sentences.zh: 季述以責胤，胤曰：「奸人偽書，從古有之，必以為罪，請誅不及族。」

translations.literal: Jishu confronted Yin with this; Yin said, "Forgeries by villains have existed since antiquity; if you must treat this as a crime, I beg that execution not extend to my clan."
translations.idiomatic: Jishu confronted Yin with the letter. Yin said, "Forged letters by schemers are nothing new. If you must treat this as a crime, I beg that execution not extend to my clan."

sentences.zh: 季述易之，乃與盟。

translations.literal: Jishu accepted this and they entered an alliance.
translations.idiomatic: Jishu accepted this explanation, and they entered an alliance.

sentences.zh: 胤謝全忠曰：「左軍與胤盟，不相害，然仆歸心於公，並送二侍兒。」

translations.literal: Yin thanked Quanzhong: "The Left Army has allied with me and we shall not harm each other; yet this servant's heart belongs to you," and sent along two maidservants.
translations.idiomatic: Yin wrote to thank Quanzhong: "The Left Army has allied with me, and we shall not harm each other. Yet my heart belongs to you." He sent along two maidservants.

sentences.zh: 全忠得書，恚曰：「季述使我為兩面人。」

translations.literal: Quanzhong received the letter and angrily said, "Jishu has made me into a double-dealer."
translations.idiomatic: Quanzhong received the letter and said in anger, "Jishu has made me into a double-dealer."

sentences.zh: 自是始離。

translations.literal: From this they began to part ways.
translations.idiomatic: From that point they began to part ways.

sentences.zh: 季述子希度至汴，言廢立本計，又遣李奉本賫示太上皇誥，全忠狐疑不決。

translations.literal: Jishu's son Xidu went to Bian, spoke of the original plan for deposition and installation, and also sent Li Fengben to present the Retired Emperor's edict; Quanzhong wavered, unable to decide.
translations.idiomatic: Jishu's son Xidu went to Bian and explained the original plan for deposing and installing emperors. He also sent Li Fengben to present the Retired Emperor's edict. Quanzhong wavered, unable to decide.

sentences.zh: 李振入見曰：「豎刁、伊戾之亂，以資霸者。

translations.literal: Li Zhen entered to see him and said, "The disorders of Shu Diao and Yi Li furnished resources for those who would become hegemons.
translations.idiomatic: Li Zhen came in to see him and said, "The disorders of Shu Diao and Yi Li furnished resources for those who would become hegemons.

sentences.zh: 今閹奴幽劫天子，公不討，無以令諸侯。」

translations.literal: Now these castrated slaves have secretly seized and coerced the Son of Heaven; if you do not punish them, you cannot command the feudal lords.
translations.idiomatic: Now these castrated slaves have secretly seized the Son of Heaven. If you do not punish them, you cannot command the feudal lords.

sentences.zh: 乃囚希度、奉本，遣振至京師與胤謀。

translations.literal: He thereupon imprisoned Xidu and Fengben and sent Zhen to the capital to plot with Yin.
translations.idiomatic: He thereupon imprisoned Xidu and Fengben and sent Li Zhen to the capital to plot with Yin.

sentences.zh: 是時季述欲盡誅百官，乃弒帝，挾太子令天下。

translations.literal: At this time Jishu intended to execute all the officials, then assassinate the emperor and hold the crown prince hostage to command the realm.
translations.idiomatic: At this time Jishu intended to execute all the officials, then assassinate the emperor and hold the crown prince hostage to command the realm.

sentences.zh: 都將孫德昭、董從實盜沒錢五千緡，仲先眾辱之，督其償，株連甚眾。

translations.literal: Commanders Sun Dezhao and Dong Congshi embezzled five thousand strings of cash; Zhongxian publicly humiliated them and forced repayment, implicating many others.
translations.idiomatic: Commanders Sun Dezhao and Dong Congshi embezzled five thousand strings of cash. Zhongxian publicly humiliated them and forced repayment, implicating many others in the process.

sentences.zh: 胤間其不逞，曰：「能殺兩中尉，迎太上皇，而立大功，何小罪足羞！」

translations.literal: Yin sensed their discontent and said, "If you can kill the two army commissioners, welcome back the Retired Emperor, and thereby win great merit — what shame is there in petty crimes!
translations.idiomatic: Yin sensed their discontent and said, "If you can kill the two army commissioners, welcome back the Retired Emperor, and thereby win great merit — what shame is there in petty crimes!

sentences.zh: 又遣客密告德昭，割帶內蜜丸通意。

translations.literal: He also sent a guest to secretly inform Dezhao, cutting open a belt and placing inside a honey pill to convey his intent.
translations.idiomatic: He also sent an agent to secretly inform Dezhao, cutting open a belt and placing a honey pill inside to convey his intent.

sentences.zh: 德昭邀別將周承誨，期十二月晦，伏士安福門待旦。

translations.literal: Dezhao invited fellow commander Zhou Chenghui; they set the last day of the twelfth month, stationed men at Anfu Gate to wait for dawn.
translations.idiomatic: Dezhao invited fellow commander Zhou Chenghui. They set the last day of the twelfth month and stationed men at Anfu Gate to wait for dawn.

sentences.zh: 仲先乘肩輿造朝，德昭等劫之，斬東宮門外，叩少陽院呼曰：「逆賊斬矣。」

translations.literal: Zhongxian rode in a sedan chair to court; Dezhao and the others intercepted him and beheaded him outside the Eastern Palace gate; they knocked on Shaoyang Courtyard and shouted, "The rebels have been beheaded!
translations.idiomatic: Zhongxian rode in a sedan chair to court. Dezhao and his men intercepted him and beheaded him outside the Eastern Palace gate. They knocked on Shaoyang Courtyard and shouted, "The rebels have been beheaded!

sentences.zh: 帝疑未信，皇后曰：「可獻賊首。」

translations.literal: The emperor doubted and did not believe; the empress said, "You may present the rebels' heads."
translations.idiomatic: The emperor doubted and did not believe. The empress said, "Present the rebels' heads."

sentences.zh: 德昭擲仲先頭以進，宮人毀扉，出御長樂門，群臣稱賀。

translations.literal: Dezhao threw Zhongxian's head forward; palace women smashed the door; they came out and took position at Changle Gate; officials offered congratulations.
translations.idiomatic: Dezhao threw Zhongxian's head forward. Palace women smashed the door. The emperor and empress came out and took position at Changle Gate, and officials offered congratulations.

sentences.zh: 承誨馳入左軍，執季述、彥範至樓前，胤先戒京兆尹鄭元規集萬人持大梃，帝詰季述未已，萬梃皆進，二人同死梃下，遂屍之。

translations.literal: Chenghui raced into the Left Army, seized Jishu and Yanfan and brought them before the tower; Yin had earlier warned Capital Prefect Zheng Yuangui to gather ten thousand men with large clubs; the emperor had not finished interrogating Jishu when ten thousand clubs advanced — both died under the clubs and their corpses were displayed.
translations.idiomatic: Chenghui raced into the Left Army, seized Jishu and Yanfan, and brought them before the tower. Yin had earlier instructed Capital Prefect Zheng Yuangui to gather ten thousand men with large clubs. The emperor had not finished interrogating Jishu when ten thousand clubs advanced. Both died under the clubs, and their corpses were displayed.

sentences.zh: 兩軍支黨死者數十人。

translations.literal: Several dozen partisans of the two armies died.
translations.idiomatic: Several dozen partisans of the two armies were killed.

sentences.zh: 中官奉太子遁入左軍，收傳國璽。

translations.literal: Eunuchs escorted the crown prince, who fled into the Left Army; they recovered the imperial succession seal.
translations.idiomatic: Eunuchs escorted the crown prince as he fled into the Left Army, and they recovered the imperial succession seal.

sentences.zh: 齊偓死井中，出其屍斬之。

translations.literal: Qiwo died in a well; they pulled out his corpse and beheaded it.
translations.idiomatic: Qiwo died in a well. They pulled out his corpse and beheaded it.

sentences.zh: 全忠檻送巖京師，斬於市。

translations.literal: Quanzhong sent Yan to the capital in a cage-cart and had him executed in the marketplace.
translations.idiomatic: Quanzhong sent Cheng Yan to the capital in a cage-cart and had him executed in the marketplace.

sentences.zh: 季述等夷三族。

translations.literal: Jishu and the others — their clans were exterminated to the third degree.
translations.idiomatic: The clans of Jishu and his allies were exterminated to the third degree.

sentences.zh: 以德昭檢校太保、靜海軍節度使，從實檢校司徒、容管節度使，並同中書門下平章事，賜氏李，曰繼昭，曰彥弼。

translations.literal: Dezhao was made Acting Grand Preceptor and military commissioner of Jinghai; Congshi Acting Minister of Education and military commissioner of Rongguan; both Grand Councilors; they were granted the surname Li — called Jizhao and Yanbi.
translations.idiomatic: Dezhao was made Acting Grand Preceptor and military commissioner of Jinghai; Congshi Acting Minister of Education and military commissioner of Rongguan. Both were appointed Grand Councilors and granted the surname Li — Dezhao taking the name Jizhao and Congshi the name Yanbi.

sentences.zh: 承誨亦檢校司徒、邕管節度使，視宰相秩。

translations.literal: Chenghui was also Acting Minister of Education and military commissioner of Yongguan, with ranks equivalent to a chief minister.
translations.idiomatic: Chenghui was also made Acting Minister of Education and military commissioner of Yongguan, with rank equivalent to a chief minister.

sentences.zh: 皆號「扶傾濟難忠烈功臣」，圖形淩煙閣，留宿衛凡十日乃休，竭內庫珍寶賜之。

translations.literal: All were styled "Meritorious Loyal Heroes Who Right the Tilted and Rescue from Peril"; their portraits were placed in Lingyan Pavilion; they remained on palace guard duty for ten days before being released; the inner treasury's treasures were exhausted in rewarding them.
translations.idiomatic: All were styled "Meritorious Loyal Heroes Who Right the Tilted and Rescue from Peril." Their portraits were placed in Lingyan Pavilion. They remained on palace guard duty for ten days before being released, and the inner treasury's treasures were exhausted in rewarding them.

sentences.zh: 當時號「三使相」，人臣無比。

translations.literal: At the time they were called "the three commissioner-ministers" — no subject had ever been their equal.
translations.idiomatic: At the time they were called "the three commissioner-ministers" — no subject had ever been their equal.

sentences.zh: 初，延英宰相奏事，帝平可否，樞密使立侍，得與聞，及出，或矯上旨謂未然，數改易橈權。

translations.literal: Initially, when chief ministers reported affairs at Yanying Hall, the emperor settled yes or no; the privy councilors stood in attendance and could hear; after leaving, they sometimes forged the sovereign's intent, saying matters were not yet decided, and repeatedly altered and usurped authority.
translations.idiomatic: Initially, when chief ministers reported affairs at Yanying Hall, the emperor decided yes or no while privy councilors stood in attendance and could hear. After leaving, they sometimes forged the sovereign's intent, claiming matters were not yet settled, and repeatedly altered decisions and usurped authority.

sentences.zh: 至是，詔如大中故事，對延英，兩中尉先降，樞密使候旨殿西，宰相奏事已畢，案前受事。

translations.literal: At this time an edict followed the Da Zhong precedent: at Yanying audiences the two army commissioners descended first; privy councilors waited for instructions west of the hall; once the chief ministers had finished reporting, they received their business before the desk.
translations.idiomatic: At this time an edict restored the Da Zhong precedent: at Yanying audiences the two army commissioners withdrew first; privy councilors waited for instructions west of the hall; and once the chief ministers had finished reporting, they received their business at the desk.

sentences.zh: 師虔請於屏風後錄宰相所奏，帝以侵官，不許，下詔與徐彥回同誅。

translations.literal: Shiqian requested to record behind the screen what the chief ministers reported; the emperor took this as encroaching on office and refused; an edict ordered him executed together with Xu Yanhui.
translations.idiomatic: Shiqian requested to record behind the screen what the chief ministers reported. The emperor took this as encroaching on official duties and refused. An edict ordered Shiqian executed together with Xu Yanhui.

sentences.zh: 韓全誨、張彥弘韓全誨、張彥弘者，皆不知所來，並監鳳翔軍。

translations.literal: Han Quanhui and Zhang Yanhong — Han Quanhui and Zhang Yanhong, neither of known origin, both supervised the Fengxiang army.
translations.idiomatic: Han Quanhui and Zhang Yanhong — Han Quanhui and Zhang Yanhong, men of unknown origin, both supervised the Fengxiang army.

sentences.zh: 全誨入為內樞密使。

translations.literal: Quanhui entered service as Inner Privy Councilor.
translations.idiomatic: Quanhui entered the capital as Inner Privy Councilor.

sentences.zh: 劉季述之誅，崔胤、陸扆見武德殿右廡，胤曰：「自中人典兵，王室愈亂，臣請主神策左軍，以扆主右，則四方藩臣不敢謀。」

translations.literal: After Liu Jishu was executed, Cui Yin and Lu Yi met in the right wing of Wude Hall; Yin said, "Since eunuchs have commanded armies the royal house has grown ever more chaotic; your servant requests to command the Left Shence Army, with Yi commanding the Right — then feudal lords in all directions will not dare to plot.
translations.idiomatic: After Liu Jishu was executed, Cui Yin and Lu Yi met in the right wing of Wude Hall. Yin said, "Since eunuchs have commanded armies, the royal house has grown ever more chaotic. I request to command the Left Shence Army, with Yi commanding the Right. Then the military commissioners in all directions will not dare to plot.

sentences.zh: 昭宗意不決。

translations.literal: Zhaozong's mind was unsettled.
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Zhaozong's mind was unsettled.

sentences.zh: 李茂貞語人曰：「崔胤奪軍權未及手，志滅藩鎮矣。」

translations.literal: Li Maozhen told someone, "Cui Yin has not yet taken military power into his hands and already intends to destroy the military commissioners.
translations.idiomatic: Li Maozhen told someone, "Cui Yin has not yet taken military power into his hands and already intends to destroy the military commissioners.

sentences.zh: 帝聞，召李繼昭等問以胤所請奈何，對曰：「臣世世在軍，不聞書生主衛兵。

translations.literal: The emperor heard this and summoned Li Jizhao and others to ask what they thought of Yin's request; they replied, "We, generation after generation, have been in the armies — never have we heard of a scholar commanding palace guards.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor heard this and summoned Li Jizhao and the others to ask what they thought of Yin's request. They replied, "We have served in the armies generation after generation — never have we heard of a scholar commanding palace guards.

sentences.zh: 且罪人已得，持軍還北司便。」

translations.literal: Besides, the guilty ones have been obtained — let them take their armies back to the Northern Office and that will suffice."
translations.idiomatic: Besides, the guilty ones have been dealt with. Let them take their armies back to the Northern Office and that will suffice."

sentences.zh: 帝謂胤曰：「議者不同，勿庸主軍。」

translations.literal: The emperor said to Yin, "Those who deliberated differ — you need not command armies."
translations.idiomatic: The emperor said to Yin, "Those who deliberated disagree. You need not command the armies."

sentences.zh: 乃以全誨為左神策中尉，彥弘為右，皆拜驃騎大將軍，袁易簡、周敬容為樞密使。

translations.literal: Thereupon Quanhui was made Left Shence Army Commissioner and Yanhong Right; both were appointed Cavalry General-in-Chief; Yuan Yijian and Zhou Jingrong were made privy councilors.
translations.idiomatic: Quanhui was then made Left Shence Army Commissioner and Yanhong Right Shence Army Commissioner. Both were appointed Cavalry General-in-Chief. Yuan Yijian and Zhou Jingrong were made privy councilors.

sentences.zh: 胤怒，約京兆鄭元規遣人狙殺之，不克。

translations.literal: Yin in anger arranged with Capital Prefect Zheng Yuangui to send men to assassinate them — it did not succeed.
translations.idiomatic: Yin in anger arranged with Capital Prefect Zheng Yuangui to send men to assassinate them, but the attempt failed.

sentences.zh: 全誨等知胤必除己乃已，因諷茂貞留選士四千宿衛，以李繼筠、繼徽總之。

translations.literal: Quanhui and the others knew Yin would not stop until he had eliminated them; they therefore prompted Maozhen to leave four thousand selected troops as palace guards, under Li Jijun and Jihui.
translations.idiomatic: Quanhui and the others knew Yin would not stop until he had eliminated them. They therefore prompted Maozhen to leave four thousand selected troops as palace guards under Li Jijun and Jihui.

sentences.zh: 胤亦諷朱全忠內兵三千居南司，以婁敬思領之。

translations.literal: Yin also prompted Zhu Quanzhong to station three thousand inner troops in the Southern Office, under Lou Jingsi.
translations.idiomatic: Yin also prompted Zhu Quanzhong to station three thousand inner troops in the Southern Office under Lou Jingsi.

sentences.zh: 韓偓聞岐、汴交戍，數諫止胤，胤曰：「兵不肯去耳。」

translations.literal: Han Wo heard that Qi and Bian troops were stationed in turn and repeatedly remonstrated with Yin to stop; Yin said, "The troops simply refuse to leave.
translations.idiomatic: Han Wo heard that Fengxiang and Bian troops were stationed in turn in the capital and repeatedly remonstrated with Yin to stop. Yin said, "The troops simply refuse to leave.

sentences.zh: 偓曰：「初何為召邪？」

translations.literal: Wo said, "Then why summon them in the first place?"
translations.idiomatic: Wo said, "Then why summon them in the first place?"

sentences.zh: 胤不對。

translations.literal: Yin did not answer.
translations.idiomatic: Yin did not answer.

sentences.zh: 議者知京師不復安矣。

translations.literal: Those who deliberated knew the capital would no longer be secure.
translations.idiomatic: Those who deliberated knew the capital would no longer be secure.

sentences.zh: 全誨、彥弘及彥弼合勢恣暴，中官倚以自驕，帝不平，有斥逐者，皆不肯行，胤固請盡誅之。

translations.literal: Quanhui, Yanhong, and Yanbi combined their power and indulged in violence; eunuchs relied on them and grew arrogant; the emperor was displeased; some who were dismissed and expelled refused to go; Yin steadfastly requested that they all be executed.
translations.idiomatic: Quanhui, Yanhong, and Yanbi combined their power and indulged in violence. Eunuchs relied on them and grew arrogant. The emperor was displeased, but those he dismissed and expelled refused to go. Yin steadfastly requested that they all be executed.

sentences.zh: 全誨、彥弘見帝祈哀，帝知左右漏言，始詔囊封奏事。

translations.literal: Quanhui and Yanhong saw the emperor and pleaded; the emperor knew those around him had leaked his words; he then ordered memorials submitted in sealed pouches.
translations.idiomatic: Quanhui and Yanhong saw the emperor and pleaded for mercy. The emperor knew those around him had leaked his words and then ordered that memorials be submitted in sealed pouches.

sentences.zh: 宦人更求麗姝知書者數十人，侍帝為內诇，由是胤計多露。

translations.literal: Eunuchs further sought several dozen beautiful and literate women to attend the emperor as internal spies; thereby many of Yin's plans were exposed.
translations.idiomatic: Eunuchs further sought several dozen beautiful, literate women to attend the emperor as internal spies. Many of Yin's plans were thereby exposed.

sentences.zh: 始，張浚判度支，楊復恭以軍貲乏，奏假鹽曲一歲入以濟用度，遂不復還。

translations.literal: Initially Zhang Jun had charge of the Directorate of Public Works; Yang Fugong, finding military funds insufficient, memorialized to borrow one year's salt and brewing revenues to meet expenses — they were never returned.
translations.idiomatic: Initially Zhang Jun had charge of the Directorate of Public Works. Yang Fugong, finding military funds insufficient, memorialized to borrow one year's salt and brewing revenues to meet expenses — and they were never returned.

sentences.zh: 至胤，乃白度支財盡，無以稟百官，請如舊制。

translations.literal: When Yin took over, he reported that the Directorate's funds were exhausted and there were no means to supply the officials; he requested a return to the former system.
translations.idiomatic: When Yin took over, he reported that the Directorate's funds were exhausted and there were no means to supply the officials. He requested a return to the former system.

sentences.zh: 全誨擿李繼筠訴軍中匱甚，請割三司隸神策。

translations.literal: Quanhui prompted Li Jijun to complain that the army was greatly depleted and requested that the Three Offices be carved out and placed under the Shence Army.
translations.idiomatic: Quanhui prompted Li Jijun to complain that the army was greatly depleted and requested that the Three Offices be carved out and placed under the Shence Army.

sentences.zh: 帝不能卻，詔罷胤領鹽鐵，胤銜之。

translations.literal: The emperor could not refuse; an edict removed Yin from charge of salt and iron; Yin harbored resentment.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor could not refuse. An edict removed Yin from charge of salt and iron, and Yin harbored resentment.

sentences.zh: 全誨等懼帝誅己，與繼誨、彥弼、繼筠交通謀亂。

translations.literal: Quanhui and the others feared the emperor would execute them; they colluded with Jihui, Yanbi, and Jijun to plot disorder.
translations.idiomatic: Quanhui and the others feared the emperor would execute them. They colluded with Jihui, Yanbi, and Jijun to plot disorder.

sentences.zh: 帝問令狐渙，渙請召胤及全誨等宴內殿和解之。

translations.literal: The emperor asked Linghu Huan; Huan requested summoning Yin and Quanhui and the others to a banquet in the inner palace to reconcile.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor asked Linghu Huan. Huan suggested summoning Yin, Quanhui, and the others to a banquet in the inner palace to reconcile.

sentences.zh: 韓偓謂：「不如顯斥一二柄臣，許餘人自新，妄謀必息。

translations.literal: Han Wo said, "Better openly to dismiss one or two power-holders and permit the rest to reform — reckless plotting will surely cease.
translations.idiomatic: Han Wo said, "Better to openly dismiss one or two power-holders and permit the rest to reform. Reckless plotting will surely cease.

sentences.zh: 不然皆自疑，禍且速，雖和解之，凶焰益肆。」

translations.literal: Otherwise everyone will suspect one another, disaster will come quickly; even if you reconcile, their vicious boldness will only grow.
translations.idiomatic: Otherwise everyone will suspect one another and disaster will come quickly. Even if you reconcile, their vicious boldness will only grow.

sentences.zh: 帝乃止。

translations.literal: The emperor then desisted.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor then dropped the matter.

sentences.zh: 是時全忠並河中，胤為急詔令入朝，又詒書曰：「上反正，公之力，而鳳翔入朝，引功自歸。

translations.literal: At this time Quanzhong had also taken Hezhong; Yin issued an urgent edict summoning him to court and also wrote, "The sovereign was restored — that was your doing; yet Fengxiang entered court and claimed the credit for himself.
translations.idiomatic: At this time Quanzhong had also taken Hezhong. Yin issued an urgent edict summoning him to court and also wrote, "The sovereign was restored through your efforts, yet Fengxiang entered court and claimed the credit for himself.

sentences.zh: 今若後至，必先見討。」

translations.literal: If you arrive later now, you will be punished first.
translations.idiomatic: If you arrive later now, you will be punished first.

sentences.zh: 全忠得詔，還汴，悉師討全誨。

translations.literal: Quanzhong received the edict, returned to Bian, and marched with all his forces to attack Quanhui.
translations.idiomatic: Quanzhong received the edict, returned to Bian, and marched with all his forces to attack Quanhui.

sentences.zh: 帝以為忠，又欲其與茂貞同功，即詔並力。

translations.literal: The emperor believed him loyal and also wished him to share the achievement with Maozhen; he immediately ordered them to join forces.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor believed him loyal and also wished him to share the achievement with Maozhen. He immediately ordered them to join forces.

sentences.zh: 令胤詒二鎮書，示帝意。

translations.literal: Yin was ordered to send deceptive letters to the two prefectures, conveying the emperor's intent.
translations.idiomatic: Yin was ordered to send deceptive letters to the two prefectures, conveying the emperor's intent.

sentences.zh: 全忠取同州，汴兵凡七萬，威震關中。

translations.literal: Quanzhong took Tongzhou; Bian troops totaled seventy thousand, their might shaking Guanzhong.
translations.idiomatic: Quanzhong took Tongzhou. Bian troops totaled seventy thousand, and their might shook Guanzhong.

sentences.zh: 全誨等泣奏曰：「全忠且至，欲脅陛下幸關東，將謀傳禪。

translations.literal: Quanhui and the others tearfully memorialized, saying, "Quanzhong is about to arrive and wishes to coerce Your Majesty into going east to the pass lands, intending to plot the transfer of the Mandate.
translations.idiomatic: Quanhui and the others tearfully memorialized, saying, "Quanzhong is about to arrive. He wishes to coerce Your Majesty into going east to the pass lands and intends to plot the transfer of the Mandate.

sentences.zh: 臣不忍見高祖天下移他姓，願至鳳翔，合義兵討元惡。」

translations.literal: Your servants cannot bear to see the empire of High Ancestor pass to another surname. We wish to go to Fengxiang and gather righteous troops to punish the arch-villain.
translations.idiomatic: Your servants cannot bear to see the empire of High Ancestor pass to another surname. We wish to go to Fengxiang and gather righteous troops to punish the arch-villain.

sentences.zh: 帝未許，方在乞巧樓，全誨急，即火其下，帝降樓，乃決西幸。

translations.literal: The emperor did not consent. He was then in the Begging-for-Skill Tower; Quanhui, in haste, set fire beneath it. The emperor descended the tower, and only then resolved to go west on a progress.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor did not consent. He was then in the Begging-for-Skill Tower. Quanhui, in haste, set fire beneath it. The emperor descended the tower and only then resolved to go west on a progress.

sentences.zh: 彥弼等以帝未即駕，愈誖，宮中禁索苛亟，帝與後相視泣，宮人私逃出都，民崩沸，或奔開化坊依胤第自固，闬無留家。

translations.literal: Yanbi and the others, because the emperor did not immediately depart, grew all the more defiant. Within the palace searches were harsh and pressing. The emperor and the empress looked at each other and wept. Palace women secretly fled the capital. The people were in uproar; some ran to Kaifahua Ward to take refuge at Yin's residence for safety; no household kept its doors closed.
translations.idiomatic: Yanbi and the others, because the emperor did not immediately depart, grew all the more defiant. Within the palace, searches were harsh and pressing. The emperor and the empress looked at each other and wept. Palace women secretly fled the capital. The people were in uproar; some ran to Kaifahua Ward to take refuge at Yin's residence, and no household kept its doors closed.

sentences.zh: 鳳翔軍與左神策兵陣大衢，長樂門外若丘墟然。

translations.literal: Fengxiang troops and the Left Shence Army lined the great thoroughfare; outside Changle Gate it was as though a desolate ruin.
translations.idiomatic: Fengxiang troops and the Left Shence Army lined the great thoroughfare. Outside Changle Gate it was as desolate as a ruined mound.

sentences.zh: 於是日南至，百官不朝，帝坐思政殿。

translations.literal: Then came the winter solstice; the hundred officials did not attend court. The emperor sat in the Hall of Governance through Reflection.
