translations.idiomatic: Then came the winter solstice. The hundred officials did not attend court, and the emperor sat in the Hall of Governance through Reflection.

sentences.zh: 時彥弼先入鳳翔，全誨逼帝出，惟皇后、諸王數百騎為衛，帝繡袍、塗金帽，以右神策軍從，實天復元年十一月壬子。

translations.literal: At that time Yanbi had already entered Fengxiang ahead of them. Quanhui pressed the emperor to depart. Only the empress and several hundred mounted guards of the princes attended him. The emperor wore an embroidered robe and a gilt-coated cap, with the Right Shence Army following. It was in truth the renchen day of the eleventh month of the first year of Tianfu.
translations.idiomatic: At that time Yanbi had already entered Fengxiang ahead of them. Quanhui pressed the emperor to depart. Only the empress and several hundred mounted princes' guards attended him. The emperor wore an embroidered robe and a gilt-coated cap, with the Right Shence Army following. It was in truth the renchen day of the eleventh month of the first year of Tianfu.

sentences.zh: 全誨等遂火宮城，繼誨、彥弼欲劫百官從天子，李德昭等按兵衛之，乃得免。

translations.literal: Quanhui and the others then set fire to the palace city. Jihui and Yanbi wished to seize the hundred officials and force them to follow the Son of Heaven. Li Dezhao and others held their troops in check to guard them, and they were thus spared.
translations.idiomatic: Quanhui and the others then set fire to the palace city. Jihui and Yanbi wished to seize the hundred officials and force them to follow the Son of Heaven. Li Dezhao and others held their troops in check to guard them, and the officials were thus spared.

sentences.zh: 茂貞以帝居盩厔。

translations.literal: Maozhen lodged the emperor at Zhouzhi.
translations.idiomatic: Maozhen lodged the emperor at Zhouzhi.

sentences.zh: 全忠取華州，下令自釋曰：「吾被詔及得宰相書令入朝，既至，皆偽也。

translations.literal: Quanzhong took Huazhou and issued an explanatory order of his own, saying, "I received an edict and also received the chief minister's letter ordering me to enter court; once I arrived, both proved forged.
translations.idiomatic: Quanzhong took Huazhou and issued an explanatory order of his own, saying, "I received an edict and also received the chief minister's letter ordering me to enter court. Once I arrived, both proved forged.

sentences.zh: 逆臣全誨震驚天子，脅乘輿出遷，暴露草莽，吾當入對言狀。」

translations.literal: The rebel minister Quanhui terrified the Son of Heaven, coerced the imperial carriage into exile abroad, and exposed him in the wild grasslands. I shall enter and speak face to face to report the facts.
translations.idiomatic: The rebel minister Quanhui terrified the Son of Heaven, coerced the imperial carriage into exile abroad, and exposed him in the wild grasslands. I shall enter and speak face to face to report the facts.

sentences.zh: 時公卿皆在長安，數日不聞朝廷敕畫。

translations.literal: At that time the nobles and chief ministers were all in Chang'an; for several days they heard no edicts or orders from the court.
translations.idiomatic: At that time the nobles and chief ministers were all in Chang'an. For several days they heard no edicts or orders from the court.

sentences.zh: 胤使王溥見全忠曰：「上猶在盩厔，公宜亟進。」

translations.literal: Yin sent Wang Fu to see Quanzhong and say, "The sovereign is still at Zhouzhi; you should advance at once.
translations.idiomatic: Yin sent Wang Fu to see Quanzhong and say, "The sovereign is still at Zhouzhi. You should advance at once.

sentences.zh: 群臣盧知猷等奏記全忠，請西迎天子，答曰：「進則似脅君，退則負國，然敢不勉？」

translations.literal: The assembled ministers Lu Zhiyou and others submitted a letter to Quanzhong requesting that he go west to welcome the Son of Heaven. He replied, "To advance seems like coercing the sovereign; to withdraw means failing the realm — yet how dare I not do my utmost?"
translations.idiomatic: The assembled ministers Lu Zhiyou and others submitted a letter to Quanzhong requesting that he go west to welcome the Son of Heaven. He replied, "To advance seems like coercing the sovereign; to withdraw means failing the realm — yet how dare I not do my utmost?"

sentences.zh: 胤率百官迎全忠灞橋，入舍長安一昔而西。

translations.literal: Yin led the hundred officials to welcome Quanzhong at Ba Bridge. He lodged one night in Chang'an and then went west.
translations.idiomatic: Yin led the hundred officials to welcome Quanzhong at Ba Bridge. He lodged one night in Chang'an and then went west.

sentences.zh: 茂貞聞全忠至，以帝入鳳翔，從臣才三四人。

translations.literal: When Maozhen learned that Quanzhong had arrived, he brought the emperor into Fengxiang; attending ministers numbered only three or four.
translations.idiomatic: When Maozhen learned that Quanzhong had arrived, he brought the emperor into Fengxiang. Attending ministers numbered only three or four.

sentences.zh: 全忠遣楊達、裴鑄入鳳翔，奉表天子。

translations.literal: Quanzhong dispatched Yang Da and Pei Zhu into Fengxiang to present a memorial to the Son of Heaven.
translations.idiomatic: Quanzhong dispatched Yang Da and Pei Zhu into Fengxiang to present a memorial to the Son of Heaven.

sentences.zh: 汴部將康懷英襲破李繼昭於武功，禽馘六千級。

translations.literal: The Bian commander Kang Huaiying launched a surprise attack and defeated Li Jizhao at Wugong, capturing and beheading six thousand men.
translations.idiomatic: The Bian commander Kang Huaiying launched a surprise attack and defeated Li Jizhao at Wugong, capturing and beheading six thousand men.

sentences.zh: 全誨懼，請救於李克用。

translations.literal: Quanhui was afraid and requested aid from Li Keyong.
translations.idiomatic: Quanhui was afraid and requested aid from Li Keyong.

sentences.zh: 克用遺全忠書，勸執崔胤，洗海內謗，全忠不答，進屯鳳翔東偏。

translations.literal: Keyong sent Quanzhong a letter urging him to arrest Cui Yin and clear away slander throughout the realm. Quanzhong did not reply and advanced to encamp on the eastern flank of Fengxiang.
translations.idiomatic: Keyong sent Quanzhong a letter urging him to arrest Cui Yin and clear away slander throughout the realm. Quanzhong did not reply and advanced to encamp on the eastern flank of Fengxiang.

sentences.zh: 茂貞登城隃語曰：「天子厭災於此，讒人誤公來，公當入覲。」

translations.literal: Maozhen climbed the wall and called across, saying, "The Son of Heaven has come here to escape calamity. Slanderers misled you into coming. You should enter and have an audience.
translations.idiomatic: Maozhen climbed the wall and called across, saying, "The Son of Heaven has come here to escape calamity. Slanderers misled you into coming. You should enter and have an audience.

sentences.zh: 全忠曰：「宦官脅驚乘輿，吾以兵問罪，迎上東還。

translations.literal: Quanzhong said, "The eunuchs coerced and terrified the imperial carriage. I come with troops to demand accountability and to welcome the sovereign back east.
translations.idiomatic: Quanzhong said, "The eunuchs coerced and terrified the imperial carriage. I come with troops to demand accountability and to welcome the sovereign back east.

sentences.zh: 王非同謀者，尚何所言？」

translations.literal: Wang is no accomplice — what more is there to say?"
translations.idiomatic: Wang is no accomplice — what more is there to say?"

sentences.zh: 明日，圍鳳翔，茂貞不出。

translations.literal: The next day he besieged Fengxiang; Maozhen did not come out.
translations.idiomatic: The next day he besieged Fengxiang. Maozhen did not come out.

sentences.zh: 帝遣中人詔全忠班師，不奉詔。

translations.literal: The emperor sent a palace envoy to order Quanzhong to withdraw his armies; he did not obey the edict.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor sent a palace envoy to order Quanzhong to withdraw his armies. He did not obey the edict.

sentences.zh: 使者再往，全忠聽命，引兵攻邠州，李繼徽嬰城三日乃降。

translations.literal: When the envoy went again, Quanzhong obeyed the order, led his troops to attack Binzhou, and after Li Jihui held the city for three days he surrendered.
translations.idiomatic: When the envoy went again, Quanzhong obeyed the order and led his troops to attack Binzhou. Li Jihui held the city for three days and then surrendered.

sentences.zh: 質其妻，復使繼徽守，回壁三原。

translations.literal: Quanzhong kept Jihui's wife as a hostage, restored Jihui to the defense, and withdrew his encampment to Sanyuan.
translations.idiomatic: Quanzhong kept Jihui's wife as a hostage, restored Jihui to the defense, and withdrew his encampment to Sanyuan.

sentences.zh: 胤與鄭元規至三原，邀說全忠。

translations.literal: Yin and Zheng Yuangui went to Sanyuan to intercept Quanzhong and persuade him.
translations.idiomatic: Yin and Zheng Yuangui went to Sanyuan to intercept Quanzhong and persuade him.

sentences.zh: 全忠亦自聞茂貞將戰，徙營渭北，據高原，戰不勝。

translations.literal: Quanzhong himself also heard that Maozhen was about to give battle. He moved his camp north of the Wei River and took the high ground, but was defeated in battle.
translations.idiomatic: Quanzhong himself also heard that Maozhen was about to give battle. He moved his camp north of the Wei River and took the high ground, but was defeated in battle.

sentences.zh: 全忠夜入盩厔，拔藍田，復屯三原。

translations.literal: Quanzhong entered Zhouzhi by night, took Lantian, and again encamped at Sanyuan.
translations.idiomatic: Quanzhong entered Zhouzhi by night, took Lantian, and again encamped at Sanyuan.

sentences.zh: 時李克用攻慈、隰，救鳳翔，全忠還河中。

translations.literal: At that time Li Keyong was attacking Ci and Xi to rescue Fengxiang. Quanzhong returned to Hezhong.
translations.idiomatic: At that time Li Keyong was attacking Ci and Xi to rescue Fengxiang. Quanzhong returned to Hezhong.

sentences.zh: 克用部將李嗣昭戰數不利，全忠取晉、汾二州，嗣昭遁還河東。

translations.literal: Keyong's commander Li Sizhao suffered repeated defeats in battle. Quanzhong took Jin and Fen prefectures, and Sizhao fled back to Hedong.
translations.idiomatic: Keyong's commander Li Sizhao suffered repeated defeats in battle. Quanzhong took Jin and Fen prefectures, and Sizhao fled back to Hedong.

sentences.zh: 全忠曰：「此茂貞所倚，今敗矣，何能久乎？」

translations.literal: Quanzhong said, "This is what Maozhen relied upon; now he is defeated — how long can he hold out?
translations.idiomatic: Quanzhong said, "This is what Maozhen relied upon. Now he is defeated — how long can he hold out?

sentences.zh: 胤復說全忠曰：「宦豎謀擁帝入蜀。」

translations.literal: Yin again urged Quanzhong, saying, "The eunuchs are plotting to take the sovereign into Shu."
translations.idiomatic: Yin again urged Quanzhong, saying, "The eunuchs are plotting to take the sovereign into Shu."

sentences.zh: 且泣。

translations.literal: And he wept as he spoke.
translations.idiomatic: And he wept as he spoke.

sentences.zh: 全忠執其手，乃定計迎天子。

translations.literal: Quanzhong took his hand and thereupon settled on a plan to welcome the Son of Heaven.
translations.idiomatic: Quanzhong took his hand and thereupon settled on a plan to welcome the Son of Heaven.

sentences.zh: 會朱友寧敗岐兵於莫父，居人皆入保。

translations.literal: At that time Zhu Youning defeated the Qi army at Mofu; the inhabitants all withdrew into fortified settlements.
translations.idiomatic: At that time Zhu Youning defeated the Qi army at Mofu. The inhabitants all withdrew into fortified settlements.

sentences.zh: 全忠以精甲五萬與茂貞決戰，岐兵敗，仆屍萬餘，茂貞帳下八百人就縛，乃嬰城，自夏訖冬，兵連不能解，勝敗略相償。

translations.literal: Quanzhong brought fifty thousand picked armored troops to fight a decisive battle with Maozhen. The Qi army was defeated; more than ten thousand corpses were strewn about. Eight hundred men under Maozhen's own command were bound on the spot. He then held the city fast. From summer until winter the fighting continued without relief; victory and defeat were roughly equal.
translations.idiomatic: Quanzhong brought fifty thousand picked armored troops to fight a decisive battle with Maozhen. The Qi army was defeated, and more than ten thousand corpses were strewn about. Eight hundred men under Maozhen's own command were bound on the spot. He then held the city fast. From summer until winter the fighting continued without relief, and victory and defeat were roughly equal.

sentences.zh: 援軍十餘壁，數為全忠擾襲，不得進，城中日困。

translations.literal: More than a dozen relief encampments were repeatedly harried and raided by Quanzhong and could not advance; inside the city conditions grew daily more desperate.
translations.idiomatic: More than a dozen relief encampments were repeatedly harried and raided by Quanzhong and could not advance. Inside the city, conditions grew daily more desperate.

sentences.zh: 全忠由是取鳳、鄜、坊、成、隴等州，間劫鈔以佐軍餉，故能不乏。

translations.literal: Quanzhong thereby took Feng, Fu, Fang, Cheng, Long, and other prefectures, and intermittently raided for plunder to supplement army provisions, and so his supplies did not run short.
translations.idiomatic: Quanzhong thereby took Feng, Fu, Fang, Cheng, Long, and other prefectures and intermittently raided for plunder to supplement army provisions, and so his supplies did not run short.

sentences.zh: 茂貞疑帝與全忠有密約，增甲士守宮殿。

translations.literal: Maozhen suspected that the emperor had a secret pact with Quanzhong and increased armored guards around the palace halls.
translations.idiomatic: Maozhen suspected that the emperor had a secret pact with Quanzhong and increased armored guards around the palace halls.

sentences.zh: 初，帝至鳳翔，有鴉數萬棲殿樹，謂之神鴉。

translations.literal: At first, when the emperor reached Fengxiang, tens of thousands of crows roosted in the palace trees; they were called the Spirit Crows.
translations.idiomatic: At first, when the emperor reached Fengxiang, tens of thousands of crows roosted in the palace trees. They were called the Spirit Crows.

sentences.zh: 俄而鴉不來，人以為恐。

translations.literal: Before long the crows came no more; people took it as an omen of dread.
translations.idiomatic: Before long the crows came no more, and people took it as an omen of dread.

sentences.zh: 全誨等小人既勢窘，更相怨疾，不復遠慮。

translations.literal: Quanhui and the other petty men, their power now straitened, turned on one another in mutual resentment and no longer looked far ahead.
translations.idiomatic: Quanhui and the other petty men, their power now straitened, turned on one another in mutual resentment and no longer looked far ahead.

sentences.zh: 時財用窶短，帝輟所御膳賜全誨等，三讓，帝曰：「難得時欲同味耳。」

translations.literal: At that time funds were exhausted and supplies scarce. The emperor set aside his own imperial meal and bestowed it on Quanhui and the others. They thrice declined. The emperor said, "Hard times — we only wish to share the same fare.
translations.idiomatic: At that time funds were exhausted and supplies scarce. The emperor set aside his own imperial meal and bestowed it on Quanhui and the others. They thrice declined. The emperor said, "These are hard times — we only wish to share the same fare.

sentences.zh: 茂貞食鲊美，帝曰：「此後池魚。」

translations.literal: Maozhen found the pickled fish delicious. The emperor said, "Those are fish from the rear pond."
translations.idiomatic: Maozhen found the pickled fish delicious. The emperor said, "Those are fish from the rear pond."

sentences.zh: 茂貞曰：「臣養魚以候天子。」

translations.literal: Maozhen said, "Your servant raised these fish awaiting the Son of Heaven."
translations.idiomatic: Maozhen said, "Your servant raised these fish awaiting the Son of Heaven."

sentences.zh: 聞者皆駭。

translations.literal: All who heard it were appalled.
translations.idiomatic: All who heard it were appalled.

sentences.zh: 於是全忠軍攻東城，焚橋鏖戰，部將李繼寵出降，茂貞懼，密圖誅中官以紓難。

translations.literal: Thereupon Quanzhong's army attacked the eastern wall, burned the bridges, and fought fiercely. His commander Li Jichong surrendered. Maozhen was afraid and secretly plotted to execute the palace eunuchs to ease the crisis.
translations.idiomatic: Thereupon Quanzhong's army attacked the eastern wall, burned the bridges, and fought fiercely. His commander Li Jichong surrendered. Maozhen was afraid and secretly plotted to execute the palace eunuchs to ease the crisis.

sentences.zh: 先遺書曰：「禍亂之生，全誨首之。

translations.literal: He first sent a letter saying, "The birth of calamity and rebellion — Quanhui led it.
translations.idiomatic: He first sent a letter saying, "The birth of calamity and rebellion — Quanhui led it.

sentences.zh: 變興倉卒，故迎天子至此。

translations.literal: The uprising arose in haste, and so I welcomed the Son of Heaven here.
translations.idiomatic: The uprising arose in haste, and so I welcomed the Son of Heaven here.

sentences.zh: 且公未至，懼它盜馮陵。

translations.literal: Moreover, before you arrived I feared other robbers would encroach.
translations.idiomatic: Moreover, before you arrived I feared other robbers would encroach.

sentences.zh: 公既志輔社稷，請奉乘輿還宮，仆願以敝賦從。」

translations.literal: Since you are minded to assist the altars of state, please receive the imperial carriage back to the palace. Your humble servant is willing to follow with what little strength remains to him.
translations.idiomatic: Since you are minded to assist the altars of state, please receive the imperial carriage back to the palace. Your humble servant is willing to follow with what little strength remains to him.

sentences.zh: 全忠然許，然軍稍薄城，大謼者三，岐軍皆投塹，無鬥意。

translations.literal: Quanzhong agreed in principle, yet his army gradually pressed close to the city. Three great battle cries went up; the Qi troops all leapt into the moat and had no will to fight.
translations.idiomatic: Quanzhong agreed in principle, yet his army gradually pressed close to the city. Three great battle cries went up. The Qi troops all leapt into the moat and had no will to fight.

sentences.zh: 帝召茂貞、全誨、彥弼及宰相蘇檢、李繼岌、繼忠議，和已決，中官復沮罷。

translations.literal: The emperor summoned Maozhen, Quanhui, Yanbi, and the chief ministers Su Jian, Li Jiji, and Li Jizhong to consult. Peace had already been decided, but the eunuchs again obstructed and stopped it.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor summoned Maozhen, Quanhui, Yanbi, and the chief ministers Su Jian, Li Jiji, and Li Jizhong to consult. Peace had already been decided, but the eunuchs again obstructed and stopped it.

sentences.zh: 它日，帝召茂貞等曰：「十六宅諸王日奏餒死者十三，王、公主、夫人皆間日食，今又將竭，奈何？」

translations.literal: On another day the emperor summoned Maozhen and the others and said, "The princes of the Sixteen Residences report daily that thirteen have died of starvation. Princes, princesses, and consorts all eat only every other day. Now supplies are again nearly exhausted — what is to be done?
translations.idiomatic: On another day the emperor summoned Maozhen and the others and said, "The princes of the Sixteen Residences report daily that thirteen have died of starvation. Princes, princesses, and consorts all eat only every other day. Now supplies are again nearly exhausted — what is to be done?

sentences.zh: 皆不敢對。

translations.literal: None dared reply.
translations.idiomatic: None dared reply.

sentences.zh: 有衛士十餘人叩左銀臺門，遮全誨罵曰：「破一州，餓死者十萬，徒以軍容數人耳！」

translations.literal: More than ten guardsmen knocked at the Left Silver Terrace Gate, intercepted Quanhui, and cursed him, saying, "You wreck one prefecture — a hundred thousand starve to death — all for the sake of a few Directors of the Army!
translations.idiomatic: More than ten guardsmen knocked at the Left Silver Terrace Gate, intercepted Quanhui, and cursed him, saying, "You wreck one prefecture and a hundred thousand starve to death — all for the sake of a few Directors of the Army!

sentences.zh: 全誨詣茂貞叩頭訴，茂貞謝曰：「士伍亦何知？」

translations.literal: Quanhui went to Maozhen, kowtowed, and pleaded his case. Maozhen apologized, saying, "What do common soldiers know?"
translations.idiomatic: Quanhui went to Maozhen, kowtowed, and pleaded his case. Maozhen apologized, saying, "What do common soldiers know?"

sentences.zh: 復訴於帝，帝不許。

translations.literal: He again appealed to the emperor; the emperor would not consent.
translations.idiomatic: He again appealed to the emperor, but the emperor would not consent.

sentences.zh: 李繼昭見全誨曰：「昔楊軍容破楊守亮一族，今驃騎復破吾族乎？」

translations.literal: Li Jizhao saw Quanhui and said, "In former days Director Yang destroyed Yang Shouliang's entire clan — will the Flying Cavalry General now destroy our clan as well?
translations.idiomatic: Li Jizhao saw Quanhui and said, "In former days Director Yang destroyed Yang Shouliang's entire clan. Will the Flying Cavalry General now destroy our clan as well?

sentences.zh: 罵之，乃出降。

translations.literal: He cursed him and thereupon went out to surrender.
translations.idiomatic: He cursed him and thereupon went out to surrender.

sentences.zh: 宦豎數傳援軍至，皆相賀，百姓笑曰：「紿我乎！」

translations.literal: The eunuchs repeatedly announced that relief troops had arrived; all congratulated one another. The common people laughed and said, "Are you fooling us?"
translations.idiomatic: The eunuchs repeatedly announced that relief troops had arrived, and all congratulated one another. The common people laughed and said, "Are you fooling us?"

sentences.zh: 是時，全忠合四鎮兵十餘萬，營壘相屬，晝夜攻。

translations.literal: At this time Quanzhong assembled troops from four prefectures, more than a hundred thousand in all; camps stretched in unbroken succession and attacked day and night.
translations.idiomatic: At this time Quanzhong assembled troops from four prefectures, more than a hundred thousand in all. Camps stretched in unbroken succession, and they attacked day and night.

sentences.zh: 外兵詬守者曰：「劫天子賊」，守者亦詬外曰「奪天子賊」。

translations.literal: The outer troops insulted the defenders as "bandits who seized the Son of Heaven"; the defenders likewise insulted those outside as "bandits who would wrest away the Son of Heaven."
translations.idiomatic: The outer troops insulted the defenders as "bandits who seized the Son of Heaven." The defenders likewise insulted those outside as "bandits who would wrest away the Son of Heaven."

sentences.zh: 諸鎮見崔胤檄，皆狐疑不出師，唯青州節度使王師範取兗州，襲華州，李克用攻晉州以為援。

translations.literal: When the various prefectures saw Cui Yin's proclamation, all hesitated in doubt and did not march forth; only Qingzhou military commissioner Wang Shifan took Yanzhou and raided Huazhou, while Li Keyong attacked Jinzhou as relief.
translations.idiomatic: When the various prefectures saw Cui Yin's proclamation, all hesitated in doubt and did not march forth. Only Qingzhou military commissioner Wang Shifan took Yanzhou and raided Huazhou, while Li Keyong attacked Jinzhou as relief.

sentences.zh: 全忠懼，圍益急。

translations.literal: Quanzhong was afraid and pressed the siege all the more fiercely.
translations.idiomatic: Quanzhong was afraid and pressed the siege all the more fiercely.

sentences.zh: 全誨等素譎險，常為全忠、胤所憚，乃請先殺之，以迎天子。

translations.literal: Quanhui and the others had always been cunning and ruthless; Quanzhong and Yin feared them alike. Maozhen therefore requested that they be killed first in order to welcome the Son of Heaven.
translations.idiomatic: Quanhui and the others had always been cunning and ruthless, and Quanzhong and Yin feared them alike. Maozhen therefore requested that they be killed first in order to welcome the Son of Heaven.

sentences.zh: 帝既惡宦人脅遷，而茂貞又其黨，全忠雖外示順，終悖逆，皆不可倚。

translations.literal: The emperor already detested the eunuchs for coercing his removal; Maozhen was their partisan; Quanzhong, though outwardly submissive, was in the end rebellious — none could be relied upon.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor already detested the eunuchs for coercing his removal. Maozhen was their partisan, and Quanzhong, though outwardly submissive, was in the end rebellious — none could be relied upon.

sentences.zh: 欲狩襄、漢，依趙匡凝，然不得去，乃定計歸全忠，以紓近禍。

translations.literal: He wished to hunt in Xiang and Han and rely on Zhao Kuangning, yet could not get away. He then settled on a plan to go over to Quanzhong to relieve the immediate calamity.
translations.idiomatic: He wished to hunt in Xiang and Han and rely on Zhao Kuangning, yet could not get away. He then settled on a plan to go over to Quanzhong to relieve the immediate calamity.

sentences.zh: 三年正月，茂貞請遣使諭全忠軍，詔崔構挾中人郭遵誨往，既行，又命宮人寵顏馳見全忠，諭密旨，乃以蔣玄暉入衛。

translations.literal: In the first month of the third year, Maozhen requested sending envoys to instruct Quanzhong's army. An edict ordered Cui Gou to go accompanied by the palace eunuch Guo Zunhui. After they had set out, the emperor also ordered the palace woman Chongyan to ride posthaste to see Quanzhong and convey a secret decree. Jiang Xuanhui was then sent in as a guard.
translations.idiomatic: In the first month of the third year, Maozhen requested sending envoys to instruct Quanzhong's army. An edict ordered Cui Gou to go accompanied by the palace eunuch Guo Zunhui. After they had set out, the emperor also ordered the palace woman Chongyan to ride posthaste to see Quanzhong and convey a secret decree. Jiang Xuanhui was then sent in as a guard.

sentences.zh: 二日，茂貞獨見，至日旰，全誨、彥弘恨甚，逮食，不能捉匕，自見勢去，計無所用，垂頭喪氣。

translations.literal: On the second day Maozhen had a private audience that lasted until sunset. Quanhui and Yanhong felt intense hatred. When food was brought they could not hold a spoon. Seeing that their power had departed and their schemes availed nothing, they hung their heads in dejection.
translations.idiomatic: On the second day Maozhen had a private audience that lasted until sunset. Quanhui and Yanhong felt intense hatred. When food was brought they could not hold a spoon. Seeing that their power had departed and their schemes availed nothing, they hung their heads in dejection.

sentences.zh: 帝召韓偓見東橫門，執手涕泗。

translations.literal: The emperor summoned Han Wo to meet him at the East Cross Gate, took his hand, and wept.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor summoned Han Wo to meet him at the East Cross Gate, took his hand, and wept.

sentences.zh: 帝曰：「今先去四大惡，餘以次誅矣。」

translations.literal: The emperor said, "Now first remove the Four Great Evils; the rest will be executed in order.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor said, "Now first remove the Four Great Evils. The rest will be executed in order.

sentences.zh: 於是內養八輩候廷中授命，每二輩以衛士十人取一首，俄而全誨、彥弘、易簡、敬容皆死。

translations.literal: Thereupon eight Inner Caretakers waited in the court to receive orders. Each pair, with ten guardsmen, took one head. Before long Quanhui, Yanhong, Yijian, and Jingrong were all dead.
translations.idiomatic: Thereupon eight Inner Caretakers waited in the court to receive orders. Each pair, with ten guardsmen, took one head. Before long Quanhui, Yanhong, Yijian, and Jingrong were all dead.

sentences.zh: 即詔第五可範為左軍都尉，王知古、揚虔朗為樞密使，知古領上院，虔朗領下院。

translations.literal: An edict immediately appointed Diwu Kefan Director of the Left Army, and Wang Zhigu and Yang Qianlang as Palace Secretaries — Zhigu headed the Upper Bureau and Qianlang the Lower Bureau.
translations.idiomatic: An edict immediately appointed Diwu Kefan Director of the Left Army, and Wang Zhigu and Yang Qianlang as Palace Secretaries — Zhigu headed the Upper Bureau and Qianlang the Lower Bureau.

sentences.zh: 繼筠、繼誨、彥弼皆伏誅，茂貞取其輜重。

translations.literal: Jijun, Jihui, and Yanbi were all executed. Maozhen took their baggage train.
translations.idiomatic: Jijun, Jihui, and Yanbi were all executed. Maozhen took their baggage train.

sentences.zh: 是夜，誅內諸司使韋處廷等二十二人，悉以首內布囊，詔蔣玄暉、學士薛貽矩送全忠，曰：「是皆不肯使乘輿東者，既斬之矣。」

translations.literal: That same night, twenty-two Directors of the Inner Offices, including Wei Chuting, were executed. All their heads were placed in cloth sacks. An edict ordered Jiang Xuanhui and academician Xue Yiju to deliver them to Quanzhong, saying, "These all refused to let the imperial carriage go east; they have now been beheaded.
translations.idiomatic: That same night, twenty-two Directors of the Inner Offices, including Wei Chuting, were executed. All their heads were placed in cloth sacks. An edict ordered Jiang Xuanhui and academician Xue Yiju to deliver them to Quanzhong, saying, "These all refused to let the imperial carriage go east. They have now been beheaded.

sentences.zh: 全忠大喜，遍告軍中，以姚洎為岐、汴通和使。

translations.literal: Quanzhong was greatly pleased and proclaimed it throughout the army. Yao Ji was appointed envoy for peace between Qi and Bian.
translations.idiomatic: Quanzhong was greatly pleased and proclaimed it throughout the army. Yao Ji was appointed envoy for peace between Qi and Bian.

sentences.zh: 全忠詒茂貞書曰：「宦者乘陴詈不已，曰『稟王旨』，是乎？」

translations.literal: Quanzhong sent Maozhen a deceptive letter, saying, "The eunuchs mount the ramparts and curse without cease, saying 'By the Prince's order' — is this so?
translations.idiomatic: Quanzhong sent Maozhen a deceptive letter, saying, "The eunuchs mount the ramparts and curse without cease, saying 'By the Prince's order' — is this so?

sentences.zh: 茂貞懼，復誅小使李繼彜等十人，於是開壘門。

translations.literal: Maozhen was afraid and again executed ten junior envoys including Li Jiyi. Thereupon the camp gates were opened.
translations.idiomatic: Maozhen was afraid and again executed ten junior envoys including Li Jiyi. Thereupon the camp gates were opened.

sentences.zh: 全忠猶攻北壘，帝遣寵顏賜御巾箱寶器，使罷兵，又捕殺中官七十人，全忠亦使京兆誅黨與百餘人。

translations.literal: Quanzhong still attacked the northern encampment. The emperor sent Chongyan to bestow imperial towel-caskets and precious vessels and order a halt to fighting. Seventy palace eunuchs were also seized and killed. Quanzhong likewise had the metropolitan prefect execute more than a hundred of their associates.
translations.idiomatic: Quanzhong still attacked the northern encampment. The emperor sent Chongyan to bestow imperial towel-caskets and precious vessels and order a halt to fighting. Seventy palace eunuchs were also seized and killed. Quanzhong likewise had the metropolitan prefect execute more than a hundred of their associates.

sentences.zh: 天子入全忠軍，全忠泥首素服，待罪客省，傳呼徹三仗，有詔釋全忠罪，使朝服見。

translations.literal: The Son of Heaven entered Quanzhong's army. Quanzhong, forehead smeared with mud and dressed in plain white, awaited judgment in the visitors' office. Three rounds of clearance were called; an edict released Quanzhong from guilt and permitted him to appear in court dress.
translations.idiomatic: The Son of Heaven entered Quanzhong's army. Quanzhong, forehead smeared with mud and dressed in plain white, awaited judgment in the visitors' office. Three rounds of clearance were called. An edict released Quanzhong from guilt and permitted him to appear in court dress.

sentences.zh: 全忠伏地泣曰：「老臣位將相，勤王無狀，使陛下及此，臣之罪也。」

translations.literal: Quanzhong prostrated himself and wept, saying, "This old minister holds rank as general and chief minister. My rescue of the throne was inept and brought Your Majesty to this pass — that is my crime.
translations.idiomatic: Quanzhong prostrated himself and wept, saying, "This old minister holds rank as general and chief minister. My rescue of the throne was inept and brought Your Majesty to this pass — that is my crime.

sentences.zh: 帝亦嗚咽，命韓偓起之，解玉帶以賜，召之食。

translations.literal: The emperor also sobbed. He ordered Han Wo to raise him up, undid his jade belt and bestowed it on him, and summoned him to eat.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor also sobbed. He ordered Han Wo to raise him up, undid his jade belt and bestowed it on him, and summoned him to eat.

sentences.zh: 帝顧衛兵，或有憤發者，因履系解，目全忠：「為吾系之。」

translations.literal: The emperor glanced at the guard soldiers; some looked ready to erupt in fury. His shoe thong came undone. He fixed his gaze on Quanzhong: "Tie it for me.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor glanced at the guard soldiers; some looked ready to erupt in fury. His shoe thong came undone. He fixed his gaze on Quanzhong and said, "Tie it for me.

sentences.zh: 全忠跪結履，汗浹於背，而左右莫敢動。

translations.literal: Quanzhong knelt and tied the shoe. Sweat soaked through to his back, yet those on either side did not dare move.
translations.idiomatic: Quanzhong knelt and tied the shoe. Sweat soaked through to his back, yet those on either side did not dare move.

sentences.zh: 是夜，帝三召，皆辭，朱友倫以兵衛帝。

translations.literal: That night the emperor summoned him three times; each time he declined. Zhu Youlun guarded the emperor with troops.
translations.idiomatic: That night the emperor summoned him three times, and each time he declined. Zhu Youlun guarded the emperor with troops.

sentences.zh: 李克用引軍去，帝還京師。

translations.literal: Li Keyong withdrew his army; the emperor returned to the capital.
translations.idiomatic: Li Keyong withdrew his army, and the emperor returned to the capital.

sentences.zh: 胤、全忠議，盡誅第五可範等八百餘人於內侍省，哀號之聲聞於路，留單弱數十人，備宮中灑掃。

translations.literal: Yin and Quanzhong agreed to execute more than eight hundred men, including Diwu Kefan, entirely within the Palace Domestic Service. Their cries of grief were heard in the streets. A few dozen feeble ones were left for palace sweeping and cleaning.
translations.idiomatic: Yin and Quanzhong agreed to execute more than eight hundred men, including Diwu Kefan, entirely within the Palace Domestic Service. Their cries of grief were heard in the streets. A few dozen feeble ones were left for palace sweeping and cleaning.

sentences.zh: 胤以鎮人性謹厚，即詔王镕擇五十人為敕使，內諸司宦官主領者皆罷。

translations.literal: Yin held that men from the provinces were cautious and steady. An edict at once ordered Wang Rong to select fifty men as Imperial Dispatch Envoys. All eunuch supervisors of the inner offices were dismissed.
translations.idiomatic: Yin held that men from the provinces were cautious and steady. An edict at once ordered Wang Rong to select fifty men as Imperial Dispatch Envoys, and all eunuch supervisors of the inner offices were dismissed.

sentences.zh: 於是追諸道監軍，所在賜死，其財產籍入之。

translations.literal: Thereupon envoys were sent to recall the Military Supervisors from each circuit; wherever found, they were granted death. Their property was registered and confiscated.
translations.idiomatic: Thereupon envoys were sent to recall the Military Supervisors from each circuit. Wherever found, they were granted death, and their property was registered and confiscated.

sentences.zh: 詔以中官脅遷狀及全忠迎乘輿本末告方鎮，罷監軍院，咸視國初故事，以三十人為員，衣黃衣，不得養子。

translations.literal: An edict reported to the regional prefectures the circumstances of the eunuchs' coerced removal and the full account of Quanzhong's reception of the imperial carriage. The Supervisory Corps was abolished. All were to follow the founding precedents of the dynasty: thirty as the quota, wearing yellow robes, forbidden to adopt sons.
translations.idiomatic: An edict reported to the regional prefectures the circumstances of the eunuchs' coerced removal and the full account of Quanzhong's reception of the imperial carriage. The Supervisory Corps was abolished. All were to follow the founding precedents of the dynasty: a quota of thirty, wearing yellow robes, and forbidden to adopt sons.

sentences.zh: 內諸司皆歸省若寺，兩軍內外八鎮兵悉屬六軍。

translations.literal: The inner offices all reverted to ministries or directorates. Troops of the Two Armies, inner and outer, and the Eight Garrisons all came under the Six Armies.
translations.idiomatic: The inner offices all reverted to ministries or directorates. Troops of the Two Armies, inner and outer, and the Eight Garrisons all came under the Six Armies.

sentences.zh: 全忠還汴州，帝以第五可範等無辜，頗悼之，為文以祭。

translations.literal: Quanzhong returned to Bianzhou. The emperor, considering Diwu Kefan and the others innocent, mourned them deeply and composed a text to offer sacrifice.
translations.idiomatic: Quanzhong returned to Bianzhou. The emperor, considering Diwu Kefan and the others innocent, mourned them deeply and composed a text to offer sacrifice.

sentences.zh: 自是宣傳詔命，皆以宮人。

translations.literal: From this time forward, proclamations and edicts were all conveyed by palace women.
translations.idiomatic: From this time forward, proclamations and edicts were all conveyed by palace women.

sentences.zh: 始，劉季述專廢立，中人皆與聞。

translations.literal: At the beginning, when Liu Jishu monopolized deposition and enthronement, all the palace eunuchs were privy to it.
translations.idiomatic: At the beginning, when Liu Jishu monopolized deposition and enthronement, all the palace eunuchs were privy to it.

sentences.zh: 帝反正，誅季述及薛齊偓數族而已，餘貸不問；

translations.literal: When the Emperor was restored to the throne, he executed only the clans of Jishu and Xue Qipu and the rest were pardoned without inquiry;
translations.idiomatic: When the emperor was restored to the throne, he executed only the clans of Jishu and Xue Qipu; the rest were pardoned without inquiry;

sentences.zh: 又悔之，後稍稍誅夷，群宦浸不安。

translations.literal: he later regretted this and gradually executed more; the eunuchs as a group grew increasingly uneasy.
translations.idiomatic: he later regretted this and gradually executed more; the eunuchs as a group grew increasingly uneasy.

sentences.zh: 時帝懲幽辱，能勵心庶政，數召見群臣問治道，有志中興，而全誨、胤爭權，外召強臣，劫本朝以相吞嚙，卒用關東軍窮討暴誅，君側雖清，而全忠勢遂張，帝卒弒死，唐室以亡，其禍本於全誨、彥弘云。

translations.literal: At that time the Emperor, chastened by his humiliating confinement, was able to apply himself to ordinary government, often summoning ministers to ask about the way of rule, with intent to restore the dynasty; yet Quanhui and Yin contended for power, summoned strong regional commanders from without, and seized the court to devour one another; in the end they employed the armies east of the Pass in exhaustive pursuit and violent executions — though those beside the throne were cleared, Quanzhong's power then expanded; the Emperor was ultimately assassinated and the house of Tang perished; the root of the calamity lay with Quanhui and Yanhong, it is said.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor, chastened by his humiliating confinement, applied himself to government and often summoned ministers to ask about the way of rule, intent on restoring the dynasty; yet Quanhui and Yin contended for power, summoned strong regional commanders from without, and seized the court to devour one another. In the end they employed the armies east of the Pass in exhaustive pursuit and violent executions — though those beside the throne were cleared, Quanzhong's power then expanded; the emperor was assassinated and the house of Tang perished. The root of the calamity, it is said, lay with Quanhui and Yanhong.

sentences.zh: 贊贊曰：袁紹誅常侍以逞，而曹操移漢；

translations.literal: The commentator says: Yuan Shao killed the Regular Attendants to gratify himself, and Cao Cao displaced Han;
translations.idiomatic: The commentator says: Yuan Shao killed the Regular Attendants to gratify himself, and Cao Cao displaced Han;

sentences.zh: 崔丞相血軍容甘心焉，而朱溫篡唐。

translations.literal: Chief Minister Cui was content to bathe the Army Commissioner in blood, and Zhu Wen usurped Tang.
translations.idiomatic: Chief Minister Cui was content to bathe the army commissioner in blood, and Zhu Wen usurped Tang.

sentences.zh: 大抵假威柄於外，以內攘奸人，則大臣專，王室卑矣。

translations.literal: In general, when one borrows authority from without to purge villains within, the great ministers grow monopolistic and the royal house is humbled.
translations.idiomatic: In general, when one borrows authority from without to purge villains within, great ministers grow monopolistic and the royal house is humbled.

sentences.zh: 漢、唐相去五百歲，產亂取亡猶蹈一轍，非天所廢，而人謀洄刺乃然邪！

translations.literal: Han and Tang were five hundred years apart, yet the birth of disorder and the path to ruin still followed the same track — was it not Heaven's abandonment, but human schemes circling and stabbing that made it so!
translations.idiomatic: Han and Tang were five hundred years apart, yet disorder and ruin still followed the same track — was it not Heaven's abandonment, but human schemes circling and stabbing that made it so!
